Keep both prism vertex legs, the intersection support projector, and every fixed-\(t_0\) source term, including trace-free central inputs.
Native and independently projected edges are compared only at the same prescribed order and contraction.

claims.title: The supported partner has every finite fresh-jet row
claims.statement: The canonical supported-partner projection is an actual current map in all four exterior rows and every finite incoming fresh-normal degree on its declared supported carrier. It retains every finite old-root, graph-slot and primitive-slot jet, the full coefficient boundary and the specified central, root and frame squares. The earlier fresh-degree-zero matrix remains its exact restriction: its zero-jet value is nonzero and its first-root Taylor correction contains both \(1/3\) and \(-1/6\). Fresh incoming powers have their own finite matrix and are not identified with outgoing contact jets.
hypotheses: Use the actual map \(\rho_q^{-1}g_q^{\mathrm{nat}}(C\,\cdot)\), \(C=(4\pi^2)^{-1}\), on the declared finite supported-current carrier, including all coefficient differentials and q-supported descendants.

Arbitrary finite incoming \(\sigma\) degree and old-root, graph-slot and primitive-slot jets are admitted, with all four contact-exterior rows. The physical incoming variable is \(S=\sigma-\alpha\); the top row retains its zero-fresh-degree indicator.
Root, retained-central and moving-frame comparisons use the displayed determinant normalizations and the unchanged original lower cochains.

claims.title: One fully supported earlier pair is an actual single action
claims.statement: For the ordered word \(a_1\,a_2\,u_3\,v_4\,v_5\,v_6\), the fully supported earlier pair factors through the prescribed single root action on the independent \((U,t)\) coefficient domain. The \(\eta\) and \(s\) limits and \(g\) rows vanish, and the \(c_t\alpha\) point order is at most \(4+J+q\). hypotheses: The classical detector is nonzero at every numerical level in the universal vacuum module. Its \(R_3\) consequence uses the existing noncritical evaluation.
All finite projections remain valid. The scalar-vacuum test itself converges, and no arbitrary-recipient or derived-functor obstruction is asserted.

claims.title: Two fixed marked maps differ by a nonzero homotopy class
claims.statement: The marked evaluation \(E_I\) and coefficient-restriction map \(C_I\), from the same polynomial finite-frame source to the independent trace recipient, differ by a nonzero class in \(H^0\operatorname{Hom}_{A_{\rm alg}^e}\), detected by \(-\mathrm{id}\). No algebraic or continuous bimodule chain homotopy connects that fixed pair, also after reduction to \(R_2\) or \(\mathbb C\). The later endpoint-bilinear scalar passage changes the evaluation within its own bimodule homotopy class and leaves the fixed coefficient factorization unchanged. On their common finite-frame restriction the signed detector still survives; restoration of the reversed scalar field does not connect this fixed pair.
hypotheses: Each fixed numerical \(K\ne-2\), over \(R_3\), with a fixed finite Cartan cutoff \(M\). Both maps have the same ordered polynomial marked source \(N_{P,M}\); inserted and rooted states are algebraic.
The independent trace recipient has zero differential; both full current endpoint actions are retained. This obstruction applies to the specified maps and their required reductions.

claims.title: A finite input does not make the full right-dual cutoff converge
claims.statement: Over \(R_2=\mathbb C[\hbar]/(\hbar^2)\), with \(\Lambda=R_2[u,u^{-1}]\), the prescribed finite inverse-antipode formula obeys \(\Theta_M P_1=P_1+2\hbar(M-1)u^{-1}P_1\) for \(M\ge1\) on the explicit finite-input projector. Consequently its unrestricted ordinary cutoff limit does not stabilize on the full finite-input Hom space.
hypotheses: Every numerical level; the inverse-antipode product has the prescribed \(A_yA_x\) order and right evaluation uses \(U\otimes U^r\).
The projector lies outside the cyclic image. Cyclic, Ward-restricted, derived and finite-prodiagram alternatives are not excluded.

claims.title: The classical germ map has its own full carrier
claims.statement: At every numerical level, the independent classical ordered carrier has a continuous dg full-\(A_0\)-bimodule germ map with kernel \(Y^0(v,u)j(\beta)\). At fixed \(K\ne-2\), the classical reduction of the pure evaluation is homotopic to this map relative to the scalar and every first root, with both Ward laws.
hypotheses: Completed left values, one ghost cutoff and finite right support per slice are retained. The restricted Laurent version has one whole-series floor and constant \(A_0\) endpoints.
The relative Ward equation includes the source Laurent derivative for nonconstant source coefficients.

claims.title: A different classical trace square has a nonzero defect
claims.statement: On the independent free algebraic trace bimodule with \(dr=J_I(0)e-eJ_I(0)\), the relative route and the germ route differ by a nonzero class in the actual full trace-recipient Hom complex, detected by \(+\mathrm{id}\). A higher-order correction cannot repair a comparison required to reduce to this same fixed square.
hypotheses: Each fixed numerical \(K\ne-2\), over \(\mathbb C\), with algebraic inserted and rooted states. The common domain is the independent free algebraic bimodule \(S_I=A_{0,\mathrm{alg}}eA_{0,\mathrm{alg}}\oplus A_{0,\mathrm{alg}}rA_{0,\mathrm{alg}}\); the two fixed arrows and the full trace recipient are retained.
The source is independently free; no injection into a finite-expression subcomplex is assumed. This square is distinct from the \(-\mathrm{id}\) coefficient-restriction comparison.

claims.title: Finite input currying retains the actual relative chain maps
claims.statement: Finite free constant first inputs curry through every ordered slot, pointwise Hom and the outer finite-word sum. The resulting inverse finite-input diagram has literal \(\kappa\) chain maps, finite inverse-antipode linear comparison squares and a corrected unit-relative chain section. These first-order comparisons act on literal quotients modulo \(\hbar^2\).
hypotheses: Four colours and all trace modes are retained over \(R_3=\mathbb C[\hbar]/(\hbar^3)\), with exact RTT-pullback module quotients and the stated ordered topology.
Every numerical level. The finite input is constant here; the separate native dg-input theorem supplies its nonzero differential. No unrestricted loop-cutoff limit is inferred.

claims.title: Whole mixed transport retains terms lost by transporting only the correction
claims.statement: The whole marked evaluation \(\mathcal E=\mathcal P+\mathcal J+\Xi\) has explicit bare mixed transport through \(R_2\), including the positive \(\mathcal J\) contribution. Its \(R_3\) projection retains both ordered cross paths, the created inserted factor and native first-order lower terms. The two stated vacuum tests stabilize for each finite Cartan cutoff \(M\ge1\) on their specified rooted input.
hypotheses: Each fixed numerical \(K\ne-2\); algebraic inserted and rooted states; the polynomial marked carrier or its restricted Laurent extension has a common floor, ghost cutoff and finite right support per right slice and inserted input.

Existing scalar agreement is with its fixed singleton-coordinate cyclic field and typed coefficient-product maps. Whole physical marked normalization, tensorators and product comparison remain separate.

claims.title: The raw outer completion has an actual augmentation contraction
claims.statement: Completion by all homogeneous left ideals open in the original nested coefficient topology gives a degreewise native rooted algebra with associative continuous multiplication, differential and translation. It admits the specified growing-length trace series and a continuous unital dg projection onto the full smooth native algebra \(A\), with a continuous unital \(R_3\)-linear section. The later normalized raw outer theorem gives an actual continuous linear strong deformation retract onto that full smooth native algebra, so its literal augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism. The separate literal marked-source contraction retains its own coefficient-module and proper-cone scope.
hypotheses: Four colours and all trace modes are retained over \(R_3=\mathbb C[\hbar]/(\hbar^3)\), with exact RTT-pullback module quotients and the stated ordered topology.

Every fixed numerical level, including zero and critical level. The normalized raw outer contraction is continuous and linear; its section and homotopy are not asserted endpoint-linear, multiplicative or translation-equivariant. No physical target comparison follows from this source result.

claims.title: Sampling the inserted unit gives another marked evaluation
claims.statement: At fixed \(K\ne-2\), \(\mathcal E_{\rm samp,ten}=\widehat f\,p_{\rm ins,0}+\Xi\) is a continuous dg full-\(A\)-bimodule map on the existing polynomial and restricted Laurent carriers. It preserves both Ward laws, the scalar and all tensor pure-root values. Its complete finite-word classical shuffle square has an actual bimodule homotopy that vanishes on the scalar and trace roots. On a first traceless root its prescribed value is \(g_{A(x[m])}\), which need not vanish.
hypotheses: Each fixed numerical \(K\ne-2\); algebraic inserted and rooted states; the polynomial marked carrier or its restricted Laurent extension has a common floor, ghost cutoff and finite right support per right slice and inserted input.

Sampling commutes with the finite and global Cartan frames. It removes positive inserted trace and \(q/\omega\) coefficient values; the old and sampled maps are not homotopic. The classical source consists of finite words and finite exterior lists.

claims.title: The sampled evaluation loses actual cohomology classes
claims.statement: The sampled map kills a cubic source cycle generating a split free cohomology summand and the independent classes from every finite family of distinct nonrepeating trace exterior lists. These are nonzero classes in the actual ordered source, transported by the finite and global frames. Hence this particular sampled map is not a quasi-isomorphism, and a homotopy of it cannot restore injectivity.
hypotheses: Each fixed numerical \(K\ne-2\); algebraic inserted and rooted states; the polynomial marked carrier or its restricted Laurent extension has a common floor, ghost cutoff and finite right support per right slice and inserted input.

The same source-local conclusion holds at its stated \(R_2\) and \(R_3\) scopes without assuming cohomology base change. Only a physical comparison requiring this map to detect those classes is excluded.

claims.title: Ward identities do not supply an ordinary source transpose
claims.statement: An explicit normalized homogeneous trace cochain in the original \(W_{\rightarrow}^{0,2}\) satisfies both actual Ward identities. Its compatible finite raw transposes are closed and Cartan-fixed, but have no coefficient-preserving ordinary value in the exact ordered source or its uniform-Laurent target.
hypotheses: Four colours and all trace modes are retained over \(R_3=\mathbb C[\hbar]/(\hbar^3)\), with exact RTT-pullback module quotients and the stated ordered topology.
Every numerical level, through \(R_3\) on finite coefficients. The obstruction retains the original source and target bounds; it does not rule out all alternative transpose domains.

claims.title: Actual native dg inputs have finite graded right duals
claims.statement: For every numerical \(K\) over \(R_2\), the transported windows \(U_a^F=F(U_a^0)\) are finite free dg inputs with a strict level-zero loop action, genuine graded right evaluation and coevaluation, and the finite inverse-antipode comparison. The full Hom differential and the frame square are retained.
hypotheses: The windows are exhaustive algebraic native inputs. They lie in underlying weights at most \(a+1\); translation lands in \(U_{a+1}^F\), requiring underlying weights at most \(a+2\).
Output/source consequences are linear chain maps on literal \(R_3/\hbar^2R_3\) quotient complexes. A strict transported input action does not supply a strict output or rooted action.
For a pure current state, \(Fv=v+\frac12\hbar(K+2)T_V^\circ v\); the trace-free translation changes the scalar comparison and cannot be discarded.

claims.title: The coefficient source carries the actual native state differential
claims.statement: The pointwise Hom coefficient source on the actual native state complex has the all-source Cartan frame, literal \(\kappa/\Gamma\) square, full unit-relative map and compatible enlarged-stage finite-input diagram through \(R_3\). Restriction along the prescribed \(j_\hbar:B\to M\) is dg and degreewise surjective, with kernel \(\operatorname{Hom}(M/j_\hbar B,K[1])[-1]\).
hypotheses: Four colours and all trace modes are retained over \(R_3=\mathbb C[\hbar]/(\hbar^3)\), with exact RTT-pullback module quotients and the stated ordered topology.
Every numerical level for the source maps; optional marked evaluation only at fixed \(K\ne-2\). Each algebraic input has finite word support, but its bound may vary with the input.
The graded section retains its differential defect; the restriction kernel is not asserted acyclic. Differential and translation use enlarged windows, not frozen native weight quotients.

The later prescribed \(j_\hbar\) derived comparison and its action homotopies are established over the literal \(R_2\) quotient at each fixed finite loop cutoff, with the signed projection and proper-cone squares. This does not assert a strict full-current raw action or the corresponding full \(R_3\) physical comparison.

claims.title: A fixed Verma source has finite extension support
claims.statement: For every nonzero finite-dimensional simple complex Lie algebra \(\mathfrak g\) and shifted level \(s\notin\mathbb Q\), a fixed horizontal affine Verma has nonzero actual smooth Ext to only finitely many target-weight and nonnegative-energy pairs, with a finite source-dependent degree bound. At every real \(s>0\), a uniform bound over its targets is \(\dim\mathfrak b+\lfloor\|\operatorname{Re}\lambda+\rho\|^2/(2s)\rfloor\).
hypotheses: Both homogeneous graded and actual ungraded smooth module Ext are included. The source highest weight is arbitrary complex; the degree bound need not be uniform as that source varies.
These are necessary support conditions, not assertions that every allowed Ext group is nonzero.

claims.title: The changing-Verma positive-shift telescope vanishes
claims.statement: Under the native hypotheses, every countable telescope of the perfect Verma preimages with strictly increasing total cohomological shifts is zero for \(s\in\mathbb C\setminus\mathbb Q_{\le0}\), allowing varying highest weights, arbitrary internal shifts and arbitrary successive maps.
hypotheses: The Lie algebra \(\mathfrak g\) is nonzero, finite-dimensional, simple and complex. The prescribed coherent native right action, actual smooth tensor–Hom adjunction, exact affine-free lifts and cutoff compatibility remain hypotheses. The graded and ungraded native realizations are supplied separately.

The native transfer also assumes the actual unit and full smooth/algebraic comparison on the common-lower-energy subcategories; these hypotheses are not replaced by an arbitrary unbounded Hom formula.
Both grading conventions are included, without a common energy bound. This is a theorem about this telescope class, not a global-unit argument.

claims.title: Verma-generated objects miss the regular horizontal top
claims.statement: At every level, the localizing category generated by affine Vermas is a proper subcategory of \(\operatorname{Loc}(W)\) in the ungraded convention. In the graded convention all internal shifts are included on both sides: \(\operatorname{Loc}\{M_\lambda\langle a\rangle\}\subsetneq\operatorname{Loc}\{W\langle a\rangle:a\in\mathbb Z\}\). Cartan-local finiteness persists throughout the Verma-generated category, whereas the regular \(U(\mathfrak g)\) top of \(W\) violates it.
hypotheses: The Lie algebra \(\mathfrak g\) is nonzero, finite-dimensional, simple and complex. The recipient assertion is representation-theoretic, in graded and ungraded conventions. The separate line-source consequence requires the native tensor comparison.

claims.title: Every unbounded smooth complex has an explicit injective replacement
claims.statement: An actual acyclic-monomorphism cell construction iterated through \(\omega_1\) gives a strict ordinary functor \(J\) and a natural monomorphic quasi-isomorphism \(M\to J(M)\). Every term of \(J(M)\) is injective and the whole complex is K-injective, so full \(\operatorname{Hom}_A(X,J(M))\) computes ordinary smooth derived Hom for arbitrary unbounded \(X,M\).
hypotheses: Graded and ungraded smooth categories use their actual Hom conventions. The replacement functor is ordinary, not asserted dg-enriched.
Under the separate native inputs, the fixed strict right-module model supplies the native Hom action and signed unit; applying \(J\) alone does not create that action.

claims.title: The ordinary unit fails at every integral affine level at most minus four
claims.statement: For \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) at raw affine level \(-p-2\), \(p\ge2\), a telescope of perfect Verma preimages gives \(L_p\ne0\) with \(\Phi_pL_p=0\). The actual ordinary unit is \(L_p\to0\), with nonzero cone \(L_p[1]\). An infinite-projection map entirely within the generated recipient also proves that \(W_p\) is not compact there.
hypotheses: The prescribed coherent native right action, actual smooth tensor–Hom adjunction, exact affine-free lifts and cutoff compatibility remain hypotheses. The graded and ungraded native realizations are supplied separately.

The native transfer also assumes the actual unit and full smooth/algebraic comparison on the common-lower-energy subcategories; these hypotheses are not replaced by an arbitrary unbounded Hom formula.

Ordinary unbounded derived categories with ordinary coefficient quasi-isomorphisms; internal weights are algebraic sums of arbitrary support. No cohomological, common energy or finite-dimensionality bound is imposed.

The actual normalized Ext-one classes have every finite initial Yoneda product nonzero. The conclusions hold graded and ungraded. The family does not cover shifted level \(-1\) or negative nonintegral rational levels.

claims.title: Every simple type has a noncritical unit kernel at a specified level
claims.statement: For every nonzero finite-dimensional simple complex Lie algebra \(\mathfrak g\) at raw affine level \(-2h^\vee\), an explicit affine-Weyl ascent chain gives an ordinary line telescope \(L\ne0\) with \(\Phi L=0\). Its actual unit has cone \(L[1]\ne0\). The same construction proves failure of compactness of \(W\) within its own localizing image.
hypotheses: The prescribed coherent native right action, actual smooth tensor–Hom adjunction, exact affine-free lifts and cutoff compatibility remain hypotheses. The graded and ungraded native realizations are supplied separately.

The native transfer also assumes the actual unit and full smooth/algebraic comparison on the common-lower-energy subcategories; these hypotheses are not replaced by an arbitrary unbounded Hom formula.

Ordinary unbounded derived categories with ordinary coefficient quasi-isomorphisms; internal weights are algebraic sums of arbitrary support. No cohomological, common energy or finite-dimensionality bound is imposed.
This is one specified noncritical level in every simple type, including nonsimplylaced types. It uses same-type extension products, and does not assert failure at every noncritical level.

claims.title: The regular top has disjoint positive-weight central supports
claims.statement: For affine \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\), \(s=\ell+2\ne0\), positive-weight smooth self-Ext of \(W\) has \(\Omega_L-\Omega_R=2sw\) and right annihilator \(Q_w(T)=\prod_{m=1}^w[(2sw-2m^2)^2-4m^2(2T+1)]\). At \(s\notin\mathbb Q\), all positive-weight left supports are disjoint from all positive-weight right supports; the resulting module-level Tor groups vanish.
hypotheses: The actual regular \(U(\mathfrak{sl}_2)\) top and its source-precomposition/target-postcomposition actions are used. Fixed-weight amplitude is finite; no common all-weight amplitude bound is asserted.
This representation-theoretic theorem requires no native adjunction. Passing to the actual native ideal is a separate derived theorem.

claims.title: A derived square-zero ideal reduces every source to two inflated complexes
claims.statement: Let \(B\to R\) be a split augmented dg algebra, K-flat over \(R\) on both sides, with ideal \(I\) satisfying \(I\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}I=0\). For \(F=R\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}-\), inflation \(U\), and \(J=R\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}I\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}R\), every unbounded \(L\) has a natural triangle \(U(J\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}F(L))\to L\to UF(L)\). For any exact adjunction out of \(D(B)\), its actual unit is globally invertible exactly when it is invertible on every inflated \(R\)-complex.
hypotheses: Ordinary algebraic direct sums and unbounded derived tensors are used, in either grading convention. The middle arrow is the actual extension-of-scalars unit.
Derived tensor vanishing is stronger than square-zero multiplication. No unrestricted coproduct preservation by a right adjoint is assumed.

claims.title: The actual nonrational rank-one ideal has zero derived tensor square
claims.statement: For \(B=Y_{-s}\), \(\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{sl}_2\) and \(s\notin\mathbb Q\), the actual positive-weight ideal \(I=\bigoplus_{w>0}B_w\) satisfies \(I\otimes_{U(\mathfrak{sl}_2)}^{\mathbf L}I\simeq0\), retaining both outer actions in the graded and ungraded bimodule categories.
hypotheses: The prescribed coherent native right action, actual smooth tensor–Hom adjunction, exact affine-free lifts and cutoff compatibility remain hypotheses. The graded and ungraded native realizations are supplied separately.
The exact supported graded unit on the free object \(B\) and the prescribed strict smooth right-module model are retained inputs.
The supported generator unit identifies the correctly oriented native bimodule structure. Finite-weight derived annihilator powers and algebraic coproducts establish the full ideal assertion.

claims.title: Restricted positive-current cofree modules are genuinely injective
claims.statement: For \(\mathfrak n=t\mathfrak{sl}_2[t]\) over \(\mathbb C\) or \(\mathbb C((q))\), its restricted finite-energy cofree module \(C\) has \(C\otimes T\) injective in the actual smooth positive-current category for every coefficient vector space \(T\). The assertion also holds in the algebraically graded category with arbitrary coefficient-weight support.
hypotheses: The current action is on \(C\) alone and every element has finite cofree support. This is not affine injectivity, a restricted affine-coinduction adjunction, or by itself an arbitrary-complex K-injectivity assertion.

claims.title: The actual unit is invertible on every inflated base complex
claims.statement: For \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\), native \(k\notin\mathbb Q\) and raw affine level \(\ell=-k-2\), the actual native unit is an equivalence on every ordinary unbounded complex inflated from the full ghost quotient \(H=U(\mathfrak g[t^{-1}])\), hence from \(R=U(\mathfrak g)\). The signed unit evaluates at the vacuum to the identity under the genuine unbounded Shapiro comparison.
hypotheses: The prescribed coherent native right action, actual smooth tensor–Hom adjunction, exact affine-free lifts and cutoff compatibility remain hypotheses. The graded and ungraded native realizations are supplied separately.

Ordinary unbounded derived categories with ordinary coefficient quasi-isomorphisms; internal weights are algebraic sums of arbitrary support. No cohomological, common energy or finite-dimensionality bound is imposed.

The cofree factor remains an algebraic sum. The proof uses the fixed coherent smooth right-module model and positive-current injectivity, without extending a bounded cochain formula to arbitrary inputs.

claims.title: Nonrational rank-one induction is fully faithful on the entire ordinary source
claims.statement: For \(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\), native \(k\in\mathbb C\setminus\mathbb Q\) and raw affine level \(\ell=-k-2\), the actual unit \(L\to\Psi\Phi L\) is an equivalence for every ordinary unbounded \(Y_k\)-module, including nonzero ghost actions. The actual realization is fully faithful with image exactly \(\operatorname{Loc}(W)\), or \(\operatorname{Loc}\{W\langle w\rangle:w\in\mathbb Z\}\) in the graded convention.
hypotheses: The prescribed coherent native right action, actual smooth tensor–Hom adjunction, exact affine-free lifts and cutoff compatibility remain hypotheses. The graded and ungraded native realizations are supplied separately.
The exact supported graded unit on the free object \(B\) and the prescribed strict smooth right-module model are retained inputs.

Ordinary unbounded derived categories with ordinary coefficient quasi-isomorphisms; internal weights are algebraic sums of arbitrary support. No cohomological, common energy or finite-dimensionality bound is imposed.

The derived native ideal theorem, the full-domain reduction and the actual all-inflated unit are combined with their exact maps. The image is not asserted to be every smooth object or every object with torsion cohomology.

claims.title: The actual counit is the cellular approximation at nonrational rank one
claims.statement: Under the same nonrational \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) native hypotheses, \(W\) and its required internal shifts are compact within the generated image. For every unrestricted smooth target \(M\), the actual counit \(\Phi\Psi M\to M\) is canonically the cellular-coreflector map \(\operatorname{Cell}_W M\to M\); it is invertible exactly on that image.
hypotheses: The prescribed coherent native right action, actual smooth tensor–Hom adjunction, exact affine-free lifts and cutoff compatibility remain hypotheses. The graded and ungraded native realizations are supplied separately.
The exact supported graded unit on the free object \(B\) and the prescribed strict smooth right-module model are retained inputs.

Ordinary unbounded derived categories with ordinary coefficient quasi-isomorphisms; internal weights are algebraic sums of arbitrary support. No cohomological, common energy or finite-dimensionality bound is imposed.

Compactness is relative to the localizing image, not to the entire smooth derived category. The positive-weight ideal in the line algebra differs from the positive-current augmentation ideal used for cellularization.

claims.title: One nilpotent current has an exact unbounded torsion comparison
claims.statement: For \(x=at\) with nonzero ad-nilpotent \(a\), smooth Ore localization \(L_x\) is exact and \(i_xR\Gamma_xM\simeq\operatorname{fib}(M\to L_xM)\) on every ordinary unbounded smooth complex. The inclusion of the derived \(x\)-torsion category is fully faithful, with exactly \(x\)-torsion cohomology as image.
hypotheses: Every nonzero finite-dimensional simple complex Lie algebra and every affine level, graded and ungraded. No native adjunction hypothesis is needed.

claims.title: A finite nilpotent basis detects joint torsion
claims.statement: A nilpotent basis \(a_i\) of \(\mathfrak g\), with \(x_i=a_it\), gives \(\mathcal T_I=\bigcap_i\ker L_{x_i}\) and \(D_I=\bigcap_i\ker DL_{x_i}\). These exact detectors characterize joint torsion and its cohomological category.
hypotheses: Every nonzero finite-dimensional simple complex Lie algebra and every affine level. These equalities do not identify the intrinsic derived torsion category with its ambient cohomological category.

claims.title: The single-current localizations do not preserve each other’s torsion
claims.statement: At every affine \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) level, an explicit smooth module is \(ft\)-torsion while its localization at \(et\) is not. Thus iterating the single-current detectors is not automatically a construction of joint derived torsion.
hypotheses: The graded and ungraded examples are actual smooth affine modules. This obstruction to a chosen construction does not refute the joint comparison.

claims.title: Positive-current torsion is stable under injective envelopes
claims.statement: The smooth positive-current category is locally noetherian, and joint augmentation torsion is stable under injective envelopes. Finite nilpotent Rees algebras and the resulting Artin–Rees statement give the actual stability theorem on every smooth cyclic module.
hypotheses: Every nonzero finite-dimensional simple complex Lie algebra. Affine injective stability is not inferred merely by restriction.

claims.title: Actual derived torsion commutes with positive-current restriction
claims.statement: Exact induction on the smooth and torsion categories yields \(\operatorname{Res}_{\mathcal T}R\Gamma_A\simeq R\Gamma_{\mathfrak n}\operatorname{Res}_{\mathcal S}\) on every ordinary unbounded complex, with the actual units and counits. Restriction is conservative; every torsion affine module is \(\Gamma_A\)-acyclic, so \(\Gamma_A\) is weakly stable.
hypotheses: Every nonzero finite-dimensional simple complex Lie algebra and every affine level. The derived functors use genuine K-injective replacements; no unrestricted continuous-cochain model is substituted.

claims.title: Positive-current derived torsion has infinite cohomological dimension
claims.statement: For \(R_N=U(\mathfrak n/\mathfrak n_N)\) with its inflated regular action, the first nonzero derived torsion lies in degree \(d_N=(N-1)\dim\mathfrak g\). Its invariant line has energy \(\Delta_N=\dim(\mathfrak g)N(N-1)/2\). These degrees are unbounded.
hypotheses: This is an actual smooth positive-current calculation for every nonzero finite-dimensional simple complex Lie algebra. Infinite cohomological dimension alone does not decide the joint derived embedding.

claims.title: Positive-current derived torsion fails to preserve a countable coproduct
claims.statement: For the shifted regular quotients \(R_N[d_N]\), the actual comparison \(\bigoplus_N R\Gamma(R_N[d_N])\to R\Gamma(\bigoplus_N R_N[d_N])\) has a nonzero degree-zero defect containing \(\mathbb C^{\mathbb N}/\mathbb C^{(\mathbb N)}\). An actual acyclic complex of injectives \(K\) realizes the defect: \(R\Gamma K=0\) but termwise \(\Gamma K\) is not acyclic.
hypotheses: Every nonzero finite-dimensional simple complex Lie algebra in the ordinary smooth positive-current category. In the algebraically graded version, the individual shift \(\langle-\Delta_N\rangle\) places all diagonal classes in energy zero.

The proof uses genuine K-injective products and the actual comparison map. It does not transfer an affine coproduct failure by restriction, or by itself decide the joint derived embedding or equality with cellularization.

claims.title: A bare exterior \(E_3\) algebra has no coupling parameter
claims.statement: A strictly unital \(E_3\)-algebra over \(\mathbb C\) with cohomology \(\Lambda(x_3)\), \(|x_3|=3\), is unique up to equivalence at the level of its bare \(E_3\) structure. That structure alone therefore supplies no varying coupling scalar. A filtration, mixed action, retained translation or central-charge class, marked comparison, or braided category is additional data.
hypotheses: This is single-generator exterior rigidity. It is not a rigidity theorem for arbitrary simple affine cohomology, and uniqueness does not construct an enhancement on a separately prescribed object.
Rank-one coefficient Koszul comparisons retain their specified unipotent sector and separate charge grading; no full all-charge braided equivalence follows from bare formality.

claims.title: The critical translation cone retains kernel and cokernel data
claims.statement: For the two-term translation object \(z_{\rm top}=\operatorname{fib}(T:Z\to Z)\), its cohomology fits into \(0\to\operatorname{coker}(T:H^{n-1}Z\to H^{n-1}Z)\to H^n(z_{\rm top})\to\ker(T:H^nZ\to H^nZ)\to0\). At critical level it cannot simply be identified with the oper-form cohomology of the input \(Z\).
hypotheses: This is the formal consequence of the stated translation-cone definition. It does not identify an actual universal critical action space, construct its \(E_2\) structure, or transfer a bracket.

claims.title: The native polar diagram has a fifth-order obstruction problem
claims.statement: Determine the actual fifth-order residual for the prescribed \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) polar comparison in diagram form over \(k[K]\), retaining its native source, lower-order maps and operation identities. The collision-only strict Hopf-twist ansatz is a separate proposal, with a proposed order-\(\hbar^2\) obstruction; neither an all-order native comparison nor uniqueness is established by that proposal. The existing all-order elliptic theorem concerns its own specified family and does not settle this diagram comparison.
hypotheses: The source and prescribed operations belong to the native diagram-form polar problem. A strict Hopf twist, published existence of other quantum vertex structures and a distinct elliptic family are not replacements for that comparison.
No new all-order theorem, uniqueness statement or universal native realization follows from this obstruction question.

claims.title: Positive recipients have a functorial entire-vector core
claims.statement: Every closed invariant subspace of a finite product of the specified positive recipients has a dense complete Fréchet space of vectors entire for the energy action. Its topology is defined using the actual Gaussian-growth final or spectral strong topology. Gaussian Fourier smoothing and the local meromorphic germs are actual continuous operations. Every continuous linear Virasoro morphism preserves these cores with one uniform energy shift, independently of the finite-product presentation.
hypotheses: Fix real \(c>1\). The objects are closed invariant subspaces of finite products of the Gaussian-growth section recipient and admitted positive spectral strong duals; no arbitrary product or nonpositive factor is included.

claims.title: The functorial positive core is not preserved by collision
claims.statement: The actual primary binary collision lies outside the positive entire-vector cores even after every finite complex energy propagation, for the canonical spectral measure and the explicitly admitted alternative measures. Gaussian smoothing changes that operation and is not a Virasoro intertwiner. Separate actual weak-meromorphic and vacuum graph-dual examples also prevent the unchanged ordinary-energy smoothing construction on those factors.
hypotheses: Real \(c>1\), the original normalized positive vertices and canonical measure, boundary hypothesis \(H\), and the stated analytic estimates are retained. Tree comparisons also retain the normalized positive-label pentagon.

For another scalar measure \(\nu\), the collision must have its actual scalar-multiplicity-one realization and satisfy \(\int_0^\infty e^{\delta h(p)}d\nu(p)=\infty\) for every \(\delta>0\). The canonical measure satisfies this condition.

For the Gaussian multiplier \(e^{-\varepsilon L_0^2}\), the specified weak-meromorphic example fails every ordinary exponential stage for all \(\varepsilon>0\); the actual vacuum graph-dual example asserts that failure for \(0<\varepsilon<1\). No assertion for its vacuum case at \(\varepsilon\ge1\) is made.

claims.title: Every finite positive radial comb has its natural output range
claims.statement: For every fixed finite number \(d\ge2\) of positive inputs, fix the output exponent \(s\). The actual radial comb is holomorphic on the universal cover of the strict radial domain, with \(a_j=e^{w_j}\) and \(\Re w_2<\cdots<\Re w_d<-s\). Each compact coordinate set admits one finite Hilbert input stage with a Hilbert–Schmidt bound uniform in all original positive labels and locally uniform in charge. The complete entangled source is \(\widehat\bigotimes_{i=1}^d{}_{\pi}\mathscr E_{p_i}\). All internal and final labels and all descendant levels are uncut, with normally convergent actual cutoffs and exact mark \(2^{(d-1)/4}\sqrt{\prod_v C_0}\).

hypotheses: \(X=\mathbb C/\Lambda\), \(E=\mathbb C/(2\Lambda)\), \(\Lambda=\mathbb Z+\tau\mathbb Z\), with the actual finite deck action and all translated pole diagonals on the cover.
The state fibers are algebraic direct sums of polynomial jets. At each deformation coefficient every input has finite state output; bounds may depend on the input and coefficient.
The inverse limit is completed meromorphic localization, with coefficient-dependent pole bounds. It is not localization by one uniform bounded divisor.
The frame is formed from the actual trace source, an already admitted scalar twist and the specified algebraic state normalization.

claims.title: Constructed regular lattices carry horizontal formal fusion
claims.statement: The abstract normal completions of the regular lattices carry horizontal formal fusion along every anchored partial diagonal. Translated-diagonal alignment, anchor changes, finite fusion forests, reorderings and units satisfy their stated cocycles. Fixed normal coefficients are outer-linear and tangentially horizontal; normal differentiation shifts the coefficient index, and the full residue factors through the stated top relative de Rham quotient.
hypotheses: Complete the regular lattice before internal-diagonal localization. The normal state coefficient at each fixed deformation and normal order is algebraic.

Actual raw Laurent inputs have finite state span over the entire scalar Laurent ring at each deformation coefficient. Larger Laurent-state extensions are defined through the abstract \(\mathsf W\)-frame.
Each subsequent actual fusion places its new Laurent variables before the retained old variables; new-variable pole bounds may depend on the old coefficient.
Anchor changes use the abstract pulled-back output frame at outer collisions. A single normal coefficient need not be anchor-invariant or linear for every normal differential operator.

claims.title: The formal descent has exact raw and numerical boundaries
claims.statement: The actual first frame coefficient fails on an explicit unrestricted raw state-valued Taylor series: one proposed output coefficient is \(\sum_{n\ge0}1\). For a nonzero linear generator \(x\), numerical creation \(e^{tT}x\) has infinite state span and cannot be a meromorphic section in \(P\otimes\mathcal M(U)\). For this same \(x\), the regular-frame diagonal map has the nonzero kernel element \(x\otimes1-1\otimes x\), so these lattice maps do not give ordinary Beilinson–Drinfeld factorization.
hypotheses: These witnesses concern the stated raw substitution, algebraic-state meromorphic recipient and particular regular-lattice diagonal maps.
The abstract formal completion, braided fusion and coefficient \(D\)-modules remain valid. Other analytic state topologies require their own construction.

claims.title: Global moments retain the Cartan cover and sign frames
claims.statement: With one unchanged Cartan coordinate \(\lambda\), the all-positive moment system descends on \(E_H=\mathbb C/(\mathbb Z+2\tau\mathbb Z)\) and intertwines ordinary-diagonal fusion. Here \(\tau\) is the elliptic period parameter. Over \(X=\mathbb C/(\mathbb Z+\tau\mathbb Z)\), independent deck moves transport sign frames. For an anchored collision partition \(\beta:I\twoheadrightarrow B\), let \(\eta_i\) be the relative deck displacements, zero at the chosen anchor of each block, and let \(\epsilon_i\in\{\pm1\}\) and \(\zeta_b\in\{\pm1\}\) be input and output signs. On that translated collision, fusion is a moment map exactly when \(\epsilon_i\chi(\eta_i)=\zeta_{\beta(i)}\), where \(\chi(m+n\tau)=(-1)^n\).
hypotheses: The relative deck displacements lie in \((\mathbb Z+\tau\mathbb Z)/(2\mathbb Z+2\tau\mathbb Z)\), so the parity character is well-defined on them. The two actions use the actual positioned frame and localized scalar base \(S^{-1}\mathbb C[\lambda]\).
Balanced tensorators use the inverse limits of their specified finite-deformation coefficient-lattice tensors after common spectral scalar extension.
The fixed all-positive system does not descend under independent \(\tau\)-moves on \(X\) with the original deck maps and unchanged right scalar action.
No tensor-closure theorem for arbitrary full normal-completed state modules is asserted.

claims.title: Formal global descent applies to the actual native quintic realization
claims.statement: The frame \(\mathsf W_I^{(5)}=\mathsf F_I\mathsf B_I^{(5)}(\mathcal H_5)_I\) gives the coefficient \(D\)-modules, regular lattices, formal fusion, typed normal cuts and Cartan sign-frame descent for the actual all-order theory matching full native \(Y_{\le5},S_{\le6}\). Its exact generating exchange and all independent linear jets are retained.
hypotheses: The admitted raw scalar is \(k_5=\hbar^2\wp+L_W+\frac32\hbar^4\wp^2\), before the ordered \(\mathcal H_5=\mathcal C\mathcal F_4\mathcal F_5\).
Use the full regular state normalizers and geometric inverses, with translation and period compatibility.
All abstract-completion, Laurent nesting, anchor and Cartan-sign conditions of formal descent remain.

The same formal descent diagrams hold for \(Y_6^\ddagger\) on the pullback of the quintic regular lattice under the sextic state map. An independently selected lattice and analytic sewing still require comparison.

claims.title: Current-equivariant supported operations have an independent definition
claims.statement: For the induced \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) modules, independently defined current coinvariants and supported operations satisfy \(\mathcal I_\kappa^{\mathrm{supp}}(m,n;p)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak{sl}_2}(U_m\otimes U_n,U_p)\). The normalized map \(\Xi\) recovers every multiplied principal part. It preserves all three stated contextual cuts, fixed finite normals, both vacuum insertions and the separate empty coaugmentation.
hypotheses: The shifted level \(\kappa=k+2\) is irrational. Inputs are algebraic induced states, with their prescribed graded output pairing and normalized tangential KZ branches.
The tensor category uses \(V(U)\odot V(W)=V(U\otimes W)\); its generated supported category retains full output-colour families and every-context-compatible maps.
A fixed selected channel is not an unrestricted tensor functor after output labels are forgotten; the rank-one versus rank-two channel witness remains.

claims.title: Current sewing has distinct fused and separated multiplicativity identities
claims.statement: Normalized oriented current kernels have finite genus-zero forest sewing and a coend comparison after the actual KZ transports on \(M_{0,5}\). A separate one-separation identity is an equality of formal Laurent series in the binary separation, in one fused induced affine module. Its top is the tensor of the two input tops transformed by \(\eta\) and the finite-support coend factor selected by the tensor-product constituents of the original input tops. The full coefficient span consists of the universal top map composed with every nonnegative power of the two-input quadratic Casimir. All multipliers and fixed finite normals are retained.
hypotheses: Keep the rigid KZ category, normalized horizontal germs, prescribed outgoing current actions and finite colour support.

Here \(\eta\) is the identity or a strong monoidal autoequivalence of the finite KZ category, with its compatible marked-current and positioned-coefficient lift. The universal top map includes its inverse tensor constraint; the product uses the prescribed inverse block crossing and actual quotient naturality.
The fused one-separation output is distinct from three ordinary affine outputs and from a uniformly finite collapse of separated collars.
No ordinary same-level diagonal affine coaction, arbitrary cyclic/genus-one sewing or unrestricted completed input is included.

claims.title: The marked balanced mixed subsystem has intrinsic operation spaces
claims.statement: Independent finite \(W\)-balance, current equations and vacuum-only homogeneity identify the supported mixed binary operation space with the current operation space and \(\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak{sl}_2}(U_m\otimes U_n,U_p)\). Extension and restriction recover every multiplied principal part and are natural in operation parameters.
hypotheses: \(\kappa=k+2\) is irrational, the Gaussian parameter \(\kappa_G\ne0\), and \(\lambda_G\) is arbitrary.
\(W=\mathbb C[\phi,j_0,j_1,\ldots]\otimes\mathbb C[\Lambda]\), with \(\Lambda\subset\mathbb C\) a free finite-rank additive subgroup and finite algebraic support in each state.
The source is the gauge-defined marked \(W\)-balanced, vacuum-normalized subsystem. Position-dependent horizontal coefficients are not silently identified with constant operation parameters.

claims.title: The mixed operation embedding preserves actual maps and all three cuts
claims.statement: The marked balanced subsystem embeds faithfully into the common mixed coefficient category on full output-colour families and every-context-compatible maps. Actual source and interacting target gauges preserve the left, right and nonconsecutive collision routes, whose supported maps satisfy \(\rho_L-\rho_R+\rho_N=0\) for their common multiplied germ. Units and finite normals are preserved. The maps extend through every fixed finite forest on the specified bounded ordered stages.
hypotheses: Retain the full gauges, paired inverse transports, original channel labels and finite non-Gaussian state spans.
At source degree/jet bounds \(d,J\), the gauge loss is \(d(2J+2)\); residue transfer updates both bounds and recomputes the target gauge loss.
Use distinct normal variables in their declared Laurent order. No same-variable reinsertion of an unrestricted full Taylor output is admitted.

claims.title: Marked mixed multiplicativity uses the finite KZ coend
claims.statement: The one-separation multiplicativity identity is an equality of formal Laurent series in the binary separation. Its output is one induced affine module tensored with \(W\); the induced top is the tensor of the two input tops transformed by \(\eta\) and the finite-support coend factor selected by the tensor-product constituents of the original input tops. Both sides retain the actual combined connection and the full coefficient span obtained by composing the universal top map with every nonnegative power of the two-input quadratic Casimir. The identity follows from naturality for actual induced finite-KZ maps tensored with \(1_W\), and survives the stated full-gauge, supported and bounded-stage extensions.
hypotheses: The coend has finite KZ support on each finite input. Here \(\eta\) is the identity or a strong monoidal autoequivalence of the finite KZ category with a compatible marked-current and positioned-coefficient lift. Its inverse tensor constraint defines the universal top map into the stated output, and its coend product retains the prescribed inverse block crossing.
The output is one fused module. This coend does not represent every family in the enlarged Gaussian or mixed category.

claims.title: The intrinsic balanced operations form a proper ambient subsystem
claims.statement: The marked \(W\)-balanced operation subsystem is not closed under arbitrary ambient horizontal postcomposition. The vacuum projection gives a counterexample even in charge zero. Thus the faithful intrinsic embedding does not identify all ambient mixed \(\operatorname{Hom}\) spaces or reconstruct the whole enlarged category from its finite KZ coend.
hypotheses: The source balance, vacuum normalization and fixed actual comparisons are retained.
Generated every-context-compatible maps remain admitted; arbitrary intermediate-channel projectors, block splittings and unrestricted completions require separate hypotheses.

claims.title: Local cyclic Riesz spaces carry actual based action Gaussians
claims.statement: Every specified finite cyclic Riesz space has a convergent even Gaussian cycle and ordered odd integral, with its independently based semidensity. With the independently chosen current determinant semidensity frames, the actual affine-to-stress/quartet change of variables gives finite Fubini with \(J_\Gamma=\varepsilon_\Gamma j_\Gamma\), where \(j_\Gamma\) is the inverse current Berezinian and \(\varepsilon_\Gamma\in\{\pm1\}\) is the separate cycle comparison.
hypotheses: Fix \(0<|q|<1\), \(\kappa\ne0\), \(\hbar>0\), the local cyclic gauge and its exact paired carriers.
Fix each Riesz contour and shrink to a constant-rank source patch; smooth or holomorphic dependence follows the actual finite data.

Choose the three homogeneous current frames independently and use their inverse determinant sections as semidensities, with stress before quartet in the determinant order. Finite stress rescaling, odd order and even-cycle phases are specified before integration. For arbitrary input density factors the density Jacobian instead retains \([\rho_{\mathrm{aff}}/(\rho_{\mathrm{st}}\rho_{\mathcal Q})]\operatorname{Ber}_{L}(m)^{-1}\), where the \(\rho\)'s are the three chosen density factors and \(m\) is the finite Lagrangian change of variables.
These Riesz action spaces are not identified with the original coefficient-cutoff integration spaces.

claims.title: The local quartet has a computed finite phase and a retained harmonic state
claims.statement: On each complete paired spectral cut, the signed singular-frame quartet integral is \(1\), while the literal-frame integral is \((-1)^{N_\Sigma+\eta_\Sigma}\). The full mass-one harmonic residual remains an eight-dimensional paired state with its internal differential; its signed integral is \(+1\) and its literal integral is \(-1\).
hypotheses: \(N_\Sigma\) counts positive coefficient singular pairs and \(\eta_\Sigma=1\) when the full mass-one block is included.
Use the specified coefficient metrics, actual finite action, real even cycle, ordered odd extraction and frame convention.
An unscaled sequence of literal signs converges only when its prescribed parity is eventually constant. Positive heat torsion alone does not establish that condition.

claims.title: The local gauge has an intrinsic heat source connection and finite part
claims.statement: On the new paired local-gauge carriers, positive-time action heat has its full weak source insertion and equals the direct coefficient endpoint heat torsion. Local bulk and boundary counterterms give an intrinsic finite part in \(C^k\), with \(O(\sqrt\epsilon)\) remainder and commutation with the prescribed finite source derivatives.
hypotheses: Use a finite-dimensional \(C^k\) family of sufficiently small smooth reflected Ward sources, with finitely many sufficiently high smooth bounds and the stated radial metrics.
The exact paired-dual weak boundary distribution and the moving native source-graph Green contact remain in source differentiation.
The finite-part prescription belongs to this local gauge. Identification with original coefficient-cutoff semidensities, physical action corrections or an absolute continuum phase remains separate.

claims.title: Actual finite shell integrals glue a local Gaussian line
claims.statement: Finite cyclic shell integration glues the local spectral charts to a Gaussian line with transition \(T_{ij}=g_j/g_i\). The graded Kato determinant connection is flat, and the actual affine density factor is source-constant in its independently parallel current frames. The full Kato connection can still have nonzero curvature.
hypotheses: Use the fixed local/Riesz carrier, actual internally invariant current projections, small reflected Ward sources and finitely many contours on each overlap.

On the finite paired cyclic Riesz space \(F_\Gamma\), let \(H_\Gamma\) be the paired heat generator and \(N\) total degree. Set \(k_\Gamma=\tfrac12\operatorname{Str}_{F_\Gamma}(N\log H_\Gamma)\), using the logarithm on the fixed right half-plane. In a parallel density-cycle frame, the actual action integral is \(g_\Gamma=c_\Gamma e^{k_\Gamma}\), with \(c_\Gamma=g_\Gamma(u_*)e^{-k_\Gamma(u_*)}\ne0\) at a chosen reference source \(u_*\). Every action constant, frame factor, quartet sign and cycle phase stays in \(c_\Gamma\).
No source neighborhood common to an unbounded family of contours, convergence of arbitrary independently based bare vacua or infinite literal phase product is asserted.

claims.title: A finite action anchor determines a horizontal renormalized section
claims.statement: An independently specified nonzero finite action anchor determines a section of the glued local Gaussian line. Its complementary heat finite part is \(h_{\mathrm{ren}}-k_\Gamma-\gamma_E\nu_\Gamma\); the finite action constants and Euler term give exact gluing. After counterterm scaling, sections converge in \(C^k\) and source connections in \(C^{k-1}\). Actual affine Fubini descends and preserves these transports.
hypotheses: Use a contractible finite-dimensional \(C^k\) source chart, \(k\ge2\), of sufficiently small smooth reflected Ward pairs, containing source zero. Its prescribed finite source jets are bounded in sufficiently many coefficient norms, on the fixed marked geometry and nonzero level.

For the finite paired cyclic Riesz space \(F_\Gamma\), \(N\) is total degree and \(H_\Gamma\) is its paired heat generator. Define \(\nu_\Gamma=\tfrac12\operatorname{Str}_{F_\Gamma}N\) and \(k_\Gamma=\tfrac12\operatorname{Str}_{F_\Gamma}(N\log H_\Gamma)\), with the logarithm on the fixed right half-plane. Here \(\gamma_E\) is Euler's constant, and \(h_{\mathrm{ren}}\) is the intrinsic local coefficient heat finite part after its specified local subtractions.

The finite anchor includes its own scalar and phase, and the quartet vacuum is counted once. In a parallel density-cycle frame, \(g_\Gamma=c_\Gamma e^{k_\Gamma}\) is the actual action integral and \(c_\Gamma\ne0\) retains its based density and cycle phase.
Positive-scale source and scale transport is exact; the stated source estimates do not give a pointwise limit of the \(d\epsilon\) component at zero.
The result is on the local/Riesz line with the exact paired boundary forms. Original cutoff, fixed-adjoint and physical-cap identifications remain additional.

claims.title: The specified boundary-zero filling has zero formal native finite part
claims.statement: For \(F_\lambda=z-\lambda z(t/r)^2\), the original fixed-adjoint native connection has zero heat finite part at every formal source degree. Its source derivative is \(\left.\partial_\lambda\Theta^{\mathrm{nat}}_{\epsilon,\lambda}\right|_0=A_\kappa\epsilon^{-3/2}+B_\kappa\epsilon^{-1/2}+O(\sqrt\epsilon)\), with both power coefficients retained. The independent stress connection vanishes at each positive heat time coefficientwise, and this family has exactly zero source-graph Green contact.
hypotheses: Use \(q=e^{-L}\in(0,1)\), \(L>0\), \(\kappa\ne0\), the original radial coefficient metric and full reflection realization.
The source is the full rational filling family and its Schwarzian stress; the adjoints are fixed at source zero.

Finite parts are coefficientwise in formal \(\lambda\). The \(\lambda^2\) coefficient of the source-zero-normalized scalar primitive is one half of the displayed connection derivative. Neither the native positive-time connection nor its unevaluated power coefficients is declared zero.
This is a theorem for the specified family, not general filling independence or a numerical resummed small-time theorem.

claims.title: The original coefficient cutoffs have a formal positive-heat limit
claims.statement: The original finite action Gaussian determines \(\mathcal G_{\Lambda,\epsilon}(\mu)=G_\Lambda(0)\exp(W_{\Lambda,\epsilon}(\mu)-W_{\Lambda,\epsilon}(0))\). At fixed positive heat time its source-normalized ratio, source connection and fixed source derivatives converge coefficientwise as the original cutoff is removed, with rapid spectral tails. At fixed finite cutoff, removing the heat recovers the original Gaussian branch.
hypotheses: Fix \(\kappa\ne0\), \(\hbar>0\), marked \(0<|q|<1\), the common coefficient metric and a fully reflected smooth integrable formal family with its actual Ward filling.

For the original cutoff coefficient complex \(C_\Lambda\), set \(a_\Lambda=d_{\Lambda,0}^{\dagger}\), \(\Delta_{\Lambda,\mu}=\{d_{\Lambda,\mu},a_\Lambda\}\) and \(W_{\Lambda,\epsilon}=-\int_\epsilon^\infty\operatorname{Str}_{C_\Lambda}(Ne^{-t\Delta_{\Lambda,\mu}})\,dt/t\). Here \(N\) is total coefficient degree including ghosts; this coefficient trace has no paired factor \(1/2\). The adjoint is fixed at source zero. Full HPL returns, mixed source jets and ordered Duhamel terms remain in every variation.
The original \(G_\Lambda(0)\), shell determinants/Pfaffians, density and phase remain. No numerical cutoff limit or joint cutoff/heat limit follows.

The original moving-graph Green contact and source-zero Gaussian factors remain separate from this difference of complete coefficient connections.

claims.title: The formal placement difference has a local boundary factor
claims.statement: The direct heat constant of the original two-placement difference is a closed local boundary one-form, determined by a finite native jet recursion. Its source-zero-normalized primitive \(C_{\mathrm{place}}\) gives the relative factor \(\exp C_{\mathrm{place}}\) after the two logarithmic potentials are renormalized in that common convention. A whole integrable family vanishing in a fixed boundary collar has \(C_{\mathrm{place}}=0\).
hypotheses: At each fixed source degree, retain the actual metric, ghost terms, distinct heat speeds, full mixed source jets and finite upper geometry.
Uniform \(O(\sqrt\epsilon)\) remainders require bounded finitely many sufficiently high \(C^K\) seminorms on the double; boundary jet values alone are insufficient.
The primitive follows the actual integrable parameter family. It is the finite part of a logarithmic potential, not the finite part of an exponential.

General boundary coefficients remain unevaluated. A zero relative phase requires the stated real \(q=e^{-L}\) family and anti-linear symmetry; the absolute source-zero phase and global holonomy remain separate.

claims.title: The original fixed-adjoint expression has numerical heat on weighted coefficients
claims.statement: The operator \(A_{\mu,T}=\{d_{\mu,T},a_0\}\), with the original \(a_0=d_0^\dagger\) held fixed, has a gapped sectorial realization on reflected coefficient offsets \((2,1,0,2,0)\), with common domain two Sobolev derivatives higher. On one small \(C^4(\mu)\oplus C^1(T)\) ball its heat is source-holomorphic and trace class, with \(\|e^{-tA}\|_1\le C(1+t^{-3/2})e^{-ct}\).
hypotheses: Fix the original radial metric, marked \(0<|q|<1\) and \(\kappa\ne0\), in component order \((E,H,F,b,c)\).
The common domain has regularities \((4,3,2,4,2)\) and all corresponding iterated reflection conditions, defined on the double.
The carrier changes; the differential expression \(a_0\) is not replaced by the Hilbert adjoint in the new norm.
Every fixed ambient source derivative obeys the same time exponent on smaller balls. Smooth-kernel assertions use smooth sources with the required finite higher bounds.

claims.title: Smooth Ward sources have a genuine weighted coefficient contraction
claims.statement: On the smooth Ward locus, the closed coefficient differential and fixed gauge have their maximal doubled distributional graph domains. The bounded map \(r=a_0A_{\mu,T}^{-1}\) satisfies \(r^2=0\) and \(dr+rd=1\) on the differential domain. It preserves the original fixed smooth gauge image and agrees with the ordinary reduced inverse on their common domain.
hypotheses: Use the numerical weighted carrier and one sufficiently small finite-norm source ball, with smooth reflected integrable sources and actual Ward stress.

In component order \((E,H,F,b,c)\), set \(\mathbf r=(2,1,0,2,0)\), \(\mathbf w=(0,1,2,0,1)\), and \(X^s=\bigoplus_iH_+^{s+r_i}(w_i)\). Here \(H_+^s(w)\) is the positive-reflection Sobolev space of weight-\(w\) coefficient forms, defined on the closed double and then restricted to the half-manifold. The graph domains contain \(X^1\) but are not identified with it; no negative-order half-manifold trace is imposed.
This contraction does not sum an original sharp-tail HPL series, construct the full paired moving-graph heat domain or overturn the original physical coefficient-\(L^2\) obstruction.

claims.title: Numerical positive-time scalars realize the formal Taylor coefficients
claims.statement: The source-normalized scalar \(\mathcal R_\epsilon=\exp(W_\epsilon-W_\epsilon(0,0))\), with \(W_\epsilon=-\int_\epsilon^\infty\operatorname{Str}_X(Ne^{-tA_{\mu,T}})\,dt/t\), is numerical, holomorphic and nonzero. Here \(N\) is total coefficient degree including internal ghost degrees, and \(\operatorname{Str}_X\) is the graded trace on the weighted coefficient carrier \(X\). Its complete source, scale and mixed derivatives have exactly the formal ordered Duhamel coefficients of the original-cutoff prescription. The numerical Ward-family placement identity uses the two actual heats.
hypotheses: Heat time is fixed and positive. In component order \((E,H,F,b,c)\), \(X=\bigoplus_iH_+^{r_i}(w_i)\), with \(\mathbf r=(2,1,0,2,0)\), \(\mathbf w=(0,1,2,0,1)\); \(H_+^s(w)\) denotes the positive-reflection Sobolev coefficient space on the double, restricted to the half-manifold. The heat generator is \(A_{\mu,T}=\{d_{\mu,T},d_0^\dagger\}\), with the original source-zero adjoint fixed.
Scalar algebra also holds for the polynomial source extension off the Ward locus; cochain and closed-tangent placement identities require Ward.
An arbitrary formal family is pulled back coefficientwise; convergence of its source series is not assumed.
No general numerical small-time expansion, logarithm exclusion, numerical finite part, numerical original-cutoff convergence or unnormalized continuum vacuum is supplied.

claims.title: Connected two-current trees admit every fixed normal order
claims.statement: Connected two-current classical-action-Hessian trees at bare order \(\chi\) have a prepared local/forward extension for every fixed pair of normal and holomorphic orders. Complete finite-upper-time moments subtract all proper one-root and two-root clusters, disjoint products and overlapping alternatives. The resolved and coincident strong limits agree with error \(O(\delta(1+|\log\delta|)^B)\), \(\delta=\sqrt\epsilon\).
hypotheses: Incoming derivatives precede zero-height restriction. Tangential roots are \(o\pm\delta\xi/2\), with \(\xi\) in a fixed compact set and \(0<L_0\le L\le L_1<\infty\).
Fix every field, component, derivative and polynomial normal-growth stage on the original completed projective joint tests; constants may depend on those stages.
Overlaps wholly inside one small rooted component remain alternative terms of its complete smaller forest. Only nested or disjoint clusters occur together.
Normal derivatives act on retained ambient extension data. Unary wheels, zero-vertex scalar pairs, arbitrary independent heights, prescribed-normalization equality and all-arity closure are separate.

claims.title: Unary current loops and their ordered products admit all fixed normal orders
claims.statement: Unary one-loop current factors have strong prepared extensions at every fixed normal and holomorphic order. Odd normal orders of a current zero-form vanish at positive cutoff; even orders retain their full finite-upper-time moments. Classical factors use the root degree \(2+m+j\), where \(m,j\) are the incoming normal and holomorphic orders, including odd scalar responses. Their graded order-one products converge with both double-subtraction terms retained.
hypotheses: Use bare \(\chi=-\hbar\), independent fixed \(\kappa\), fixed field/component stages, common positive cutoff and compact positive upper-time intervals.
The classical root-degree and scalar-edge estimates apply at every fixed incoming normal order.
An inert ghost carries the complete normal/holomorphic Leibniz sum, so an odd total normal order of a ghost composite need not vanish.
The nonzero rescaled even-order \(h\)-row witness concerns the raw leading term; it does not assert a nonzero renormalized finite part for every row.
Only the specified finite linear tail/forward words and compact tangential root resolutions are included; arbitrary independent-height or normalization comparisons remain separate.

claims.title: Mixed current primitives extend across boundary and interior collisions
claims.statement: The ordinary and first-plus-normal \(u,h\) one-vertex matrices, with their actual tree-dressed outgoing fields, admit finite current records and strong collision extensions. The boundary difference is \(O(a(1+|\log a|)^2)\), uniformly in all independent height, separation and common-cutoff ratios. At each fixed mean height \(m>0\), the interior difference is \(O(C_m b(1+|\log b|))\), uniformly in \(b/\sqrt\epsilon\).
hypotheses: Work in \(a\le a_0<\min(1,\sqrt{L_0}/16)\), with \(L\in[L_0,L_1]\subset(0,\infty)\), bare order \(\chi\) and fixed field, test and holomorphic-jet stages.

The boundary record retains the exact heated degree-one layer; the interior direct diagonal also uses its moving Taylor record. Divergent moments keep the actual cutoff-dependent legs and finite \(L\).
The centered subtraction gives the same boundary finite part of this primitive. Its separate interior current power is zero at the boundary itself.
The result covers one-vertex ordinary/first-normal rows, including their ordered \(h,s\) spectator extensions; it does not prove higher incoming normals or higher connected cores.

claims.title: The independent-height source comparison retains a spatial Poisson contact
claims.statement: At separated roots, the original common-cutoff source equals the zero-lower-cutoff interior kernel on the same original residuals plus its explicit spatial Poisson layer and an \(O(\delta b^{-j-k-6})\) error. The layer has bound \(O(a(1+|\log a|))\); its spatial kernel has boundary-first value \(\Pi_{<\epsilon}(0,\cdot)=\pi\delta_0\). Its opposite mixed-current signs and every spectator derivative remain.
hypotheses: These source and layer estimates require \(0<\delta=\sqrt\epsilon\le b/8\), in the fixed collar. For root heights \(r_\pm\ge0\) and tangential separation \(d\), \(a^2=(r_++r_-)^2+2|d|^2\) and \(b^2=(r_+-r_-)^2+2|d|^2\); \(j,k\) are the fixed incoming holomorphic orders. This restriction is not imposed on the separate all-ratio boundary extension.

With \(g_s(v)=(4\pi s)^{-1/2}e^{-v^2/(4s)}\) and \(h_s(z)=(2\pi s)^{-1}e^{-|z|^2/(2s)}\), the spatial kernel is \(\Pi_{<\epsilon}(r,z)=\pi r\int_0^\epsilon g_s(r)h_s(z)\,ds/s\). Its boundary-first value \(\pi\delta_0\) is assigned separately; it is not obtained by substituting \(r=0\) inside the integrand.

For a root \(q=(r,o)\), the zero-lower finite-upper-time responses are \(\Phi_q=2\pi\partial_z\int_0^L\operatorname{erfc}((t+r)/(2\sqrt s))h_s(z-o)\,ds\) and \(R_{t,q}=-2\pi\partial_z\int_0^L[g_s(t-r)+g_s(t+r)]h_s(z-o)\,ds\). The Poisson factor is centred at the plus root and these responses at the minus root; their products are evaluated at the boundary. At an opposing boundary root, both \(\Pi_{<\epsilon}R_t\) and \(\Pi_{<\epsilon}\partial_z\Phi\) are signed distributions defined by tangential derivative transfer.

A different example uses constant fields, zero translation and the dual-number algebra \(k[\varepsilon]/(\varepsilon^2)\): for each \(n\ge4\), the stated \(\lambda\)-corrected maps form a valid vacuum residue system through arity \(n\), and extension through \(n+1\) on the same partition coefficients, preserving the lower maps, cuts, monotone collisions and both vacuum formulas, exists exactly when \(\lambda=0\). Full all-partition residue systems with vacuum remain determined by binary and ternary residues, with arity-three locality propagating to all arities. The positive full-recipient all-arity conclusions are unchanged.
hypotheses: The cut-lattice assertion concerns precisely the stated lattice tests and their regular unit sections. It makes no claim about bounded presentations supplied with additional structure.
The delayed-failure examples concern arity. They do not establish arbitrarily late failure, or uniformity, in deformation order, energy or normal depth.

claims.title: The radical filtration gives an exact recognition criterion
claims.statement: The actual radical grading gives a finite-weight subcoalgebra tower and full derived quasi-free bimodule cells. For each positive radical layer, let \(T_n\) be the exact extension complex for either \(G=C_V\) or \(G=C_V\otimes^{!}C\). If \(H^j(T_n)=0\) for all \(j\le0\), for every full weight-zero map with the prescribed singleton unit, both full pointed restriction maps are equivalences. The first extension fibre is \(\Omega^\infty T_1\). The criterion retains the entire twisting map and the supplied full path \(hu\simeq\nu_V\).
hypotheses: Over a characteristic-zero field on the affine line, use the actual derived ordered-collision coefficient category, extraordinary collision restriction, disjoint convolution and same-position tensor. Retain complete pointings, action paths, ordered faces and arbitrary parameter spaces.

Let \(V\) be an arbitrary unbounded unital dg chiral algebra with its genuine closed horizontal vacuum and native main-diagonal finite-partition Chevalley source. For \(G=C_V\) or \(C_V\otimes^{!}C\), use the actual sector actor \(F_G=P(J_1)\otimes^{!}G\), with \(C=C_{k^2}\). The pointing on \(F_{C_V}\) is supplied with a path \(hu\simeq\nu_V\) of full coassociative pointings.
The hypothesis concerns both full character and action recipients and every positive radical weight. A zero vacuum composite does not remove the other components of the twist.

claims.title: A strict idempotent pointing has full recognition
claims.statement: Let \(A\) be an arbitrary unbounded commutative unital dg algebra with zero translation, and let \(e\in Z^0A\) satisfy \(e^2=e\). Give its Chevalley actor the full pointing induced by \(1\mapsto e\). Projection to \(eA\) induces equivalences on both full pointed character and action spaces, and the intrinsic maps \(\Theta\) and \(\Psi\) are inverse. Naturality includes arbitrary pointed coassociative maps between these actors. For \(A=k^2\) and \(e=p_1\), both spaces are contractible; if \(e=0\), or if \(e\) is a boundary, both are empty.
hypotheses: Over a characteristic-zero field on the affine line, use the actual derived ordered-collision coefficient category, extraordinary collision restriction, disjoint convolution and same-position tensor. Retain complete pointings, action paths, ordered faces and arbitrary parameter spaces.
The idempotent is strict and closed, the translation is zero, and the whole coassociative pointing is retained. A singleton value or a homotopy idempotent is not a replacement for these data.

Its unary vacuum image is homotopic to the specified unit precisely when the singleton \(H^0\)-class agrees with that unit. When it agrees, the space of unary homotopies is contractible and coherent in parameters.

claims.title: The native product retains its symmetric bicomodule pairing
claims.statement: The one-sided PBW products have universal graded expansions with Bernoulli coefficients \(B_k^\pm\). After selecting the target normal coefficient, the two operators are \(A_b^L=\tfrac12+N_b\) and \(A_b^R=-\tfrac12+N_b\), with \(N_b\) locally nilpotent in old-block number. The symmetric native bicomodule pairing is their signed adjoint: the terms involving several old blocks cancel before that selection. Derived support makes the unary maps primitive, and the supplied Taylor family places the remaining higher twists in positive source length after extraction.

Transport the full map \(\varphi:A\to R^+\) along the unital equivalence \(\theta:A\simeq U\) to \(\widehat\varphi:U\to R^+\). Then \(T_n(\varphi)\simeq R\operatorname{Hom}_U(N_n[-1],\operatorname{Ad}_{\widehat\varphi}R)\). The adjoint module is obtained by restriction along \(x\mapsto x\star1-1\star x^{\mathrm{op}}\). This identification retains every higher component of the transported map, the displayed shift and the complete row filtration.

Take \(G=C_V\) or \(C_V\otimes^{!}C\) for a genuine unital dg chiral algebra \(V\). The coefficient is this actual symmetric radical layer; arbitrary positive Lie coefficients are outside the statement.

If the resulting error \(\mathcal E\) raises the complete row filtration, then \(H^{\prime}(1+\mathcal E)^{-1}\) contracts the full twisted layer. The exact enhanced recipient and primitive unary comparison are hypotheses of this contraction statement. Its inverse is rowwise finite; it is not a contraction inferred from a finite arity truncation.

The actual \(\mathrm{T2}\) roof with scalar value \(f(b)=\eta\) maps to the constant alternating matrix \(B_{12}=\eta\), \(B_{21}=-\eta\).

claims.statement: The genuine six-generator bounded tower defines a Kan, quasi-isomorphism-invariant tuple space \(N(B)\) for every ordinary dg vertex target.
