claims.title: The sharp formal range and finite determinant algebra
claims.statement: For every integer \(N\ge1\), let \(\mathcal D\) be the \(\mathbb C[[\hbar]]\)-complete Arakawa–Kuwabara–Möller vertex sheaf on \(M_N=\operatorname{Hilb}^N(\mathbb C^2)\). For each of \(\mathcal D\), every quotient \(\mathcal D/\hbar^m\mathcal D\) with integer \(m\ge1\), and the classical quotient \(\mathcal D/\hbar\mathcal D\), its sheaf cohomology is nonzero exactly in degrees \(0\le k<N\). These groups are taken before numerical specialization. For \(N\ge2\), on \(M_N=\operatorname{Hilb}^N(\mathbb C^2)\), let \(\mathcal D\) be the Arakawa–Kuwabara–Möller formal vertex sheaf over \(R=\mathbb C[[\hbar]]\), let \(\beta\) be the connecting map for \(0\to\mathcal D\xrightarrow{\hbar}\mathcal D\to\mathcal D/\hbar\mathcal D\to0\), and put \(\kappa_r=T^r\beta(\phi\psi)\), where \(\phi\psi\) is the classical invariant contraction of the two fundamental fermions. The normal-cup subalgebra generated by the scalar vacuum and the \(\kappa_r\), using finite sums and finite products, is \[\frac{R\otimes_{\mathbb C}\Lambda(e_0,e_1,\ldots)}{(\hbar e_r\ (r\ge0),\ \Lambda^{\ge N})},\qquad e_r\mapsto\kappa_r.\] Each \(e_r\) has sheaf degree one, intrinsic even parity and conformal weight \(r+1\); the exterior sign comes from sheaf degree, and there is no completion in the translation index. Every nonempty increasing product of fewer than \(N\) generators is nonzero and not \(\hbar\)-divisible, remains nonzero in every finite \(\hbar\)-quotient, and vanishes under torus-finite specialization at \(\hbar=1\).
hypotheses: Use \(R=\mathbb C[[\hbar]]\), integer \(N\ge1\), and each finite quotient \(\mathcal D/\hbar^m\mathcal D\) with \(m\ge1\).
The determinant algebra uses no completion in the translation index. Its exterior sign comes from sheaf degree, not intrinsic odd parity.

claims.title: Completed rank-two torsion blocks
claims.statement: For the formal rank-two Hilbert-scheme vertex sheaf, the completed block description assembles complexes before taking cokernels. It exhibits arbitrary finite \(\hbar\)-torsion orders and a nonzero nonseparated/Milnor part. Derived completeness therefore does not imply ordinary separated completeness in this example. Torus-finite specialization alone can fail vertex-module truncation; the ordinary module assertion also imposes conformal local finiteness.
hypotheses: Use \(R=\mathbb C[[\hbar]]\), integer \(N\ge1\), and each finite quotient \(\mathcal D/\hbar^m\mathcal D\) with \(m\ge1\).
The determinant algebra uses no completion in the translation index. Its exterior sign comes from sheaf degree, not intrinsic odd parity.

claims.title: The top torsion representation at every reduced charge
claims.statement: In the rank-two calculation, remove the \(\mathrm{Sb}\otimes bc\) spectators and work over \(R=\mathbb C[[\hbar]]\). For positive reduced fermion number \(r\), put \(a=\lfloor(r-1)/2\rfloor\), \(h=r(r-2)/2+q\), \(d=2q-r\) and \(\mu=a-r/2\). Torsion first occurs at \(q=a+1=\lceil r/2\rceil\). At every \(q\ge a+1\), its full highest-weight-\(d\) component is \[\mathcal T_{r,q}[d]\cong R/(\hbar^{q-a})[\mu]\otimes\operatorname{Sym}^{d}\mathbb C^2.\] The divided \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) action is defined on the torsion-free sheaf before cohomology. The projected normal-current map between adjacent top components is \(\hbar\) times the specified Cartan product; lower-spin outputs can occur before projection. Spectators shift total charge and conformal weight.
hypotheses: Remove the \(\mathrm{Sb}\otimes bc\) spectators. Fix \(r\ge1\), set \(a=\lfloor(r-1)/2\rfloor\), \(h=r(r-2)/2+q\), \(d=2q-r\), and \(\mu=a-r/2\).
The divided \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) action is defined on the torsion-free sheaf before cohomology; it does not divide elements inside torsion.
Charge is reduced charge. Reattaching spectators shifts total charge and conformal weight. Omit zero-length torsion summands.

claims.title: The next torsion spin and the first two occurrences
claims.statement: In the spectator-free rank-two calculation, let \(R=\mathbb C[[\hbar]]\), take positive reduced fermion number \(r\), and set \(a=\lfloor(r-1)/2\rfloor\), \(d=2q-r\), with conformal weight \(h=r(r-2)/2+q\). For \(q\ge a+2\), the multiplicity module of highest weight \(d-2\) is \(R/(\hbar^{q-1})[-1/2]\) when \(r=1\); it is \((R/(\hbar^{q-1-a})[-1/2])^{\oplus2}\) when \(r\ge3\) is odd; and it is \(R/(\hbar^{q-1-a})[-1]\oplus R/(\hbar^{q-2-a})[0]\) when \(r\) is even. Zero-length summands are omitted. The first two occurrence energies have complete representation descriptions. Components of spin \(d-4\) and below, their birth bounds, the full specialization quotient and a closed all-weight interval character remain undetermined.
hypotheses: Remove the \(\mathrm{Sb}\otimes bc\) spectators. Fix \(r\ge1\), set \(a=\lfloor(r-1)/2\rfloor\), \(h=r(r-2)/2+q\), \(d=2q-r\), and \(\mu=a-r/2\).
The divided \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) action is defined on the torsion-free sheaf before cohomology; it does not divide elements inside torsion.
Charge is reduced charge. Reattaching spectators shifts total charge and conformal weight. Omit zero-length torsion summands.

claims.title: The continuous D3 and independent bulk comparison
claims.statement: Over \(\mathbb C\), for the boundary vertex algebras at every finite rank \(N\ge1\) and their polynomial rank-parameter family, construct a completed chiral Koszul dual together with a specified category of smooth modules and a functorial equivalence preserving the vacuum and collisions. Compare that construction with independently defined twisted bulk observables and defects, including the normalization of the rank parameter; the classical bar models and the finite-word vacuum-mode algebra do not supply this comparison. The continuous recipient and collision tensor must retain the formal torsion and nonseparated information. A rank-changing Hall action cannot commute with the conformal modes in the naive way: the central charge changes by \(-3(2N+1)\), so a compatible stress-tensor intertwining law must be supplied. The stable trace comparison holds only in \(2h\le N\), with its first deficit at weight \((N+1)/2\).
hypotheses: Preserve the actual vacuum, finite-rank boundary algebra and formal/nonseparated information in any completed recipient.
The Kodaira–Spencer bulk and defect action must be independently defined; the stable trace range is not an all-rank identification.

claims.title: The particle cohomology category at nonzero Weyl parameter
claims.statement: At Cherednik coupling \(c=0\) and fixed numerical \(\hbar\in\mathbb C^\times\), put \(B_N=((W_\hbar\otimes\Lambda\theta)^{\otimes N})^{S_N}\). Fullness of the symmetric idempotent in the Weyl–exterior crossed product identifies ordinary unbounded derived \(B_N\)-modules with the specified equivariant coderived comodules and contraderived contramodules over a curved conilpotent coalgebra. The small relative presentation has curvature \(\hbar\sum_i\xi_i\eta_i\), and its even generators \(u_i\) act locally nilpotently in the comodule interpretation. This is a cohomology-algebra theorem, not formality of the full BRST complex. The fullness argument fails at \(\hbar=0\), \(N\ge2\).
hypotheses: Fix \(c=0\), \(\hbar\in\mathbb C^\times\), and \(B_N=((W_\hbar\otimes\Lambda\theta)^{\otimes N})^{S_N}\).
Use ordinary unbounded derived modules, equivariant coderived comodules and equivariant contraderived contramodules over the specified curved conilpotent coalgebra.
The small curved presentation has curvature \(\hbar\sum_i\xi_i\eta_i\); its even generators \(u_i\) act locally nilpotently on the comodule side.

claims.title: Full invariant models and a nonzero fourth operation
claims.statement: Over \(\mathbb C(\hbar)\), the relative curved cobar based on \(D_N(1)\) models the full \(\mathfrak{gl}_N\)-invariant two-matrix complex at every rank, retaining its scalar odd factor. For \(N\ge3\), \(j_*[m_4]=-[\beta\smile\beta]\ne0\) has exact \(\hbar^2\) order and is detected in three-cycle sectors; the polynomial integral complex and every nonzero numerical fibre are nonformal. At \(N=3,4\), a transpose-equivariant minimal model has only \(m_2,m_4\); an \(m_6\) first has room at \(N=5\), without a nonvanishing assertion. Separately, for \(1\le N\le3\) an integral comparison over \(\mathbb C[\hbar]\), without inversion or completion, has a curved discrete-module quotient modelling the ordinary unbounded category. Its derived zero fibre is formal; nonflat modules require derived specialization.
hypotheses: The all-rank curved cobar comparison is over \(\mathbb C(\hbar)\) and uses the affine wreath algebra \(D_N(1)\).
The separate integral comparison is over \(\mathbb C[\hbar]\), without inversion or completion, for \(1\le N\le3\).
Zero-fibre assertions are derived. Nonflat modules require derived specialization.

claims.title: The absolute rank-two source model
claims.statement: The written absolute rank-two model retains a degree-three Chevalley class \(\chi\), with cohomology in degrees \(-1,0,2,3\). Its stated secondary operation on \(s\theta\) and \(\chi\) is \(\hbar^2s^2\) with zero indeterminacy, ruling out formality when \(\hbar^2\ne0\); its zero-parameter model has a strict formality zigzag. The relative complex omits \(\chi\) and has a different formality question. For a nonzero square-zero parameter, vanishing of this detector alone does not prove formality. These source-model conclusions retain their proposed status here; the absolute, relative and full invariant comparisons have different inputs.
hypotheses: Retain the positive Chevalley class \(\chi\); the relative complex has different inputs.
At a nonzero square-zero parameter, vanishing of the \(\hbar^2\) detector does not establish formality.

claims.title: The four established polynomial transport ranges
claims.statement:
Let \(N\ge1\), work over \(\mathbb Q[h]\), and give \(L_h=\mathbb Q[x,y][h]\) the divided Moyal bracket \(b_h=(f*_hg-g*_hf)/h\), with \([x,y]_* =h\). Let \(K_N\) be the polynomial \(GL_N\)-invariant quantum two-matrix BRST complex, with \([X_{ij},Y_{kl}]=h\delta_{il}\delta_{jk}\), the moment matrix \(YX-XY+hNI\), antighost degree \(-1\), and \(\operatorname{Tr}\psi=0\), using divided graded commutators in the target. The symmetrized trace \(J(f)=\operatorname{Tr}\operatorname{Sym}f\) extends to polynomial \(L_\infty\) Taylor maps of ghost degree \(1-n\) through arity five on all polynomial inputs, and to all arities when \(1\le N\le4\). At each proved arity, coupling equations use the arity-completed space \(\prod_{n\ge1}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb Q[h]}(\Lambda^nL_h,K_N)\) with divided convolution bracket; the ordinary associative convention instead uses source bracket \(hb_h\) and Taylor maps multiplied by \(h^{n-1}\). Universally over \(\mathbb Q[
u,h]\), arity four holds in all degrees and all arities hold through total degree 23. The fifth obstruction satisfies \(
u E=\delta\zeta\); specialization \(
u=N>0\) uses division by a rational integer, without inverting \(h\). A universal unlocalized primitive, including \(
u=0\), is not supplied.
hypotheses: Use \(\mathbb Q[h]\), positive numerical ranks, the effective target \(K_N\), and the divided Moyal/convolution brackets.
The universal parameter regime is \(\mathbb Q[\nu,h]\); specialization \(\nu=N\) divides only by a nonzero rational integer, not by \(h\).
The ordinary associative convention instead uses source bracket \(hb_h\) and Taylor maps \(h^{n-1}\Phi_n\).

claims.title: A proposed universal degree-24 transport extension
claims.statement: A proposed universal extension carries all arities through total degree 24 by changing the closed fifth component and using the absence of the required \(V_2\) in \(H_6(q)_{12}\). It remains a candidate beyond the established degree-23 range. Its numerical detector requires quadratic-relative lower maps and allowed changes: classical single-trace normalization or \(r_{(4,0)}=0\) alone allows a ternary change shifting a test by \(-4147200z(x)z(y)\). No completed degree-24 theorem or universal unlocalized primitive is asserted here.
hypotheses: The degree-24 extension is proposed, beyond the established universal degree-23 range.
Its numerical detector restricts lower maps and their allowed changes to the quadratic-relative class.

claims.title: The all-rank degree-two sewing correction
claims.statement: Over \(\mathbb C\), with algebraic tensor products and ordinary derived functors, fix \(\hbar\ne0\) and \(N\ge1\), let \(W=\mathbb C\langle x,y\rangle/(xy-yx-\hbar)\), \(\mathfrak g=W^{\mathrm{Lie}}\), \(U_N=U(\mathfrak g)/(z-N1)\), where \(z\) denotes the central Lie element \(1_W\), and \(A_N=(W^{\otimes N})^{S_N}\). For the algebraic power-sum map \(U_N\to A_N\), \(J(f)\mapsto\sum_i f^{(i)}\), the multiplication \(A_N\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{U_N}A_N\to A_N\) is never a quasi-isomorphism. The module \(F_N=\mathbb C[x_1,\ldots,x_N]^{S_N}\), with \(y_i=-\hbar\partial_{x_i}\), has no flat first-order lift as the central value varies from \(N\), and its resulting class in \(\operatorname{Ext}^2_{U_N}(F_N,F_N)\) is nonzero. For every \(N\ge1\), the kernel of \(U_N\twoheadrightarrow A_N\) is generated by one Newton relation \(e_{N+1}\) and is idempotent. Hence \(\operatorname{Tor}^{U_N}_1(A_N,A_N)=0\), while \(\operatorname{Tor}^{U_N}_2(A_N,A_N)\ne0\) has a split flux-cap surjection onto \(A_N\). The first positive sewing Tor degree is therefore two at every rank.
hypotheses: Fix \(N\ge1\) and \(\hbar\in\mathbb C^\times\); put \(W=W_\hbar\), \(\mathfrak g=W^{\mathrm{Lie}}\), \(U_N=U(\mathfrak g)/(z-N1)\) and \(A_N=(W^{\otimes N})^{S_N}\).
Use algebraic tensor products and ordinary derived functors. Infinite multiplicity spaces are allowed in the Harish–Chandra decomposition.
The split decomposition of \(\operatorname{Tor}_2\) uses a choice of section; projectivity is on each side, not an assertion over \(A_N^e\).

claims.title: The Harish–Chandra sewing bimodules
claims.statement: For the same algebraic power-sum map at \(N\ge1\) and fixed \(\hbar\in\mathbb C^\times\), every \(\operatorname{Tor}^{U_N}_j(A_N,A_N)\) is a direct sum of the Harish–Chandra summands \(D(\tau)=(\tau\otimes W_\hbar^{\otimes N})^{S_N}\), with possibly infinite multiplicities, and is projective as a left and as a right \(A_N\)-module. Projectivity over \(A_N^e\) is not asserted. After choosing a section of the flux cap, \[\operatorname{Tor}^{U_N}_2(A_N,A_N)\cong A_N\oplus K_N^{\mathrm{flux}},\qquad K_N^{\mathrm{flux}}\cong\operatorname{Tor}^{U(W_\hbar^{\mathrm{Lie}})}_2(A_N,A_N).\] The kernel vanishes for \(N=1\). Its vanishing at higher rank, all higher multiplicities, multiplication, higher operations and formality remain open. Ordinary \(\operatorname{Hom}\) and \(\operatorname{Ext}^1\) comparison hold for every module at every rank.
hypotheses: Fix \(N\ge1\) and \(\hbar\in\mathbb C^\times\); put \(W=W_\hbar\), \(\mathfrak g=W^{\mathrm{Lie}}\), \(U_N=U(\mathfrak g)/(z-N1)\) and \(A_N=(W^{\otimes N})^{S_N}\).
Use algebraic tensor products and ordinary derived functors. Infinite multiplicity spaces are allowed in the Harish–Chandra decomposition.
The split decomposition of \(\operatorname{Tor}_2\) uses a choice of section; projectivity is on each side, not an assertion over \(A_N^e\).

claims.title: The remaining transport, sewing and physical comparisons
claims.statement: Over \(\mathbb Q[h]\), extend the polynomial Moyal-to-two-matrix transport to every arity at the remaining ranks \(N\ge5\), without inverting \(h\), and determine the permitted changes of lower Taylor maps. The integral full-complex model beyond matrix size three is a separate category-level question. For independently quantized five-dimensional noncommutative Chern–Simons theory, construct supported bulk, line and surface observables and compare their products and junctions with the algebraic transport, retaining the loop parameter, Moyal parameter and rank normalization. The flux-cap kernel \(K_N^{\mathrm{flux}}\) for \(N\ge2\), all higher Tor multiplicities and the derived sewing multiplication and higher operations also remain undetermined.
hypotheses: Use \(\mathbb Q[h]\), positive numerical ranks, the effective target \(K_N\), and the divided Moyal/convolution brackets.
The universal parameter regime is \(\mathbb Q[\nu,h]\); specialization \(\nu=N\) divides only by a nonzero rational integer, not by \(h\).
The ordinary associative convention instead uses source bracket \(hb_h\) and Taylor maps \(h^{n-1}\Phi_n\).
The all-rank curved cobar comparison is over \(\mathbb C(\hbar)\) and uses the affine wreath algebra \(D_N(1)\).
The separate integral comparison is over \(\mathbb C[\hbar]\), without inversion or completion, for \(1\le N\le3\).
Zero-fibre assertions are derived. Nonflat modules require derived specialization.
Fix \(N\ge1\) and \(\hbar\in\mathbb C^\times\); put \(W=W_\hbar\), \(\mathfrak g=W^{\mathrm{Lie}}\), \(U_N=U(\mathfrak g)/(z-N1)\) and \(A_N=(W^{\otimes N})^{S_N}\).
Use algebraic tensor products and ordinary derived functors. Infinite multiplicity spaces are allowed in the Harish–Chandra decomposition.
The split decomposition of \(\operatorname{Tor}_2\) uses a choice of section; projectivity is on each side, not an assertion over \(A_N^e\).

claims.title: Universal Miura rank addition
claims.statement: For positive integers \(N_1,N_2\), take independent Heisenberg currents with \(J_i(z)J_j(w)\sim k\delta_{ij}/(z-w)^2\) over \(\mathbb C[a,k]\), and form the universal Miura images of \(\prod_{i=1}^N(a\partial+J_i)\). If \(\widehat U\) is the Weyl symbol obtained from the normally ordered symbol by \(\exp(-\tfrac a2\partial_z\partial_p)\), the coproduct is \[\widehat U^{(12)}=\widehat U^{(1)}\exp\!\left[\frac a2\left(\overleftarrow\partial_p\overrightarrow\partial_z-\overleftarrow\partial_z\overrightarrow\partial_p\right)\right]\widehat U^{(2)}.\] This is a coassociative, vacuum-preserving vertex-algebra map from rank \(N_1+N_2\) to the tensor product of the two Miura images. After inverting \(k\), its stress tensor has central charge \(c(N)=N-N(N^2-1)a^2/k\).
hypotheses: Work over \(\mathbb C[a,k]\) in the fixed PBW basis; use independent factors with \(J_i(z)J_j(w)\sim k\delta_{ij}/(z-w)^2\).
The stress-tensor formula inverts \(k\). No arbitrary simple quotient at exceptional parameters is included.

claims.title: Algebraic Miura reflection and the derivative term
claims.statement: For the universal Miura images over \(\mathbb C[a,k]\), use the fixed PBW basis of normally ordered differential monomials in the Weyl fields \(\widehat U_r\). Transposition, reversal of the independent Heisenberg factors and PBW independence show that the scalar structure constants at every pole of \(\widehat U_i(z)\widehat U_j(w)\) lie in \(\mathbb C[a^2,k]\). The rank-addition coproduct has derivative contribution \[\frac a2\bigl(N_1\,1\otimes\partial\widehat U_1-N_2\,\partial\widehat U_1\otimes1\bigr)\] in \(\Delta\widehat U_2\). These formulas concern universal Miura images, without an assertion for arbitrary exceptional simple quotients. They do not require a physical defect interpretation.
hypotheses: Work over \(\mathbb C[a,k]\) in the fixed PBW basis; use independent factors with \(J_i(z)J_j(w)\sim k\delta_{ij}/(z-w)^2\).
The stress-tensor formula inverts \(k\). No arbitrary simple quotient at exceptional parameters is included.

claims.title: Reflection with an independently quantized defect
claims.statement: Consider one-flavour noncommutative Chern–Simons theory on \(\mathbb R_t\times\mathbb C^2\), with \([z_1,z_2]_* =c_{\mathrm M}\), surface \(t=z_2=0\), fixed classical surface currents, current level and universal or finite-rank boundary condition for the surface algebra, and logarithmic flux odd in the loop parameter \(\hbar\). Assume a perturbative defect quantization exists with coincident-point counterterms compatible with \(t\mapsto-t\), and that its Ward equations are reflection covariant with solutions unique modulo changes that are the identity on the classical currents. Then the first-order surface deformation class vanishes. If the currents and source coupling themselves admit a reflection-equivariant choice, their first-order coefficients vanish in that choice.
hypotheses: Assume an actual defect quantization with compatible coincident-point extensions, reflection-covariant Ward equations and uniqueness modulo changes trivial on classical currents.
Coefficient-level vanishing requires a reflection-equivariant choice of currents and source coupling; all-orders evenness also requires quantization to all orders.

claims.title: The conditional physical normalization
claims.statement: With the oriented source couplings of the separated line–surface calculation, the connected tree pole has coefficient \(+\hbar_{\mathrm b}/(4\pi^2)\) for unit source factors. Matching the sign and phase to independently marked physical sources requires a comparison of their couplings. Under the specified perturbative defect and coupling assumptions, the leading relation is \(q=K\hbar/(4\pi^2c_{\mathrm M})\); the further elementary-probe assumptions give \(a=\hbar/(4\pi^2)\). These are leading normalization conditions. Coefficient vanishing requires reflection-equivariant currents and source coupling, and all-orders evenness requires those choices and quantization to all orders. Off-origin propagator vanishing does not determine contact terms.
hypotheses: Assume an actual defect quantization with compatible coincident-point extensions, reflection-covariant Ward equations and uniqueness modulo changes trivial on classical currents.
Coefficient-level vanishing requires a reflection-equivariant choice of currents and source coupling; all-orders evenness also requires quantization to all orders.

claims.title: One physical domain for surfaces, lines and junctions
claims.statement: For an independently renormalized five-dimensional noncommutative Chern–Simons theory with M5 surface defects, construct the surface coefficient complexes and compare physical surface fusion with the rank-adding Miura coproduct. Construct, on the same domains, the line-fusion and mixed line–surface junction maps and compare them with the shifted affine Yangian operations, retaining their distinct parameters and units.
hypotheses: Assume an actual defect quantization with compatible coincident-point extensions, reflection-covariant Ward equations and uniqueness modulo changes trivial on classical currents.
Coefficient-level vanishing requires a reflection-equivariant choice of currents and source coupling; all-orders evenness also requires quantization to all orders.

claims.title: The polynomial two-tower gauge dual
claims.statement: Let \(\mathfrak g\) be a finite-dimensional simple complex Lie algebra and \(\mathfrak a=\mathfrak g\otimes\mathbb C[v_1,v_2,\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)\), with \(\epsilon\) even, so the second current tower is an abelian adjoint module. The universal level-zero current vertex algebra \(V(\mathfrak a)\) has polynomial ghost algebra \(B_{\mathrm{pol}}=C_*(\mathfrak a[t])^{\vee_{\mathrm{fib},t}}\), using the restricted dual in polynomial fibre degree and \(t\)-degree, with \(Qc^i=-\tfrac12f_{jk}{}^ic^jc^k\). There is a graded algebraic identification \(B_{\mathrm{pol}}\simeq(\operatorname{Bar}U(\mathfrak a[t]))^{\vee_{\mathrm{fib},t}}\); cobar recovers \(U(\mathfrak a[t])\), whose primitives and \(d/dt\) recover the current conformal algebra and then \(V(\mathfrak a)\). The coefficients are polynomial in ghosts and jets; full energy-homogeneous coefficient cochains and completed smooth duals have different carriers.
hypotheses: Take a finite-dimensional simple complex \(\mathfrak g\), with \(\mathfrak a=\mathfrak g\otimes\mathbb C[v_1,v_2,\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)\) and even \(\epsilon\).
The polynomial ghost dual is restricted jointly in fibre and jet degree. Smooth completed modules and full algebraic blocks have different carriers.

claims.title: The four-degree quantum quotient and coupling
claims.statement: Let \(\mathfrak g\) be finite-dimensional and simple over \(\mathbb C\), normalize its invariant form \(K\) by long-root squared length two, and choose \(a,\ell\in\mathbb C\) satisfying \(2a\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm{ad}}((\operatorname{ad}X)^4)=3\ell^2K(X,X)^2\) for every \(X\in\mathfrak g\). Over \(R=\mathbb C[s]/(s^3)\), with \(e_1=(1,0)\), \(e_2=(0,1)\), retain currents \(J[0],J[e_1],J[e_2],J[e_1+e_2],\widetilde J[0]\) and axions \(E[e_1],E[e_2],E[e_1+e_2],F[0]\), assign \(J[\alpha],E[\alpha]\) twistor degree \(\alpha\) and \(\widetilde J[\alpha],F[\alpha]\) degree \(\alpha+e_1+e_2\), and kill every state of total degree outside \(\{0,e_1,e_2,e_1+e_2\}\). This quotient admits an \(R\)-free one-loop vertex deformation with quadratic current coefficient \(s^2a\), linear coefficients \(-s^2h^\vee a/3\), \(-2s^2h^\vee a/3\), axion coupling \(s\ell\), and an explicit differential ghost vertex algebra, both free on their retained ordered derivative monomials. Their pairing \(I\) satisfies \(QI+\tfrac12I_{(0)}I=D_{\mathrm{tot}}H\) for an explicit \(H\), so \(Q+I_{(0)}\) squares to zero on the ghost algebra tensored with every ordinary untwisted module of this quotient; the coupling is Maurer–Cartan modulo total translation. At nonzero axion coupling the displayed state-level total derivative is nonzero; zero-mode square-zero does not imply the stronger state-level Maurer–Cartan equation.
hypotheses: Work over \(\mathbb C[s]/(s^3)\); retain twistor degrees \(\{0,e_1,e_2,e_1+e_2\}\) and kill every state outside that total degree set.
Retain the quartic-trace cancellation \(2a\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm{ad}}(X^4)=3\ell^2K(X,X)^2\) and its associated linear coefficient ratios.
The module coupling is for ordinary untwisted modules of this finite quotient.

claims.title: A proposed larger celestial boundary quotient
claims.statement: For \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) and \(\mathfrak{sl}_3\), the proposed bidegree-\((2,2)\) boundary presentation retains \(D_2=\{0,1,2\}^2\) and kills every state of total degree outside \(D_2\), not merely the generators outside it. This larger boundary construction remains a candidate. It has no accompanying \(D_2\) ghost, coupling or module-tensor theorem, so it does not enlarge the established four-degree quantum comparison by itself.
hypotheses: The proposed \(\mathfrak{sl}_2/\mathfrak{sl}_3\) boundary quotient kills every state outside \(D_2=\{0,1,2\}^2\).
Its larger ghost, coupling and module tensor have not been constructed.

claims.title: Algebraic co-vacuum endomorphisms and coinvariants
claims.statement: Over \(\mathbb C\), let \(\mathfrak g\) be finite-dimensional and simple, \(\mathfrak a=\mathfrak g\otimes\mathbb C[u,v,\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)\) with \(\epsilon\) even, \(A=U(\mathfrak a[t,t^{-1}])\), \(\mathfrak p=\mathfrak a[t]\), and \(\mathfrak n=t^{-1}\mathfrak a[t^{-1}]\). Form the level-zero vacuum \(V=A\otimes_{U(\mathfrak p)}\mathbb C\) and co-vacuum \(W=A\otimes_{U(\mathfrak n)}\mathbb C\), inducing from the trivial modules, and compute derived Hom in all algebraic left \(A\)-modules with full algebraic cochains and product totalization. Then \(H^0\operatorname{REnd}_A(W)=U(\mathfrak a)^{\mathrm{op}}\), and \(\mathfrak a^*\) embeds as a split vector-space summand of \(H^1\operatorname{REnd}_A(W)\). Moreover, \(\operatorname{RHom}_A(W,V)=0\), whereas \(\mathbb C\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{U(\mathfrak n)}V\simeq\mathbb C\).
hypotheses: Retain the named vacuum and opposite-induced co-vacuum, full algebraic cochains and their original module categories.
The determinant formula uses the stated invariant-form normalization and total fibre-degree cutoff \(N\).

claims.title: The unrenormalized gauge vacuum pairing diverges
claims.statement: For the level-zero two-tower gauge current algebra \(\mathfrak g\otimes\mathbb C[v_1,v_2,\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)\), with \(\mathfrak g\) finite-dimensional simple over \(\mathbb C\) and \(\epsilon\) even, use the vacuum polarization and normalize \(K\) by long-root squared length two. At total polynomial fibre-degree cutoff \(N\), the determinant cocycle on mode numbers \(m,-m\) of the constant currents is \(2h^\vee(N+1)(N+2)mK_{ab}\). It has no finite limit when \(mK_{ab}\ne0\), so this unrenormalized vacuum construction supplies no finite complementary-level ghost pairing.
hypotheses: Retain the named vacuum and opposite-induced co-vacuum, full algebraic cochains and their original module categories.
The determinant formula uses the stated invariant-form normalization and total fibre-degree cutoff \(N\).

claims.title: The Hessian class survives all algebraic cochains
claims.statement: Let \(S=\mathbb C[v_1,v_2,z,z^{-1}]\) carry the Poisson bracket in \(v_1,v_2\), and give \(S\) its adjoint module structure over \(\mathfrak h=(S,\{\ ,\ \})\). With \(\mathrm{vol}=dv_1\wedge dv_2\wedge dz\), \(\partial^1=\partial_2\), \(\partial^2=-\partial_1\), and \(J_f=(\partial^a\partial_bf)\), define \(\iota_{\psi(f,g)}\mathrm{vol}=\operatorname{tr}(dJ_f\wedge dJ_g)\) and \(\Phi(f,Y)=\sum_{a,b=1}^2\partial_a\partial^b\bigl(Y(\partial^a\partial_bf)\bigr)\). The cocycle \(\Omega_H(f,g,h)=\Phi(f,\psi(g,h))+\Phi(g,\psi(h,f))+\Phi(h,\psi(f,g))\) represents a nonzero class in \(H^3(\mathfrak h;S)\) computed with all algebraic cochains. No algebraic two-cochain has differential equal to this cocycle.
hypotheses: The Hessian class uses the Laurent Hamiltonian Lie algebra with adjoint polynomial coefficients and all algebraic cochains.
The numerical finite-polynomial ghost statement fixes \(h\in\mathbb C^\times\); the homological coalgebra and \(h\)-adic cochains are separate constructions.
Graviton and axion loop kernels must remain separate until an all-input physical equality is supplied.

claims.title: The numerical polynomial Moyal ghosts are not a complex
claims.statement: For polynomial functions on \(\mathbb C^2\), set \(f*_hg=m\exp(\tfrac h2(\partial_1\otimes\partial_2-\partial_2\otimes\partial_1))(f\otimes g)\) and \(b_h(f,g)=(f*_hg-g*_hf)/h\). At every fixed \(h\in\mathbb C^\times\), the finite-polynomial ghost dual is not preserved by the Chevalley–Eilenberg differential: the constant coefficient of \(b_h(v_1^{2r+1},v_2^{2r+1})\) is \((2r+1)!h^{2r}/2^{2r}\) for every \(r\ge0\). The homological Chevalley–Eilenberg coalgebra remains defined, and \(h\)-adic cochains provide the formal dual.
hypotheses: The Hessian class uses the Laurent Hamiltonian Lie algebra with adjoint polynomial coefficients and all algebraic cochains.
The numerical finite-polynomial ghost statement fixes \(h\in\mathbb C^\times\); the homological coalgebra and \(h\)-adic cochains are separate constructions.
Graviton and axion loop kernels must remain separate until an all-input physical equality is supplied.

claims.title: Separate graviton and axion kernels
claims.statement: If the physical graviton and axion contributions are assigned a common loop kernel, the checked linear residual constrains their sum; it does not identify the two contributions separately. Finite tests imposing equality of those sectors do not establish an all-input physical kernel identity. The Hessian obstruction remains a statement about the fixed Laurent Hamiltonian source and adjoint polynomial module, even with all algebraic cochains, while an essentially higher source is a different target.
hypotheses: The Hessian class uses the Laurent Hamiltonian Lie algebra with adjoint polynomial coefficients and all algebraic cochains.
The numerical finite-polynomial ghost statement fixes \(h\in\mathbb C^\times\); the homological coalgebra and \(h\)-adic cochains are separate constructions.
Graviton and axion loop kernels must remain separate until an all-input physical equality is supplied.

claims.title: Smooth quantum modules and global physical comparison
claims.statement: For the two adjoint towers of a simple complex gauge Lie algebra, construct a completion and localization that compare smooth celestial modules with a curved or differential ghost dual, retaining the vacuum and all polynomial fibre degrees. Extend the quantum current and ghost construction beyond the four-degree quotient, and compare its collision operations with the local observables of an independently quantized self-dual gauge theory on twistor space. A finite-on-input principal-parts operator must be promoted to an algebra-valued operation on the chosen completed carrier before it can define the required coproduct and module tensor product. For the universal Hamiltonian current algebra over \(\mathbb C\) and, separately, its \(h\)-adic Moyal deformation or specialization at fixed \(h\in\mathbb C^\times\), construct a completed dual and an equivalence for discrete smooth modules, with common domains for collision operations and exchange. Extend the classical twist on an affine twistor chart to a global comparison with an independently quantized bulk theory, keeping the graviton and axion contributions to the quantum brackets separate.
hypotheses: Take a finite-dimensional simple complex \(\mathfrak g\), with \(\mathfrak a=\mathfrak g\otimes\mathbb C[v_1,v_2,\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)\) and even \(\epsilon\).
The polynomial ghost dual is restricted jointly in fibre and jet degree. Smooth completed modules and full algebraic blocks have different carriers.
Work over \(\mathbb C[s]/(s^3)\); retain twistor degrees \(\{0,e_1,e_2,e_1+e_2\}\) and kill every state outside that total degree set.
Retain the quartic-trace cancellation \(2a\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm{ad}}(X^4)=3\ell^2K(X,X)^2\) and its associated linear coefficient ratios.
The module coupling is for ordinary untwisted modules of this finite quotient.
The Hessian class uses the Laurent Hamiltonian Lie algebra with adjoint polynomial coefficients and all algebraic cochains.
The numerical finite-polynomial ghost statement fixes \(h\in\mathbb C^\times\); the homological coalgebra and \(h\)-adic cochains are separate constructions.
Graviton and axion loop kernels must remain separate until an all-input physical equality is supplied.

claims.title: The induced vacuum and co-vacuum compute different functors
claims.statement: For \(n=2,3\) and a nonzero finite-dimensional complex Lie algebra \(\mathfrak g\), use the polynomial punctured-space current model \(L_n\), its regular subalgebra \(P_n\) and negative subalgebra \(N_n\), at zero central extension. In the ordinary algebraic derived category put \(W_n=U(L_n)\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{U(N_n)}\mathbb C\) and \(V_n=U(L_n)\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{U(P_n)}\mathbb C\). For both full Hom and internally graded Hom, \[R\operatorname{Hom}_{U(L_n)}(W_n,V_n)=0,\qquad \mathbb C\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{U(N_n)}\operatorname{Res}_{N_n}V_n\simeq\mathbb C.\] At \(\mathfrak g=0\), the derived Hom is \(\mathbb C\), so the nonzero hypothesis is essential.
hypotheses: For the mixed vacuum/co-vacuum vanishing take a nonzero finite-dimensional complex Lie algebra; the zero Lie algebra is a separate case.
The dimension-three endomorphism formula uses internally graded Hom and the restricted internal-weight dual.

claims.title: Cohomology and strict two-step endomorphism models
claims.statement: For any finite-dimensional complex Lie algebra \(\mathfrak g\), use the polynomial punctured-space current model at zero central extension and \(W_n=U(L_n)\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{U(N_n)}\mathbb C\), in ordinary algebraic derived modules. In complex dimension two, its derived endomorphism dg algebra is formal for either full or internally graded Hom, with the multiplication for arbitrary nonabelian gauge algebra still separate. In dimension three the internally graded cohomology algebra is \[H^*R\operatorname{End}_{\mathrm{gr}}(W_3)\cong U(P_3)\ltimes\Lambda(N_3^\vee[-1]),\] where \(\vee\) is the restricted internal-weight dual, the exterior generators have degree \(-1\), and the action is \(\rho^\vee(p)\lambda=-\lambda\circ\rho(p)\), with \(\rho(x\otimes f)(y\otimes t)=[x,y]\otimes ft\) using truncated multiplication on principal parts. Before the antipode converts right multiplication, degree zero is canonically \(U(P_3)^{\mathrm{op}}\); formality for an arbitrary nonabelian gauge algebra in dimension three remains open. When \([\mathfrak g,[\mathfrak g,\mathfrak g]]=0\), explicit central primitives \(db(p,v)=[p,v]-\rho(p)v\) correct right multiplication and give a strict unital dg-algebra quasi-isomorphism from the zero-differential semidirect presentation to the actual endomorphism algebra in both dimensions.
hypotheses: All induced objects use zero central extension and ordinary algebraic derived modules; the dimension-three cohomology formula uses internally graded Hom.
The strict multiplicative conclusion in both dimensions adds \([\mathfrak g,[\mathfrak g,\mathfrak g]]=0\). It does not assert arbitrary nonabelian dimension-three formality.

claims.title: The full-Hom coefficient extension
claims.statement: For finite-dimensional complex two-step nilpotent gauge algebras, in dimensions two and three at zero central level, the strict endomorphism model extends to full Hom with polynomial or formal regular coefficients. Only the ghost coefficient families are completed; each regular coefficient remains an algebraic enveloping-algebra element. Scalar extension from polynomial to formal regular coefficients induces an injection on derived co-vacuum endomorphisms. For \(0\ne x\in\mathfrak g\), the formal current \(x/(1-z_1)\) gives an endomorphism outside its image. At \(\mathfrak g=0\) the map is the identity on \(\mathbb C\). This is not an \(\mathfrak m\)-adic completion of the punctured-space model, whose such completion is zero. The theorem includes the nonabelian six-dimensional quadratic cotangent-Heisenberg gauge algebra.
hypotheses: Assume \([\mathfrak g,[\mathfrak g,\mathfrak g]]=0\) and keep ordinary algebraic derived modules at zero level.

For the full-Hom extension, polynomial or formal regular coefficients are permitted, but only ghost coefficient families are completed. Each regular coefficient remains an algebraic enveloping-algebra element.

claims.title: The all-arity paired free surface comparison
claims.statement: For finite-dimensional degree-zero \(V\), fixed volume on \(\mathbb A^2\), \(R=\mathbb C[\hbar,\kappa]\) and \(\lambda=\hbar\kappa\), the compact smooth realization of the paired coalgebra is factorization-equivalent to the independently defined free theory, with all finite marked insertion diagrams and quantum operation cells. The coefficient dual and its inverse also exist. The five-position comparison is already \(1+H_5\), with inverse \(1-H_5\) and \(H_5^2=0\). The nonzero fixed-binary ternary contact \(-\lambda^3(8\pi^2)^{-1}D_{uv}\delta_4\) is carried by that realization; it is a test for the new independent dual, not an obstruction to the existing equivalence. The independent dual and its module tensor are still separate constructions.
hypotheses: Take finite-dimensional degree-zero \(V\), a fixed volume on \(\mathbb A^2\), \(R=\mathbb C[\hbar,\kappa]\) and \(\lambda=\hbar\kappa\).

The paired free comparison retains both colour shifts, the central pairing, local vacuum, translations and every finite marked diagram. Its independent singular-field/internal-line dual and native module tensor remain separate.

claims.title: The full retained-point cubic current morphism
claims.statement: For invariant cubic current systems on a complex surface, let \(A\) be the prescribed unary map and let \(\ell\theta\), \(\ell^{\prime}\theta^{\prime}\) be the central cubic tensors. A filtered vacuum-preserving morphism of the full retained-point systems exists exactly when \(A\) is a Lie map and \(\ell\theta=\ell^{\prime}A^*\theta^{\prime}\). The system retains collisions, vacant-position maps, permutations, partitions, and their mixed coherences. The map \(\operatorname{Sym}(A)\) supplies a full morphism when these conditions hold. Lower correction terms have the stated differential image, while full morphisms between fixed invariant-cubic fibres have zero supported residual. Finite stages bound total particle, central, and Koszul weight together. An independent mixed bulk, a singular-field realization, and an automorphism classification require further constructions.
hypotheses: Use the full retained-point invariant-cubic current system with collisions, vacancies, permutations, partitions and mixed coherences.

claims.title: The specified pure-open six-dimensional obstruction
claims.statement: The specified pure-open quadratic \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) holomorphic Chern–Simons theory on \(K3\times E\) has a nonzero first quantum-master obstruction in its finite-order smooth local category. This rules out quantization in that stated model and category. Adding closed fields or changing the gauge algebra changes the problem; no obstruction to every six-dimensional field content is asserted.
hypotheses: The obstruction concerns the pure-open quadratic \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) model on \(K3\times E\) in its finite-order smooth local category.

claims.title: The conditional cotangent and open–closed theories
claims.statement: For finite positive-height cotangent BF theory, a colour-independent A–B propagator gives a tree quantum-master solution. The rank-compatible \(\mathfrak{sl}(N|N)\) open–closed theory near a compact curve has its stated perturbative quantization. These conclusions retain the finite-height, propagator and rank-compatibility assumptions of their respective theories. They do not identify the coupled normal–polar defect comparison, quantum junction or state/sewing map.
hypotheses: The cotangent BF assertion assumes finite positive height and a colour-independent A–B propagator.
The separate \(\mathfrak{sl}(N|N)\) open–closed assertion assumes rank compatibility near a compact curve.

claims.title: The supported normal-jet construction
claims.statement: The proposed normal-jet construction specifies all-normal-jet maps, independent one-current and profile recipients, cyclic actions, disk operations, common traces, a polarized boundary action and a supported lift. These maps provide concrete source data. The coupled normal–polar variational comparison, quantum junction, state/sewing construction and global oper map remain required; the exact constructor is not asserted here as a completed physical comparison.
hypotheses: These are proposed normal-jet, profile, disk and supported source data, not a completed physical bulk–defect identification.

claims.title: The independent interacting surface bulk
claims.statement: An independent interacting bulk on \(\mathbb R_{\ge0}\times\mathbb C^2\) must carry the actual ternary central operation through a supported boundary/trace map. For the rank-one abelian cubic, the test is \(\ell_3(e_{-1,-1},z_1,z_2)=K_{\mathrm{cen}}\) at retained level \(+\ell\). A binary level with the same shifts cannot replace it. The free paired realization and regular abelian elliptic pushforward do not supply the interacting comparison, its independent field dual, or quantum line theory.
hypotheses: For the paired free branch, take finite-dimensional degree-zero \(V\), a fixed volume on \(\mathbb A^2\), \(R=\mathbb C[\hbar,\kappa]\) and \(\lambda=\hbar\kappa\). The comparison retains both colour shifts, the central pairing, local vacuum, translations and every finite marked diagram.
The cubic-current statement uses the full retained-point system with its collisions, vacancies, permutations, partitions and mixed coherences.

claims.title: Restricted four-dimensional RTT cochain fusion
claims.statement: Over \(\mathbb C\), take the \(\mathfrak{gl}_n\) Yangian in its RTT presentation without a determinant-one quotient, \(n\ge2\), with formal \(\hbar\) of weight \(-1\), and torsion-free lattices \(M=\bigoplus_w\prod_{j\ge0}\hbar^jM_0[w+j]\), where \(M_0[w]=0\) for \(w<0\) and every \(M_0[w]\) is finite-dimensional. If \(B\) is the restricted RTT ghost algebra and \(\mathcal K(M)\) its Koszul cochains with the coaction-dressed left \(B\)-action and ordinary right \(B\)-action, then the associative unital cup product gives \(\mathcal K(M)\widehat\otimes_B\mathcal K(N)\simeq\mathcal K(M\widehat\otimes N)\) on these lattices. On fundamental evaluation modules, \(R(u)=1-\hbar P/u\), with \(P\) the tensor flip, intertwines the two fusions after formal spectral localization; at numerical \(\hbar\), it is invertible when \(u\ne0\) and \(u^2\ne\hbar^2\).
hypotheses: Take \(\mathfrak{gl}_n\), \(n\ge2\), with no determinant-one quotient and formal \(\hbar\) of weight \(-1\).
Use torsion-free weightwise-complete lattices with nonnegative underlying weights and finite-dimensional weight spaces. Boundedness below is essential.

claims.title: The restricted RTT ghost algebra and its level shift
claims.statement: For \(\mathfrak{gl}_n\), \(n\ge2\), with no determinant-one quotient, formal \(\hbar\) of weight \(-1\) and torsion-free weightwise-complete lattices of nonnegative finite-dimensional underlying weights, the restricted RTT construction gives a dg quantum ghost vertex algebra with PBW basis, \(dc=-c^2\), translation and exchange containing \((2,0)\) and \((0,2)\) ghost components. The mixed relation fixes the traceless affine form: the scalar sector has level zero, complementary shift \(2n\) and critical level \(-n\). Boundedness below is essential to the associative unital cochain fusion theorem; arbitrary full duals can fail lower truncation.
hypotheses: Take \(\mathfrak{gl}_n\), \(n\ge2\), with no determinant-one quotient and formal \(\hbar\) of weight \(-1\).
Use torsion-free weightwise-complete lattices with nonnegative underlying weights and finite-dimensional weight spaces. Boundedness below is essential.

claims.statement: The proposed general point-operator formulas extending this restricted RTT construction fail square-zero and left-connection identities already at \(\hbar=0\) and level zero. This excludes those formulas. The associative unital cochain fusion theorem on the stated positive finite-type lattices remains intact, and an independently defined physical boundary-category comparison still requires its own maps.

Use torsion-free weightwise-complete lattices with nonnegative underlying weights and finite-dimensional weight spaces. Boundedness below is essential.

claims.title: Physical boundary recognition and supported sewing
claims.statement: For perturbative four-dimensional Chern–Simons theory with complex \(\mathfrak{gl}_n\) gauge algebra, \(n\ge2\), construct the comparison from independently defined boundary fields to the normalized Yang-double quantum vertex algebra, retaining the formal coupling, central level and completion. Prove that it preserves the vacuum, operator products, line actions and collision operations, and identify the corresponding physical dual and module category. Determine the normalization relating the formal coupling to a numerical affine level wherever such a specialization exists. For four-dimensional Chern–Simons theory with a spectral curve, its meromorphic one-form and a chosen gauge domain, construct cap amplitudes and sewing along a common circle using one compatible cutoff. Transport the regulators, punctured primitive and determinant line through every required boundary face, and prove compatibility with higher edge compositions, junctions, bundles and the divisor of the spectral form.
hypotheses: Take \(\mathfrak{gl}_n\), \(n\ge2\), with no determinant-one quotient and formal \(\hbar\) of weight \(-1\).
Use torsion-free weightwise-complete lattices with nonnegative underlying weights and finite-dimensional weight spaces. Boundedness below is essential.

claims.title: The corrected all-weight local boundary
claims.statement: The corrected relative BRST source for \(T[SU(2)]\) has two symplectic-boson and two fermion pairs; their levels \(-2\) and \(+2\) cancel. The all-weight quartet contraction leaves harmonic cohomology in degree zero and identifies the boundary with the simple \(L_1(\mathfrak{psl}(2|2))\) in the declared categories. Its vacuum Yoneda ring is \(Z=\mathbb C[u,v,w]/(uv-w^2)\), with all three generators of degree two. The ordinary augmentation dual has rank eight over its central polynomial ring \(\mathbb C[\tau]\) and dimensions \(1,3,4,4,\ldots\); it has not been identified with the full boundary co-vacuum algebra.
hypotheses: The corrected relative source has two symplectic-boson and two fermion pairs; levels −2 and +2 cancel.
Give \(Z=\mathbb C[u,v,w]/(uv-w^2)\) degrees \(|u|=|v|=|w|=2\), zero differential and augmentation at the singular point; use ordinary unbounded dg modules and full derived Hom.

claims.title: The graded Clifford-type ordinary dual
claims.statement: Over \(\mathbb C\), give \(Z=\mathbb C[u,v,w]/(uv-w^2)\) cohomological degrees \(|u|=|v|=|w|=2\), zero differential and augmentation at the singular point, and use the ordinary unbounded dg-module category with full derived Hom. Its derived augmentation endomorphism algebra is formal and is \(U(\mathfrak l)\) with zero differential, where \(\mathfrak l\) has generators \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma\) of degree \(-1\), a central generator \(\tau\) of degree \(-2\), brackets \([\alpha,\beta]=-\tau\), \([\gamma,\gamma]=2\tau\), and all other generator brackets zero up to graded skewsymmetry. Every generator is primitive, and \(R\operatorname{Hom}_{U(\mathfrak l)}(\mathbb C,\mathbb C)\simeq Z\) multiplicatively; this duality has no extra spectral parameter.
hypotheses: The corrected relative source has two symplectic-boson and two fermion pairs; levels −2 and +2 cancel.
Give \(Z=\mathbb C[u,v,w]/(uv-w^2)\) degrees \(|u|=|v|=|w|=2\), zero differential and augmentation at the singular point; use ordinary unbounded dg modules and full derived Hom.

claims.title: Negative-current coinvariants fail to preserve the unit
claims.statement: Over \(\mathbb C\), let \(A=L_1(\mathfrak{psl}(2|2))\) be the simple affine boundary algebra with its even \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) factors at levels \(-1,+1\), let \(\mathfrak g=A_1\) be its weight-one current space, and let \(\mathfrak n_-=t^{-1}\mathfrak g[t^{-1}]\) act by the actual negative current modes. In the ordinary algebraic derived category, \(F_-(A)=\mathbb C\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{U(\mathfrak n_-)}A\) has \(H_{0,0}=\mathbb C\) and \(H_{1,2}=\mathbb C^{24\mid24}\), with every other group of conformal weight at most two zero; the indices denote homological degree and conformal weight. Consequently \(F_-\) cannot be strong unital monoidal from a tensor category with unit \(A\) to complexes of vector spaces with their ordinary tensor product.
hypotheses: Use the boundary vacuum of \(L_1(\mathfrak{psl}(2|2))\) and its actual negative current modes in the ordinary algebraic category.
The exchange comparison fixes the specified \(T^*\mathbb P^1\) carrier and permits a scalar factor and same-fibre similarity only.

claims.title: A same-fibre spectral and KZ comparison fails
claims.statement: On the specified \(T^*\mathbb P^1\) carrier, the stable-envelope exchange is \(R(u)=(uI+\hbar P)/(u+\hbar)\). Its antisymmetric-to-symmetric eigenvalue ratio varies with \(u\), while the indicated KZ half-turn ratio is constant. A scalar factor and same-fibre similarity cannot identify these generic families. This excludes that marked comparison, not every parameter correspondence or a different relative/factorization functor. A geometric Hall comparison must keep framing rank distinct from instanton number and compare Hall product with direct-sum coproduct on the same carrier.
hypotheses: Use the boundary vacuum of \(L_1(\mathfrak{psl}(2|2))\) and its actual negative current modes in the ordinary algebraic category.
The exchange comparison fixes the specified \(T^*\mathbb P^1\) carrier and permits a scalar factor and same-fibre similarity only.

claims.title: Conditional sheaf invariants of the torus-fibration family
claims.statement: For the specified \((3,4,\infty)\) torus-fibration family with twists \((0,1,-1)\), assume the analytic construction, gluing, properness/flatness and separate sphere-homology premise. The conditional calculation gives its Hodge, Bott–Chern and Aeppli tables, \(E_1\ne E_2=E_\infty\), exactly four rank-one \(d_1\) maps, and \(\chi(\Omega^p)=(0,-1,1,0)\). The logarithmic extension and direct-image maps compute these invariants within the stated geometry; they do not independently establish a complex structure on \(S^6\). Numerical indices alone do not determine chiral de Rham cohomology.
hypotheses: Assume the analytic construction, gluing, properness/flatness and the separate sphere-homology premise.
The logarithmic extension and direct-image calculations use the specified geometric family; they do not independently establish a complex structure on S⁶.

claims.title: The remaining local and six-sphere comparisons
claims.statement: The ordinary augmentation dual of the graded surface singularity has not been identified with the full boundary co-vacuum algebra. A geometric Hall comparison must retain framing rank separately from instanton number and compare product and direct-sum coproduct on one carrier. For the specified torus-fibration family, the analytic construction, gluing, properness/flatness and sphere-homology premise remain required; its conditional sheaf tables do not prove the underlying geometry. Comparison with the Liu–Rollenske family and actual chiral de Rham cohomology requires the relevant maps, beyond numerical indices.
hypotheses: The corrected relative source has two symplectic-boson and two fermion pairs; levels −2 and +2 cancel.
Give \(Z=\mathbb C[u,v,w]/(uv-w^2)\) degrees \(|u|=|v|=|w|=2\), zero differential and augmentation at the singular point; use ordinary unbounded dg modules and full derived Hom.
Use the boundary vacuum of \(L_1(\mathfrak{psl}(2|2))\) and its actual negative current modes in the ordinary algebraic category.
The exchange comparison fixes the specified \(T^*\mathbb P^1\) carrier and permits a scalar factor and same-fibre similarity only.
Assume the analytic construction, gluing, properness/flatness and the separate sphere-homology premise.
The logarithmic extension and direct-image calculations use the specified geometric family; they do not independently establish a complex structure on S⁶.

claims.title: The precision-three native fields act on all algebraic states
claims.statement: For \(R_3=\mathbb C[\hbar]/(\hbar^3)\), the full native algebraic complex \(M_3=V^{KB}(\mathfrak{gl}_2)\otimes_{R_3}F_0\) carries a dg quantum vertex superalgebra \((d_M,\mathbb Y_-,T,\mathbf1,S_M)\) at every numerical \(K\), including \(0\) and \(-2\). Locality has an exponent depending on the first two inputs and valid for every final state. The opposite \(\mathbb Y_+\) is a weakly associative chain field with the prescribed homotopy \(\delta\mathbb H=\mathbb Y_+-\mathbb Y_-\). Exchange is an invertible chain map homotopic to the identity.
hypotheses: All four colours, trace currents, trace ghosts, ordinary Koszul signs and the full corrected differential remain on the algebraic state carrier.
No separate full opposite quantum vertex structure, higher-precision extension or critical physical evaluation is inferred.

claims.title: Native state cohomology has ordinary local fields
claims.statement: The induced fields on \(H^\bullet(M_3,d_M)\) form an ordinary local vertex superalgebra at every numerical \(K\), with \(R_3\)-bilinear fields and the original faithful central \(R_3\)-action. Both ordered fields induce the same operation. A finite Laurent exchange homotopy makes each exchanged product difference a coefficientwise boundary after one locality power, without a Künneth identification over \(R_3\). Ordinary locality does not force singular products to vanish.
hypotheses: The state carrier is algebraic and the precision is exactly \(R_3\).

The separate fixed-noncritical state frame is retained; the critical invariant ghost-vacuum submodule is not an exhaustion of critical cohomology. No flatness or cohomology/base-change theorem is inferred from locality alone.

claims.title: The specified inflated endpoint lift has a nonzero derived obstruction
claims.statement: Let \(q:A\to A_3\) be the actual nonnegative endomorphism dg fibre product and inflate \(\mathcal N_3[1]\) along \(q\). A closed square-zero trace creator \(c\in\ker q\) kills the source unit class but acts nontrivially on every closed normalized bulk lift. At fixed \(K\ne-2\), the two ordered marked evaluations therefore have the same nonzero class \(\beta_AE_3[1]=\beta_A\overline E_3[1]\) in \(\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A^e)}(\mathcal N_3[1],\mathcal K[1])\). The exterior trace detector splits off a free cyclic \(R_3\)-submodule. The specified map has no derived bimodule lift or standard uncurved \(A_\infty\)-bimodule lift, including after an equivalent source-module resolution.
hypotheses: The original quotient-inflated source action, normalized scalar fibre and actual corner sequence are fixed.

The positive noncritical marked evaluations and scalar homotopy correction remain valid. Changing the action, actor or recipient is a different problem requiring an operation-preserving comparison; no universal physical obstruction is asserted.

claims.title: The nonrational sl3 ideal has sharp derived tensor exponent four
claims.statement: For \(B=Y_{-s}(\mathfrak{sl}_3)\), \(s\notin\mathbb Q\), and \(R=U(\mathfrak{sl}_3)\), the actual positive-weight ideal has fourth derived tensor power zero over \(R\), while its cube is nonzero. Every source has an algebraic filtration with at most four inflated unrestricted \(R\)-complexes, and \(R\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}-\) is conservative.
hypotheses: The split augmentation, K-flatness on both sides and actual two-action ideal are retained, in the stated graded and ungraded conventions.
This is a theorem for this type and nonrational parameter range. It does not infer an exponent for another simple type.

claims.title: Nonrational sl3 induction has its full ordinary unit and exact image
claims.statement: For \(B=Y_{-s}(\mathfrak{sl}_3)\), \(s\notin\mathbb Q\), at raw affine level \(s-3\), the original tensor–Hom unit is invertible on every ordinary unbounded source under the retained native realization hypotheses. Its image is \(\operatorname{Loc}(W)\), or the localizing category generated by all internal shifts of the regular-top \(W\). The original counit is the coreflection onto that image, whose stated generators are relatively compact.
hypotheses: Retain the specified coherent smooth affine–right-\(B\) realization, native resolution, enhanced comparison and actual tensor–Hom maps in each grading convention.
No ambient compactness, equality with the whole smooth category, all-type theorem or rational-parameter extension follows.

claims.title: A common current tail gives completeness and a criterion for cellularity
claims.statement: For positive-current \(\mathfrak n=t\mathfrak{sl}_2[t]\), let \(F:D(\mathcal S)\to D(\mathfrak M)\) be the exact smooth inclusion and \(G=R\operatorname{sm}\). If one \(L\ge1\) satisfies \(\mathfrak n_LH^q(X)=0\) for all \(q\le b\), the original unit \(X\to GF(X)\simeq\operatorname{holim}_n\tau^{\ge-n}X\) is invertible. Every smooth derived source has the actual Hom comparison into \(X\), with all shifts. The lower truncation becomes noncanonically formal after sufficiently deep tail restriction; if the hypothesis holds in every degree, the whole restricted object does. The index \(M=4L-2\) suffices. If every cohomology module is jointly augmentation-torsion, this common-tail hypothesis also places \(X\) in the localizing category generated by the trivial cells. The cellularity assertion holds in the ungraded category as well. In the algebraic grading it suffices for cellularity that \(\mathfrak n_L(H^qX)_{\le a}=0\) for one fixed \(a\) and all \(q\le b\).
hypotheses: The smooth-vector and formality statements use algebraic integer-energy gradings, with currents lowering energy and maps preserving it. Products are formed energy by energy before the outer algebraic direct sum.
Multiplicities, cohomological degrees and energy support are unrestricted. The result asserts no formality over the original algebra and no general left-completeness or idempotence theorem.

claims.title: Unrestricted generation by the positive-current cells
claims.statement: For algebraically graded positive-current \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\), the equality \(\operatorname{Loc}\{\mathbb C\langle e\rangle:e\in\mathbb Z\}\) with the full subcategory of joint augmentation-torsion cohomology remains unresolved. A nonzero torsion-cohomology object in the right orthogonal would be the correctly scoped null witness. Such a witness must escape every common annihilating tail in arbitrarily low cohomological degrees. In the graded category this holds even after restricting those cohomology modules to any fixed lower energy half-line \(e\le a\).
hypotheses: The category is the actual smooth positive-current category, distinct from native affine induction and the intrinsic torsion adjunction.

Torsion-term complexes, bounded-below torsion-cohomology objects and the stated common lower energy-bounded class are already cellular. Completion failure, non-full-faithfulness of the torsion inclusion and a failed sufficient test are not noncellularity witnesses.

claims.title: The genuine Heisenberg comparison reduces to a zero sector and automorphisms
claims.statement: For \(H=V_\kappa\), \(\kappa\ne0\), and \(B=\Lambda(\epsilon_1)\), the actual tuple map \(\Pi:F\to\mathbb C^2_{\mathrm{disc}}\times K(\mathbb C,1)\) has weak-equivalence composite with the original actor-roof map \(q_B\). Actual translations give \(F\simeq\mathbb C^2_{\mathrm{disc}}\times F^0\). In the genuine pointed slice \(\mathcal V_{H//H}\), let \(U\) be the automorphisms of \(X_1=H\oplus\epsilon_1H\) inducing the identity on state cohomology. The connected scalar-detector fibre \(\Phi\) on the trivial-action component satisfies \(U\simeq\Omega\Phi\). Hence \(q_B\) is an equivalence exactly when the whole \(F^0\) is connected and \(U\) is contractible.
hypotheses: Ordinary algebraic dg vertex localization at state quasi-isomorphisms; both original roof legs, every admissible boundary arrow and the full unit path remain.
Both under- and over-\(H\) homotopy data are retained. Splittings are of spaces over the scalar set: endomorphism composition multiplies scalars, whereas loop concatenation adds them.

claims.title: Connectivity and invisible genuine automorphisms remain to be determined
claims.statement: The genuine Heisenberg actor map \(q_B\) remains open after its exact reduction. The two residual requirements are connectedness of the entire charge/constant zero sector \(F^0\), and contractibility of the genuine pointed automorphism space \(U\) acting trivially on state cohomology. Based loop calculations concern only the trivial-action component and cannot exclude other zero-sector components. The computed ordinary exterior-source spaces and the actual tuple composite do not by themselves identify the whole recipient.
hypotheses: Keep the original full actor-roof source and genuine unit fibre at nonzero Heisenberg level.
A plain over-\(H\) slice is a different mapping problem. Nonstability of the pointed slice does not prove that \(U\) is noncontractible.

claims.title: The full three-pole evaluation factors through the rational inner pair
claims.statement: At nonrational \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) parameter, the full rational-current resolution has a normalized tensorator \(\Delta^{(12|3)}:P_c^{(3)}\to(P_c^{(12)}\otimes_{\mathbb C}P)((q))\), retaining the inner rational pole and satisfying \((\Delta^{(12)}\otimes1)\Delta^{(12|3)}=\Delta^{(3)}\) on the whole source. The actual direct-sum bar roof gives a full-source derived evaluation into the original binary target for ordinary unbounded constant inputs. Restriction recovers the old affine evaluation.
hypotheses: The inner scalar field is \(\mathbb C((p))\), the outer field is \(\mathbb C((p))((q))\), and the right-twisted kernel differential, incoming rational action and outgoing translated line action are retained.

The affine-to-rational target comparison is a quasi-isomorphism in the original two-pole current category. No new strict three-pole action on the literal old target, invertibility of the further evaluation \(\Theta\), or reversal of Laurent order follows.

claims.title: Finite-total spectators reach the independently factorized endpoint
claims.statement: For a constant input \(T=T_{12}\otimes M_3\), retain the joint object \(E=S_w^{12}(T)\), the separately factorized object \(E_1=S_w(T_{12})\otimes M_3\), and their actual map \(c:E_1\to E\). If \(H^\bullet(M_3)\) has finite total dimension, \(c\) is a quasi-isomorphism. Under the native realization hypotheses, the complete three-pole evaluation then agrees at the independently factorized endpoint, preserving the original affine restriction and outgoing unit. The first pair may be correlated and unbounded. Fixed left combs admit stagewise comparisons when every subsequently attached spectator satisfies the same finite-total condition.
hypotheses: Retain the specified coherent ordinary smooth affine–right-line realization, tensor–Hom adjunction, full original unit, restricted cofree model and common-cutoff actions, the native bimodule-functorial derived ideal triangle, and the bounded-below positive-current torsion theorem.

Finite dimension in each cohomological degree is insufficient. The native application is proved for the specified joint, refined-bar and factorized intermediates, not every arbitrary module over the cluster/third-slot algebra.
Strict squares belong to the algebraic bar models; native smooth replacement keeps the enhanced comparison with its specified coherences.

claims.title: Native regular intermediates and integral tree comparison
claims.statement: Full regular-current evaluations exist on the three- and four-point algebraic factorized intersections with independently resolved bars, retaining finite spectator span across each inner series. Native regular-intermediate representability, proper integral ternary composition before projection, both occupied unit maps and mixed change-of-tree coherence require further maps. The unprojected regular slot can carry a simple pole. The rank of the joint/factorized defect can be nonzero even on an inflated regular spectator.
hypotheses: Work with \(\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{sl}_2\), \(k\in\mathbb C\setminus\mathbb Q\), and constant ordinary unbounded input complexes over \(\mathbb C\). Tensor totalization is algebraic by direct sums before each degreewise Laurent completion.

Native recipient conclusions retain the coherent ordinary smooth affine–right-line realization, tensor–Hom adjunction and full original unit, restricted cofree model and common-cutoff actions, the native bimodule-functorial derived ideal triangle, and the bounded-below positive-current torsion theorem.

Factorized incoming actions are factorwise or separately support-preserving. Fixed-word coefficient identities, spectral vectors and first action homotopies do not supply the adapted full-current evaluation or all higher coherence.

The full-complex decoupling problem retains the specified continuous endomorphism complex, normalized map, inverse and action homotopies. A finite Wilson matrix gauge, cycle map or zigzag does not solve it.

The native parameter comparison must be natural over polynomial forms, preserve literal facets and both units, and supply mixed interchange/associativity for arbitrary trees. Any stronger derived fusion identification also needs its intertwining Jacobi and grading/completion theorem.

claims.title: The original coefficient heat has a finite part and a based local line
claims.statement: On the original reflected fixed-adjoint weighted coefficient realization, the small-source heat supertrace has its stated local expansion and vanishing constant logarithmic term. The original subtraction gives a numerical finite part \(W_{\mathrm{fp}}\), with its controlled source derivatives. Finite original spectral-shell action integrals and the complementary finite part give a nonzero based local vacuum-line section with an actual finite action anchor. The covariant source connection retains the positive counterterm sign.
hypotheses: Smooth reflected sources are sufficiently small in the stated \(C^4\)/\(C^1\) norms, with the required bounded higher seminorms and a common right-half-plane gap.

Action and line assertions additionally use integrability and a supplied smooth Ward filling. This is local renormalized coefficient heat, not a bare infinite determinant, a global holonomy theorem, or a physical spatial-cut comparison.

claims.title: Original heat finite parts have a relative positive-level formula
claims.statement: On the square-zero reflected Ward family, put \(x=|\kappa|^2\) and scale the level and filling together. A common gapped realization on \([a,b]\subset(0,\infty)\), the positive-cutoff variation identity, continuous \(x\)-differentiability and a uniform inserted expansion in one fixed finite power/logarithm scale give \(c_F(v,x)=\operatorname{FP}_{\epsilon\downarrow0}\operatorname{Str}_X(P_Fe^{-\epsilon A_x})=\tfrac12R_2[JP_F](v,x)\) and \(W_{\mathrm{fp}}(v,x_1)-W_{\mathrm{fp}}(v,x_0)=\int_{x_0}^{x_1}c_F(v,x)\,dx/x\). If the inserted coefficients are continuous in \(x\), then \(x\partial_xW_{\mathrm{fp}}=c_F\). Absence of an inserted constant logarithm makes \(C(v,x)\) constant in \(x\); the original Mellin relation remains \(W_{\mathrm{fp}}=-Z'(0)+\gamma_EC\).
hypotheses: The uniform expansion includes the claimed source derivatives and a decaying remainder. These hypotheses are additional analytic input, not a consequence of compactness.
The reflected coefficient \(R_2\) already includes the normal-reflection factor. Neither \(C\) nor \(c_F\) is asserted zero; the absolute Euler term is retained.

claims.title: The positive-level formula leaves zero-level heat control open
claims.statement: The positive-interval level comparison has a remainder estimate containing \(\log(b/a)\) and gives no estimate at \(x=0\). A passage through zero must supply an integrable endpoint estimate for the inserted finite part and compatible heat control there. A reference amplitude, global line holonomy and an independently normalized geometric cap remain additional data.
hypotheses: The established formula is on a compact interval strictly inside \((0,\infty)\), with its common gapped realization and fixed uniform asymptotic scale.
No zero-endpoint result follows by formally putting \(x_0=0\) in the integral.

claims.title: The local line and numerical state combine on a common based family
claims.statement: On a based reflected Ward family small enough for both constructions, the actual line-valued functional \(\mathcal Z_u(F)=s_{\mathrm{fp}}(u)\omega_u(F)\) is continuous and satisfies the fixed-source Ward identity. It retains the finite action anchor of the local line and the independently constructed covariance of the normalized numerical Gaussian. Identification with a state prepared by the geometric cap requires the original uncut-to-cut field map, amplitude-line comparison and transport of observables through spatial sewing.
hypotheses: The numerical Gaussian and original local coefficient-line constructions must both be defined on the same specified based reflected Ward family.
Finite spectral-shell Fubini is not spatial-cut sewing. No infinite bare phase, global cap equality or arbitrary-source extension is asserted.

claims.title: Retained kernels give continuous rooted evaluations at every level
claims.statement: Through \(R_3=\mathbb C[\hbar]/(\hbar^3)\), put \(V=M_3^0\) and \(F_L=\mathcal G/\widehat I_L\), where \(\mathcal G\) is the completed ghost algebra and \(\widehat I_L\) its closed left ideal generated by modes of index at least \(L\). The retained kernel space \(\mathcal E^n_{\rm ret}\), for \(n\ge0\), consists of compatible \(R_3\)-linear maps \(T_L:V\to(V\otimes F_L^n)((u))\), with Laurent floor allowed to depend on \(L,w\); set \(\mathcal E^n_{\rm ret}=0\) for \(n<0\). Retained cochains have degree components \(\mathcal Q^{\mathrm{ret},j}=\prod_{p\ge0}\operatorname{Hom}_{R_3}(M_3^p,\mathcal E^{p+j}_{\rm ret})\). The dressed native field gives a cocycle \(\mathcal Y_-\in\mathcal Q^{\mathrm{ret},0}\). The combined current–ghost differential squares to zero; write \(\delta\) for its induced Hom differential. Let \(\Lambda^V\) be the restriction of the degree-minus-one exchange homotopy to \(M_3\otimes(V\otimes1)\), identifying the second factor with \(V\). Set \(\mathfrak h^\Lambda(x)(w)=\mathcal Y_-^\otimes(\Lambda^V(x\otimes w))\), where \(\mathcal Y_-^\otimes(x'\otimes w')=\mathcal Y_-(x')(w')\). Then \(\mathcal Y^\sharp=\mathcal Y_-+\delta\mathfrak h^\Lambda\) is a retained cocycle. The coefficient pairing below defines continuous dg current-bimodule maps \(E^\flat,E^\sharp:N_{\rm rt}\to Q_3\), with scalars \(W_-,W_+\), both endpoint actions and both translation laws. They are joined on the entire ordered rooted carrier by \(H(y)=(-1)^{n+1}y\cap\mathfrak h^\Lambda\) in middle degree \(n\). The result holds at every numerical \(K\), including \(0\) and \(-2\).
hypotheses: The corrected current modes are \(\widehat J_\alpha(m)\), where \(\alpha\) ranges over all four \(\mathfrak{gl}_2\) colours and \(m\in\mathbb Z\); the ghost modes are \(c^\alpha_n\), \(n\in\mathbb Z\), and \(*=\ast'_K\) is the completed ghost product. The left coupling is \(Q(w\otimes g)=\sum_\alpha\sum_{m\in\mathbb Z}\widehat J_\alpha(m)w\otimes c^\alpha_{-m-1}*g\). For \(T\in\mathcal E^n_{\rm ret}\), \(\mathscr DT=DT+QT-(-1)^nTQ\), with \(D\) the ghost derivation on the output, \((QT)(w)=Q(T(w))\), and \((TQ)(w)=\sum_\alpha\sum_{m\in\mathbb Z}T(\widehat J_\alpha(m)w)*c^\alpha_{-m-1}\). For \(\Psi\in\mathcal Q^{\mathrm{ret},j}\), \(\delta\Psi=\mathscr D\Psi-(-1)^j\Psi d_M\).

For the full smooth current algebra \(A\) and its right quotients \(A_R\), the source is \(N_{\rm rt}^{1-n}=\varprojlim_R\operatorname*{colim}_{L\ge1}(\operatorname{Hom}_{R_3}(F_L^n,A)\otimes_{R_3,\mathrm{alg}}A_R)\). Its coefficients are \(u\)-independent, with one middle ghost cutoff and finite right PBW support at each right quotient; no uniform cutoff over all right quotients is imposed. The recipient is \(Q_3=\operatorname{Hom}_{R_3}(M_3,\operatorname{Hom}_{R_3}(V,V((u))))[-1]\), with pointwise Laurent topology in the algebraic inputs.

At a right quotient adapted to \(w\), write \(y=\sum_iF_i\otimes b_i\), with \(F_i:F_L^n\to A\) and \(b_i\in A_R\), using one common \(L\). For \(\Psi\in\mathcal Q^{\mathrm{ret},j}\) and \(x\in M_3^{n-j}\), the coefficient pairing is \((y\cap\Psi)(x)(w)=\sum_{i,t,\gamma}u^tF_i(\gamma)[u^t][\gamma]\Psi(x)_L(b_iw)\). Here \(t\in\mathbb Z\), \(\gamma\) ranges over the ghost-monomial basis of \(F_L^n\), and the coefficient \(F_i(\gamma)\) acts on the output after Laurent and ghost coefficient extraction. The retained homogeneity bounds supply the finite ghost box and Laurent floor on each fixed input.

Ghost multiplication and differentiation are evaluated at sufficiently enlarged upper-mode cutoffs before projection. The quotient-family differential is curved and is not an honest dg differential on each \(V\otimes F_L\); square zero belongs to the retained kernel differential.

Keep all four colours, trace factors and order-two corrections. The restricted whole-series marked comparison also requires noncritical level and prescribed positive-inserted maps. At critical level these formulas already give the ordered rooted maps.

claims.title: A noncritical retained homotopy aligns the scalar and first roots
claims.statement: At fixed \(K\ne-2\), including \(K=0\), use the retained kernel spaces \(\mathcal E^n_{\rm ret}\), with \(\mathcal E^n_{\rm ret}=0\) for \(n<0\). A degree-\(j\) retained cochain lies in \(\mathcal Q^{\mathrm{ret},j}=\prod_{p\ge0}\operatorname{Hom}_{R_3}(M_3^p,\mathcal E^{p+j}_{\rm ret})\): it sends each inserted state to a kernel on current inputs. Let \(E_3\) be the prescribed pure-root evaluation, with retained cochain \(\Phi\in\mathcal Q^{\mathrm{ret},0}\), and let \(\Delta=\Phi-\mathcal Y^\sharp\). Write \(\Delta_1=\Delta|_{M_3^1}\). For the translation-compatible state contraction \(k\) retaining the full trace factor, set \(\kappa^{(1)}|_{M_3^2}=\Delta_1k\) and set its other inserted-degree components to zero. This cochain has zero scalar pairing, homogeneity and both translations. The cocycle \(\mathcal Y^{\sharp,1}=\mathcal Y^\sharp+\delta\kappa^{(1)}\) agrees with \(\Phi\) on inserted ghost degrees zero and one. Its continuous bimodule evaluation agrees with \(E_3\) on the subcomplex of middle degrees at most one and is globally homotopic to \(E^\sharp\) on \(N_{\rm rt}\).
hypotheses: The exact ordered rooted carrier has \(u\)-independent source coefficients. The contraction and comparison are at a fixed noncritical numerical level through \(R_3\).
The first-root correction may change inserted degree two. Its scalar normalization does not impose strict creation or an order-two onset.
The all-degree construction uses the two full seed identities. Its extension to the marked whole series keeps the prescribed positive-inserted maps.

claims.title: Trace classes obstruct lifts when the source has no first cohomology
claims.statement: At every numerical level through \(R_3\), put \(F^1M_3=M_3^{\ge1}\). Let \(\mathcal B\) be the subcomplex of two-input Laurent cochains \(\operatorname{Hom}_{R_3}(M_3\otimes M_3,M_3((u)))\) satisfying \(G(M_3\otimes F^1M_3)\subset(F^1M_3)((u))\). Its subcomplex \(\mathcal K\) consists of cochains whose every output lies in \((F^1M_3)((u))\). The corner map \(\pi:\mathcal B\to\mathcal C=\operatorname{Hom}_{R_3}(M_3\otimes V,V((u)))\), with \(V=M_3^0\), restricts the rooted second input to ghost degree zero and projects the output to ghost degree zero; its kernel is \(\mathcal K\). For a closed \(G\in\mathcal B^0\) with \([\pi G]=[W_\pm]\), multiplication of its output by exterior trace monomials gives a split copy of \(\Lambda_{R_3}(\xi^I_0,\xi^I_1,\ldots)\) in \(H^\bullet(\mathcal B)\); its positive-degree part splits into \(H^\bullet(\mathcal K)\). Suppose a dg algebra acts on this corner exact sequence and contains a closed degree-one element acting on \(\mathcal B\) by output multiplication by a trace ghost. If a dg module map \(S\to\mathcal C\) sends a closed degree-zero element to the normalized scalar class \([W_\pm]\) and \(H^1(S)=0\), it has no lift to \(\mathcal B\) in the derived module category or as a standard uncurved \(A_\infty\)-module map. The same statement applies to bimodules and equivalent module diagrams.
hypotheses: The splitting is of graded \(R_3\)-modules; no multiplication on these Hom cohomology groups is asserted.
The closed output trace-creator action, dg corner diagram and normalized source class are essential. For the prescribed marked evaluations the level remains \(K\ne-2\).
The obstruction does not exclude the retained-kernel coefficient pairing, a differently typed physical comparison or a relative cone whose cohomology has changed.

claims.title: The field homotopy does not descend through both ghost-truncated inputs
claims.statement: Write \(F^pM_3=M_3^{\ge p}\). At every numerical level through \(R_3\), neither the exchange homotopy \(\Lambda\) nor \(\mathbb H=\mathbb Y_-\Lambda\) descends through both inputs to \(M_3/F^pM_3\), for any \(p\ge1\). Put \(\theta_p=\xi^I_0\cdots\xi^I_{p-2}\), with \(\theta_1=1\). The inserted Cartan-ghost state \(h_0\theta_p\) vanishes in the quotient, but its homotopy with the current state \(E_1\) has nonzero coefficient \(\hbar u^{-1}E_1\otimes\theta_p\) of ghost degree \(p-1\).
