hypotheses: The fields and their exchange do descend to these quotients. The negative statement concerns the specified degree-minus-one homotopies through both quotient inputs.
Projection in the rooted argument and output remains valid when the full inserted complex is retained. The witness uses all trace ghosts and applies also at \(K=0,-2\).

claims.title: The constrained higher retained class vanishes at noncritical level
claims.statement: Over \(R_3\) at \(K\ne-2\) let \(\mathscr C\) impose homogeneity, both translations and zero scalar pairing. The class \([\Phi-\mathcal Y^{\sharp,1}]\) vanishes in \(H^0(\mathscr C)\) in every inserted degree. Subtracting the first-root primitive from \(\kappa=(\Phi-\mathcal Y^\sharp)k-h^\Lambda ip\) gives a primitive for the already aligned representative. The choices modulo boundaries form a torsor under \(H^{-1}(\mathscr C)\).
hypotheses: Keep the full trace-current polynomial and trace-ghost exterior factor in the noncritical retract. The two explicit nontrace seed identities and their spectator extensions are needed.
The marked continuation keeps the prescribed positive-inserted operations. Its independent physical derivation and the three proper unit comparisons remain open.

claims.title: Cluster-infinity expansion reaches a Taylor-completed resolution
claims.statement: Let \(P\) be the affine Chevalley resolution, \(\mathfrak n_N=t^N\mathfrak g[t]\), and \(F_NP\) the subcomplex generated by coefficient vectors in the left ideal \(\mathcal A\mathfrak n_N\) and exterior factors in \(\mathfrak n_N\). Over \(K_w=\mathbb C((w^{-1}))\), put \(\widehat P_{K_w}=\varprojlim_N\bigl((P/F_NP)\otimes K_w\bigr)\). Expansion at cluster infinity gives a quasi-isomorphism \(e_\infty:P_c^{(12)}\to\widehat P_{K_w}\) from the rational two-pole resolution, compatible with the rational-current and right-line actions. Composing the outer rational tensorator with \(e_\infty\) gives a full three-pole evaluation into the corresponding Taylor-completed bar target.
hypotheses: Work with \(\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{sl}_2\), \(k\in\mathbb C\setminus\mathbb Q\), and constant ordinary unbounded input complexes over \(\mathbb C\). Tensor totalization is algebraic by direct sums before each degreewise Laurent completion.
The completion uses the actual positive-mode subcomplexes and their quotient tower. The Taylor formulas are finite at each cutoff; individual quotients are not thereby declared right-line modules.
The target is the specified positive-mode completion, not the literal affine resolution. A continuous extension of the affine inner evaluation through this completion does not follow.

claims.title: The affine retraction and Taylor-evaluation routes have precise obstructions
claims.statement: For the rational cluster and full three-pole resolutions, there is no normalized map to the corresponding finite affine or two-pole resolution that commutes with all right ghost operators. An extra-pole exterior generator has infinitely many nonzero ghost contractions. The affine inner tensorator also has no continuous extension along the cluster-infinity completion in the specified coefficient topology: at pole order \(r\ge1\), a fixed output coefficient of its Taylor partial sums is \(\binom{r+H}{H}\), which does not converge as the cutoff \(H\) grows.
hypotheses: Work with \(\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{sl}_2\), \(k\in\mathbb C\setminus\mathbb Q\), and constant ordinary unbounded input complexes over \(\mathbb C\). Tensor totalization is algebraic by direct sums before each degreewise Laurent completion.

The retraction statement concerns the named scalar-linear resolution maps with \(1\mapsto1\); the nonextension statement retains the separated topology in which the displayed coefficient is continuous.

The complete rational-cluster evaluation remains valid. An affine-linear contraction and its first action homotopy do not supply a typed full twisted-bar evaluation lift or its higher coherences. These results do not exclude other native fusion comparisons.

claims.title: The actual pair-first operation has an algebraic common domain
claims.statement: Put \(p=w^{-1}\), \(q=z^{-1}=sp\), \(\mathcal O=\mathbb C[s]_{(s)}\), \(D=\mathcal O((p))[s^{-1}]\), \(K_R=\mathbb C(s)((p))\) and \(K_N=\mathbb C((p))((s))\). For \(T=T_{12}\otimes M_3\), use \(L_D=(T\otimes\mathcal O)((p))[s^{-1}]\), \(L_R=(T\otimes\mathbb C(s))((p))\), \(L_N=T((p))((s))\), and \(N_1=(T_{12}((p))\otimes M_3)((s))\), all with \(d_T+\rho(r_{12}(w)+r_{13}(z+w)+r_{23}(z))\). The coefficient-array intersection \(L_D^{\mathrm{fac}}=L_D\cap N_1=L_R\cap N_1\) is a dg \(Y_D\)-module and gives the actual span \(L_R\leftarrow L_D^{\mathrm{fac}}\to N_1\), including for regular inputs. Degree by degree, each outer \(s^j\)-coefficient has finite spectator support across its whole inner \(p\)-series. The domain is stable under the outgoing action, factorwise or separately support-preserving incoming actions, and the logarithmic spectral connection. It preserves quasi-isomorphisms in each input.
hypotheses: Work with \(\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{sl}_2\), \(k\in\mathbb C\setminus\mathbb Q\), and constant ordinary unbounded input complexes over \(\mathbb C\). Tensor totalization is algebraic by direct sums before each degreewise Laurent completion.
The finite spectator subspace may depend on the outer coefficient. A joint commuting endomorphism can destroy this support condition; no invariance under every such endomorphism is claimed.

The middle term is a factorized intersection, preserving finite spectator support. Two independently adapted incoming bars give the three-pole current evaluation there. Native outer continuity and representability remain additional requirements.

claims.title: Finite total spectator cohomology identifies the common-domain inclusion
claims.statement: Put \(p=w^{-1}\), \(q=z^{-1}=sp\), \(\mathcal O=\mathbb C[s]_{(s)}\), \(D=\mathcal O((p))[s^{-1}]\), \(K_R=\mathbb C(s)((p))\) and \(K_N=\mathbb C((p))((s))\). For \(T=T_{12}\otimes M_3\), use \(L_D=(T\otimes\mathcal O)((p))[s^{-1}]\), \(L_R=(T\otimes\mathbb C(s))((p))\), \(L_N=T((p))((s))\), and \(N_1=(T_{12}((p))\otimes M_3)((s))\), all with \(d_T+\rho(r_{12}(w)+r_{13}(z+w)+r_{23}(z))\). Let \(L_D^{\mathrm{fac}}=L_D\cap N_1\). If \(H^\bullet(M_3)\) has finite total dimension, the original inclusion \(L_D^{\mathrm{fac}}\to L_D\) is a quasi-isomorphism. Together with \(N_1\to L_N\), it identifies the two raw cones of \(L_R\leftarrow L_D^{\mathrm{fac}}\to N_1\) with the corresponding joint-domain cones. For trivial input these are \(K_R/D\) and \(K_N/D\), so they do not vanish merely from finite-total cohomology.
hypotheses: Work with \(\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{sl}_2\), \(k\in\mathbb C\setminus\mathbb Q\), and constant ordinary unbounded input complexes over \(\mathbb C\). Tensor totalization is algebraic by direct sums before each degreewise Laurent completion.
The first pair is arbitrary and may be correlated and unbounded. Finite dimension in each cohomological degree is insufficient.

The proof contracts the underlying spectator complex and perturbs by the cross terms, positive in both variables. No dg line action on the auxiliary cohomology space is asserted; the canonical inclusion supplies the line-linear map.

Native recipient conclusions retain the coherent ordinary smooth affine–right-line realization, tensor–Hom adjunction and full original unit, restricted cofree model and common-cutoff actions, the native bimodule-functorial derived ideal triangle, and the bounded-below positive-current torsion theorem.

claims.title: Two completed pairs have factorized, symmetric and ordered carriers
claims.statement: For positions \((z+w_1,z,w_2,0)\), put \(p_i=w_i^{-1}\), \(q=z^{-1}\), \(\Lambda_{\mathrm{fac}}=\mathbb C((p_1))\otimes\mathbb C((p_2))\), \(\Lambda_{\mathrm{sym}}=\mathbb C[[p_1,p_2]][(p_1p_2)^{-1}]\), \(F_{12}=\mathbb C((p_1))((p_2))\) and \(F_{21}=\mathbb C((p_2))((p_1))\). For \(T=T_{12}\otimes T_{34}\), define \(E_{\mathrm{fac}}=S_{w_1}(T_{12})\otimes S_{w_2}(T_{34})\) and \(N_{\mathrm{fac}}=S_z^{\Lambda_{\mathrm{fac}}}(E_{\mathrm{fac}})\), with carrier \(E_{\mathrm{fac}}((q))\). The ordered objects \(N^{12},N^{21}\) have carriers \(T((p_1))((p_2))((q))\) and \(T((p_2))((p_1))((q))\), with the same four-point spectral differential. Their array intersection is \(N_{\mathrm{sym}}=(T[[p_1,p_2]][(p_1p_2)^{-1}])((q))\). The two images of \(N_{\mathrm{fac}}\) have identical coefficients in this symmetric carrier.
hypotheses: Work with \(\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{sl}_2\), \(k\in\mathbb C\setminus\mathbb Q\), and constant ordinary unbounded input complexes over \(\mathbb C\). Tensor totalization is algebraic by direct sums before each degreewise Laurent completion.
The factorized carrier uses the two independently completed inner factors. Its incoming actions are factorwise or otherwise proved to preserve finite separated tensor rank.

There is no homomorphism between the two ordered fields fixing both \(p_1,p_2\). This does not deny common overfields. Independent outer binary recipients on full ambient tests belong to the named fields; no ambient recipient theorem over \(\Lambda_{\mathrm{fac}}\) or \(\Lambda_{\mathrm{sym}}\) follows.
Strict coefficient agreement is not a full native bar-interchange theorem for arbitrary trees.

claims.title: Finite total pair cohomology gives the canonical ordered-field comparisons
claims.statement: For positions \((z+w_1,z,w_2,0)\), put \(p_i=w_i^{-1}\), \(q=z^{-1}\), \(\Lambda_{\mathrm{fac}}=\mathbb C((p_1))\otimes\mathbb C((p_2))\), \(\Lambda_{\mathrm{sym}}=\mathbb C[[p_1,p_2]][(p_1p_2)^{-1}]\), \(F_{12}=\mathbb C((p_1))((p_2))\) and \(F_{21}=\mathbb C((p_2))((p_1))\). Let \(E_{\mathrm{fac}}=S_{w_1}(T_{12})\otimes S_{w_2}(T_{34})\), \(N_{\mathrm{fac}}=S_z^{\Lambda_{\mathrm{fac}}}(E_{\mathrm{fac}})\), and let \(E^F,N^F\) denote the inner and outer objects with order \(F=F_{12}\) or \(F_{21}\). If both \(H^\bullet(T_{12})\) and \(H^\bullet(T_{34})\) have finite total dimension, the canonical maps \(E_{\mathrm{fac}}\otimes_{\Lambda_{\mathrm{fac}}}F\to E^F\) and \(N_{\mathrm{fac}}\otimes_{\Lambda_{\mathrm{fac}}((q))}F((q))\to S_z^F(E_{\mathrm{fac}}\otimes_{\Lambda_{\mathrm{fac}}}F)\to N^F\) are quasi-isomorphisms. Under the native hypotheses they preserve the independent binary recipients, original evaluations and units on all smooth tests over \(F((q))\) with jointly locally nilpotent positive-current cohomology, using the ambient derived maps.
hypotheses: Work with \(\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{sl}_2\), \(k\in\mathbb C\setminus\mathbb Q\), and constant ordinary unbounded input complexes over \(\mathbb C\). Tensor totalization is algebraic by direct sums before each degreewise Laurent completion.

Native recipient conclusions retain the coherent ordinary smooth affine–right-line realization, tensor–Hom adjunction and full original unit, restricted cofree model and common-cutoff actions, the native bimodule-functorial derived ideal triangle, and the bounded-below positive-current torsion theorem.
The canonical algebraic maps are quasi-isomorphisms under finite total underlying cohomology. The auxiliary contractions are only complex-linear; no line-module structure on cohomology is needed.
The unextended scalar legs are different maps and need not be equivalences. The theorem neither identifies the two ordered fields nor extends to arbitrary infinite pair inputs.

claims.title: The full four-pole evaluation factors through two rational clusters
claims.statement: Put \(p_i=w_i^{-1}\), \(q=z^{-1}\), \(\Lambda=\mathbb C((p_1))\otimes\mathbb C((p_2))\) and \(B=\Lambda((q))\). Let \(P_{c,B}^{(4)}\) resolve the four-pole rational-current algebra over \(B\), and let \(P_c^{(12)},P_c^{(34)}\) be the two rational cluster resolutions over their inner fields. The normalized tensorator \(\Delta^{12|34}:P_{c,B}^{(4)}\to(P_c^{(12)}\otimes_{\mathbb C}P_c^{(34)})((q))\) is a chain map with the specified current and right-line actions. The two inner tensorators commute, their composite is the full four-point tensorator, and the corresponding algebraic bar evaluations factor accordingly.
hypotheses: Work with \(\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{sl}_2\), \(k\in\mathbb C\setminus\mathbb Q\), and constant ordinary unbounded input complexes over \(\mathbb C\). Tensor totalization is algebraic by direct sums before each degreewise Laurent completion.

For bars over \((Y\otimes Y)_{\Lambda^{\prime}}\), extend the head to \((P_c^{(12)}\otimes P_c^{(34)})\otimes_\Lambda\Lambda^{\prime}\). Retain the canonical map to the completed target, without an assertion of injectivity after arbitrary nonflat scalar extension.

The unchanged-copy normalization concerns exterior resolving generators. Coefficient currents have cross Taylor tails. Polynomial bounds are for unreduced word expressions; PBW reordering can introduce inverse differences.

The identities are defined on the rational-position ring and its stated coefficient extensions. The adapted full-current evaluation on the split intersection uses two independently resolved input pairs. Ambient ring-test recipients require a derived test domain.

claims.title: The factorized conic intersection needs a smaller scalar ring
claims.statement: For positions \((z+w_1,z,w_2,0)\), put \(p_i=w_i^{-1}\), \(q=z^{-1}\), \(\Lambda_{\mathrm{fac}}=\mathbb C((p_1))\otimes\mathbb C((p_2))\), \(\Lambda_{\mathrm{sym}}=\mathbb C[[p_1,p_2]][(p_1p_2)^{-1}]\), \(F_{12}=\mathbb C((p_1))((p_2))\) and \(F_{21}=\mathbb C((p_2))((p_1))\). Put \(s_i=q/p_i\), \(\mathcal O_2=\mathbb C[s_1,s_2]_{(s_1,s_2)}\), \(\mathfrak q=s_1^{-1}\mathcal O_2+s_2^{-1}\mathcal O_2\) and \(D_{\mathrm{con}}=\bigcup_{c\ge0}\{\sum_{n\ge-c}q^n\theta_n:\theta_n\in\mathfrak q^{n+c}\}\). Its symmetric expansion lies in \(\Lambda_{\mathrm{sym}}((q))\). Define \(D_*=D_{\mathrm{con}}\cap\Lambda_{\mathrm{fac}}((q))\) there. For \(T=T_{12}\otimes T_{34}\), let \(L_{D_{\mathrm{con}}}(T)\) have the same support condition with \(T\)-valued coefficients and the four-point spectral differential, and let \(N_{\mathrm{fac}}=(S_{w_1}(T_{12})\otimes S_{w_2}(T_{34}))((q))\) with its outer spectral differential. Then \(L_*^{\mathrm{fac}}=L_{D_{\mathrm{con}}}(T)\cap N_{\mathrm{fac}}\) is a dg \(Y_{D_*}\)-module giving an algebraic radial/factorized span. It is generally not a \(D_{\mathrm{con}}\)-module.
hypotheses: Work with \(\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{sl}_2\), \(k\in\mathbb C\setminus\mathbb Q\), and constant ordinary unbounded input complexes over \(\mathbb C\). Tensor totalization is algebraic by direct sums before each degreewise Laurent completion.

At each outer coefficient, the factorized condition is finite algebraic tensor rank in the two completed cluster factors. The conic scalar with expansion \(\sum_{n\ge0}p_1^np_2^n\) has infinite separated rank and does not preserve that target.
Fixed outgoing words have coefficients in the common finite rational-position ring contained in \(D_*\); incoming actions are factorwise or separately support-preserving.

Use \(D_*\) and incoming actions that are factorwise or separately preserve finite support. Independent resolutions give a full current evaluation on this factorized intersection. Native outer continuity, a maximal coefficient ring and arbitrary ambient derived tests have different requirements.

claims.title: A normalized occupied vacuum can be deleted in every slot
claims.statement: Put \(p=w^{-1}\), \(q=z^{-1}=sp\), \(\mathcal O=\mathbb C[s]_{(s)}\), \(D=\mathcal O((p))[s^{-1}]\), \(K_R=\mathbb C(s)((p))\) and \(K_N=\mathbb C((p))((s))\). Place the normalized trivial or resolved-vacuum input in any one of the three slots. Restrict proper-current functionals to wedges without that block and apply its normalized cofree energy-zero covector. This actual map to the two-point current complex at the surviving positions is a quasi-isomorphism on all smooth tests with jointly locally nilpotent positive-current cohomology over \(K_R,K_N\), and on constant tests from the same ground-field category over \(D\), with arbitrary ordinary unbounded surviving inputs. It preserves the original two-point evaluation. Deleting slot three leaves positions \((z+w,z)\) with outgoing action \(\Delta_w\circ\tau_z\).
hypotheses: Work with \(\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{sl}_2\), \(k\in\mathbb C\setminus\mathbb Q\), and constant ordinary unbounded input complexes over \(\mathbb C\). Tensor totalization is algebraic by direct sums before each degreewise Laurent completion.

Native recipient conclusions retain the coherent ordinary smooth affine–right-line realization, tensor–Hom adjunction and full original unit, restricted cofree model and common-cutoff actions, the native bimodule-functorial derived ideal triangle, and the bounded-below positive-current torsion theorem.

The ambient test category consists of smooth derived objects with jointly locally nilpotent positive-current cohomology. The common-ring statement uses constant ground-field tests, not ordinary Hom on arbitrary \(D\)-defined representatives.
The deleted input is the normalized vacuum, not the regular line module or its full horizontal top. The proper contraction acts only on the occupied block.
The third-slot change to an anchored inner test chart, integral collision deletion and nonzero jets, scalar-extension/completion comparisons and opposite insertion maps remain separate.

claims.title: Constant spectral inputs carry a flat connection at any finite number of points
claims.statement: For positions \(a_1,\ldots,a_d\), put \(R_{\mathbf a}=\sum_{i<j}r_{ij}(a_i-a_j)\). Let \(L\) be the odd line derivation with \(Lc_{a,n}=k^{-1}\kappa^{ab}B^b_n\), \(LB^a_n=0\) and \([Q,L]=T_Y\), where \(Q\) is the line differential. For a constant ordinary dg \(Y^{\otimes d}\)-module \(T\), the connection \(\nabla_i=\partial_{a_i}+\rho_T(L^{(i)}R_{\mathbf a})\) is flat and commutes strictly with \(d_T+\rho_T(R_{\mathbf a})\). Writing \(\Delta_{\mathbf a}\) for the outgoing translated action, its horizontality holds up to \(\lambda_i=L^{(i)}\Delta_{\mathbf a}\). The logarithmic corner form preserves the stated coefficient carriers.
hypotheses: Work with \(\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{sl}_2\), \(k\in\mathbb C\setminus\mathbb Q\), and constant ordinary unbounded input complexes over \(\mathbb C\). Tensor totalization is algebraic by direct sums before each degreewise Laurent completion.

The identities are fixed-mode rational identities on carriers where the coefficient derivations and outgoing action are defined. The underlying chain connection is strictly flat; higher action coherence is not supplied by that fact.
For \(sG^{\prime}=A(s)G-GA_0\) and \(\nabla_s=s\partial_s-A(s)\), the normalized Wilson horizontal frame is \(G(s)s^{+A_0}\), with a chosen logarithm.
No canonical connection on arbitrary shape-field inputs, normalized full-complex decoupling map, current-recipient/evaluation comparison over polynomial forms, or native facet/tree coherence follows.

claims.title: Ordinary Hom over the common ring is not invariant on arbitrary test representatives
claims.statement: Put \(p=w^{-1}\), \(q=z^{-1}=sp\), \(\mathcal O=\mathbb C[s]_{(s)}\), \(D=\mathcal O((p))[s^{-1}]\), \(K_R=\mathbb C(s)((p))\) and \(K_N=\mathbb C((p))((s))\). Let \(g=p+s\) and let \(W_D\) be the scalar extension of the regular-top affine object. The complex \(E=[D\xrightarrow{g}D\to D/g]\), in degrees \(0,1,2\), is acyclic, but \(H^0\operatorname{Hom}_D(E,D)=D/g\ne0\). For trivial incoming coefficient, the ordinary current formula on the acyclic smooth test \(W_D\otimes_D E\) retracts onto this Hom complex. It therefore fails quasi-isomorphism invariance on arbitrary \(D\)-test representatives, including those representing the zero object in the localizing category generated by \(W_D\).
hypotheses: Substitution \(p=-s\) gives a unital map \(D\to\mathbb C((s))\) killing \(g\), so \(g\) is a nonunit. The polynomial and proper-cofree contractions used in the witness are \(D\)-linear.
The closed field and constant ground-field test theorems remain valid. The counterexample concerns the displayed ordinary Hom formula, not every possible derived current construction.

claims.title: Explicit finite cell tests retain the current comparison over D
claims.statement: Put \(p=w^{-1}\), \(q=z^{-1}=sp\), \(\mathcal O=\mathbb C[s]_{(s)}\), \(D=\mathcal O((p))[s^{-1}]\), \(K_R=\mathbb C(s)((p))\) and \(K_N=\mathbb C((p))((s))\). Let \(W_D\) be the scalar extension of the regular-top affine object. An explicit finite \(W_D\)-cell model is a bounded complex obtained from \(W_D\) by finitely many shifts, finite sums and cones, with its actual enhanced maps. Finite cone induction extends the original current comparison at \(W_D\) to every such model and proves invariance under quasi-isomorphisms between them. For \(\mathfrak b=\langle H,E\rangle\subset\mathfrak{sl}_2\), let \(D_s\) have rank one with \(H=s\), \(E=0\). The parameter-Verma object has the finite induced Chevalley model \(W_D\otimes_D\Lambda^\bullet\mathfrak b_D\otimes_D D_s\), which gives a nonconstant common-form example.
hypotheses: Native recipient conclusions retain the coherent ordinary smooth affine–right-line realization, tensor–Hom adjunction and full original unit, restricted cofree model and common-cutoff actions, the native bimodule-functorial derived ideal triangle, and the bounded-below positive-current torsion theorem.

Evaluate the coefficient formula on the supplied finite cell model. This is not an assertion of ordinary Hom on an arbitrary representative of the same derived object or on all of the localizing category generated by \(W_D\).
The highest-weight parameter \(s\) remains nonconstant after either named field extension. General ring-defined tests need a derived construction and its support proof.

claims.title: The Gaussian ray and its charged endpoint
claims.statement: At nonzero level \(k\) the rotation-finite endpoint of the oriented abelian Wilson ray of charge \(\alpha\) is the Heisenberg Fock space \(\mathcal F_\alpha\) in degree zero. The normalized intertwiner adds charges. In the upper half-plane the exchange has scalar \(e^{\pi i\alpha\beta/k}\) and a framing rotation by \(\theta\) acts by \(e^{i\theta\alpha^2/(2k)}\).
hypotheses: Use regular compact kernels, the fixed Cauchy propagator, the radial regulator, outgoing subtraction and common-chamber continuation. The endpoint includes every finite oscillator descendant.

claims.title: A joint monodromy test for a collision
claims.statement: Let \(j\) include the distinct ordered points and let \(L\) be a finite-rank complex local system there. At a collision partition the ordinary stalk of \(\operatorname{Cone}(j_!L\to Rj_*L)\) is nonzero exactly when the full radial twists of the nonsingleton blocks have a common generalized eigenspace of eigenvalue one.
hypotheses: Work on a nonopen collision partition in an ordered configuration on a smooth complex curve, locally the affine line, with a finite-dimensional complex Betti local system in ordinary degree zero. The full twists commute. Eigenvalue one on different summands for different blocks does not meet the joint condition.

claims.title: The two cohomological degrees of the deepest link
claims.statement: For one cluster of \(n\) points with total twist \(C\), suppose the induced direction systems on \(\ker(C-1)\) and \(\operatorname{coker}(C-1)\) have clean extension along the boundary of \(M_{0,n+1}\). The only possible stalk groups are in degrees \(n-2\) and \(n-1\). Both have dimension \((n-2)!\dim\ker(C-1)\).
hypotheses: Take \(n\ge3\). Each boundary divisor of the compactified direction space must have no eigenvalue one on either angular coefficient system. Radial invariants and coinvariants occur in circle degrees zero and one, respectively, and their coefficient systems can differ.

claims.title: Four charged lines have a deepest collision invisible on every proper link
claims.statement: Pair the fused ray with its normalized outgoing highest-weight functional. Its separated coefficient is \(\prod_{a<b}(z_a-z_b)^{\alpha_a\alpha_b/k}\). At a partition the ordinary comparison stalk survives exactly when \(k^{-1}\sum_{a<b\in S}\alpha_a\alpha_b\) is integral in every nonsingleton block \(S\). For four charges one at level two, proper blocks have twist \(-1\) and the full block has twist \(+1\). At the full collision the cone has rank two in degrees two and three.
hypotheses: Use the charge-four outgoing functional for the four-line example, its fixed framing and the common chamber. This selects the separated top coefficient. Selecting a physical extension across the full diagonal requires an attaching map.

claims.title: A projective line of attachments with the same stalk and costalk dimensions
claims.statement: Consider the four-charge coefficient at level two on the normal slice \(X=\mathbb C^3\). Write \(i\) for the origin, \(K=i^*Rj_*L\) and \(V=H^2K\). For every line \(W\subset V\) the perverse quotient \(P_W=j_!L[3]/i_*W\) has stalk \(W[1]\) and costalk cohomology \(V/W\) in degree zero and \(H^3K\) in degree one. The image of the attaching arrow in \(V\) recovers \(W\). Thus \(\mathbb P(V)\simeq\mathbb P^1\) indexes pairwise nonisomorphic extensions with identical rank tables.
hypotheses: Fix the connected separated rank-one coefficient and its clean extension on the punctured slice. Its scalar automorphisms preserve every line. Factorization, self-duality and selection by a physical or Hall operation impose further conditions.

claims.title: Which attaching morphism does the physical collision choose?
claims.statement: For a specified physical coefficient on four charged lines, determine its actual deepest point coefficient and arrow to \(i^*Rj_*L\). With point coefficient \(V_0\) and attachment fixed, \(Rj_*L\mathbin{\times}^{h}_{i_*i^*Rj_*L}i_*V_0\) reconstructs the sheaf at this gluing step. A coherent factorization system must also identify all iterated collisions and both vacua.

claims.title: The Gaussian change of fields transports the marked current and charge
claims.statement: On the Gaussian half-space with \(k=\hbar\kappa\ne0\), the change of fields \(T(s\alpha e_\Phi)=-\kappa^{-1}dz\wedge\alpha\) and \(T(s\beta e_\eta)=(-1)^{|\beta|+1}\beta\) identifies the regular quantum complex with its abelian Chern–Simons model. It preserves the differential, mixed contraction, disjoint products, boundary condition and empty unit. With the same Cauchy regulator it also identifies the annular current and charged ray coupling.
hypotheses: Use the marking \(\zeta=+i\), unit-integral interior collar profile, boundary condition \(i^*\eta=0\), compact smooth joint kernels at fixed field number and the algebraic sum over field numbers.

claims.title: The harmonic disk fixes its own probability law
claims.statement: Fix the constant mode of a real harmonic scalar on the unit disk to zero. At finite Fourier cutoff the squared Dirichlet amplitude \(\exp[-(4\pi)^{-1}\int_D|\nabla\phi|^2]\) normalizes to a product Gaussian density. The compatible marginals give independent circular complex coefficients \(Z_n\) with \(\mathbb E|Z_n|^2=n\). Writing \(h(r)=\sum_{n>0}Z_nr^n/n\), the Fock isometry sends \(p_n\) to \(Z_n\). The normalized real Mehler collar acts on an energy-\(E\) holomorphic polynomial by \(q^E\).
hypotheses: The angular coordinate and action fix the normalization. Use \(0<r<1\) and \(0<q\le1\).

claims.title: An interior cochain differentiates the boundary polynomial
claims.statement: At level one, give the \(j\)th interior linear insertion a compact normal support strictly above the collar and a tangential cutoff equal to one on the test annulus. Its Wick pairing with \(p_m\) is \(\delta_{jm}\). On the annular representative of any finite polynomial it therefore acts by \(\partial_{p_j}\), while the boundary creation mode acts by multiplication by \(p_j\).
hypotheses: The compact annular representatives have finite angular support. The interior insertion is a cochain. Its descent as an individual class would require a further closedness calculation.

claims.title: A mixed interior observable distinguishes two disk preparations
claims.statement: The normalized states \(w_\pm=(p_1^2\pm p_2)/2\) give the same single-mode marginals for the harmonic disk. The supported interior derivative and boundary creators give the mixed symbol \(Z_1^2\overline{Z_2}+\overline{Z_1}^{\,2}Z_2\). Its disk expectations are \(+2\) and \(-2\). The unnormalized one-sided collar pairings are \(+2q^2\) and \(-2q^2\).
hypotheses: The annular current has level one. Use the independent zero-mode-fixed harmonic disk action and its real Mehler collar. The cochain acts on the polynomial representatives. An absolute gravitational cap would have to supply its own cycle and sewing.

claims.title: Two neutralizing rays prepare the linearly sourced harmonic disk
claims.statement: At level one a regulated collision of charges \((a,-a)\) at \((r,0)\) gives \(r^{-a^2}\exp(a\sum_{n>0}r^nJ_{-n}/n)|0\rangle\). Its disk image is \(r^{-a^2}e^{a h(r)}\), of squared norm \(r^{-2a^2}(1-r^2)^{-a^2}\). Independently tilting the disk action by \(2a\operatorname{Re}h(r)\) gives the same normalized law, with mode means \(ar^n\) and variances \(n\). Its normalized one-sided collar value is \(((1-r^2)/(1-qr^2))^{a^2}\).
hypotheses: Use real \(a\), \(0<r<1\), the real logarithm of \(r\), the fixed Wilson regulator and the disk with its constant mode fixed. The normalization divides out the mutual ray scalar. A charged zero mode or an absolute three-dimensional cap requires separate data.

claims.title: The native unit on inflated complexes
claims.statement: Let \(B\) be the native algebra, \(H\) its ghost quotient and \(R\) its algebra of weight zero. With the coherent right action and cofree realization on the smooth regular-top bimodule \(W\), the original tensor–Hom unit is invertible on every ordinary unbounded \(H\)-complex inflated to \(B\), hence on every inflated \(R\)-complex.
hypotheses: Keep the signed evaluations of the actual adjunction. In the graded category allow all internal shifts.

claims.title: Affine linkage has only finitely many energies at nonrational shift
claims.statement: For a finite-dimensional simple complex Lie algebra at shifted level \(s\notin\mathbb Q\), the integral real roots over a highest weight form the graph of a rational-linear mode function on a finite reflection subsystem. Their Weyl group embeds into the finite Weyl group, with longest length at most \(|\Phi^+|\).

claims.title: Positive-weight tensor words advance inside one linkage block
claims.statement: For the augmentation ideal \(I=\ker(B\to R)\), a nonzero positive-weight tensor step sends energy \(a\) to \(a+m\) in the same affine linkage block, with \(m>0\). Testing the actual fixed-weight bimodule complexes on horizontal Verma modules detects their acyclicity.
hypotheses: Take a nonrational shifted level. The cofree model uses smooth positive-current invariants and the horizontal action on both sides of the balanced tensor.

claims.title: The positive ideal vanishes at the positive-root bound
claims.statement: Put \(d=|\Phi^+|\). For every simple type at nonrational shifted level, \(I^{\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}(d+1)}=0\) in the derived category of \(R\)-bimodules. Each nonzero step strictly decreases the remaining length in the finite reflection subsystem. This bound holds for each fixed tuple of positive weights, in the graded and ungraded settings.

claims.title: The derived tensor exponent is exactly one plus the number of positive roots
claims.statement: A saturated chain for the longest Weyl element gives a nonzero word of length \(d=|\Phi^+|\) at every nonrational shifted level. Multiplication on this derived \(R\)-balanced tensor is nonzero. Combined with vanishing in length \(d+1\), the sharp exponent of the actual positive-weight ideal is \(1+|\Phi^+|\).
hypotheses: Use the split weight-zero quotient of the native algebra and the actual positive-weight bimodule, with all simple types allowed. The corresponding \(B\)-balanced fibre-inclusion power is also nonzero at length \(d\).

claims.title: Nonrational induction recovers the entire ordinary source
claims.statement: Under the native realization hypotheses, the original unit \(X\to\Psi\Phi X\) is invertible for every \(X\in D(B)\), with no bound on cochain degree. The image in the smooth target is \(\operatorname{Loc}(W)\), and the actual counit is the coreflection onto it. The split augmentation and the tensor bound give a tower with at most \(1+|\Phi^+|\) factors inflated from \(R\).
hypotheses: Take a finite-dimensional simple complex Lie algebra and a nonrational shifted level. Use the coherent native right action, actual affine-free lifts, cofree realization and inflated-unit identifications. Include all internal shifts of \(W\) in the graded category.

claims.title: The split weight-zero quotient has no finite exponent at rational shift
claims.statement: At every rational shifted level, in every simple type, all positive multiplication powers of the ideal of the split weight-zero quotient survive. The \(R\)-balanced products and the \(B\)-balanced fibre inclusions are nonzero in every length. This tests the quotient \(B\to R\). Classification of the original unit requires the actual right action and ghost quotient.
hypotheses: Take the split weight-zero quotient for a finite-dimensional simple complex Lie algebra at rational shifted level. Retain both the \(R\)-balanced multiplication and the \(B\)-balanced inclusion of the actual fibre.

claims.title: The raw level minus-three telescope has invertible original unit
claims.statement: For the specified rank-one telescope \(L\) at raw level \(-3\), \(R\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}L=0\) while \(H\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}L\ne0\). Its actual unit is invertible. Thus vanishing after weight-zero base change does not detect the realization kernel on this example.

claims.title: The noncritical cohomology field is regular
claims.statement: Over \(R_3=\mathbb C[\hbar]/(\hbar^3)\) at \(K\ne-2\), the full state cohomology is \((R_3\mathbf1\oplus R_3 b)\otimes_{\mathbb C} L\), with \(|b|=3\), \(Tb=b^2=0\) and \(L=\mathbb C[I_1,I_2,\ldots]\otimes\Lambda(\xi_j^I:j\ge0)\). The field is \(Y(x,u)y=(e^{uT}x)y\). All singular products vanish, and coefficientwise reduction gives the prescribed lower precisions.
hypotheses: The translation-compatible state deformation retract acts on the full algebraic trace-current and trace-ghost factor. Zero level is included.

claims.title: The ordered kernel agrees on both nontrace seed states
claims.statement: For the dressed minus field the seed on \(q_\hbar\) includes the term \(-2\hbar^2 B_q\) from the shifted ghost–current kernel. The seed on \(\omega_\hbar\) equals the prescribed operator. Translation and pairing with a single finite ghost germ extend both equalities to all trace spectators. They agree on the small state complex used in the noncritical retract.
hypotheses: Preserve the order of right current words and the full trace factor. At critical level the seed computation applies on the specified included states only.

claims.title: The normalized retained comparison holds in every rooted degree
claims.statement: At fixed \(K\ne-2\) write \((i,p,k)\) for the translation-compatible state deformation retract, \(\Phi\) for the prescribed pure-root kernel and \(\mathcal Y^\sharp\) for the dressed comparison. With \(\Delta=\Phi-\mathcal Y^\sharp\), the cochain \(\kappa=\Delta k-h^\Lambda ip\) has \(\delta\kappa=\Delta\) and exactly zero scalar pairing. Contracting with it compares the two evaluations in every middle degree, with both translation laws.
hypotheses: Work over \(R_3\) on the ordered rooted carrier. Keep the complete algebraic trace factor in \(ip\). Agreement of the two seeds kills the difference on the small complex. The creation column is preserved up to homotopy.

claims.title: The marked homotopy on a whole Laurent series
claims.statement: On each right slice choose a single Laurent floor, a common middle ghost cutoff and finite right PBW support for the entire series. Each output coefficient of the retained evaluation is then a finite convolution. Extending the rooted homotopy to the restricted marked carrier compares the two evaluations on whole series and transports through the global Cartan isomorphism. The two positive-inserted pieces \(\mathcal J,\Xi\) are prescribed identically on the two sides.
hypotheses: Use \(R_3\) and a noncritical numerical level, original nested operation order, fixed inserted state and algebraic rooted input. Precomposition to the raw source uses its specified projection. Derivation of the positive-inserted pieces by independent physical products, the proper unit diagrams and both adjunction triangles are further problems.

claims.title: All critical state cohomology lifts freely through precision three
claims.statement: At \(K=-2\) the full graded state cohomology over \(R_3\) is free on the classical critical state cohomology. Critical invariant states, their oper forms and the absolute ghost group yield native cycle lifts. Ordered products of lifts and the differential on a classical complement give an invertible triangular change of basis.
hypotheses: This is additive state cohomology. The critical small complex contains the positive relative oper-form part and its absolute ghost copy. A comparison of the critical fields on these classes needs their operations as well.

claims.title: A critical frame preserves translation and its first coefficient
claims.statement: At \(K=-2\) a critical frame \(F=1+\hbar F_1+\hbar^2 F_2\) with the prescribed \(F_1\) intertwines the classical and native state differentials and commutes with total translation and constant \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\). The resulting deformation retract acts by the identity on the trace factor and includes the lifted positive oper forms.
hypotheses: Take the algebraic four-colour state complex over \(R_3\). The critical small complex is larger than the noncritical one. This frame addresses the state differential.

claims.title: Trace creators force free cohomology in any covariantly lifting source
claims.statement: If \(t\) distinct closed degree-one elements act as the prescribed trace creators in the precision-three corner, a normalized covariant derived module lift forces a split free summand of rank \(\binom{t}{p}\) in source degree \(p\). Increasing products of creators followed by the exterior detector split off the corresponding basis words.
hypotheses: Take the same corner actions and normalized vacuum value at any numerical level. Already one creator forces a free degree-one class. The retained coefficient pairing uses contraction in its middle dual and has a different variance.

claims.title: The principal-part flip reroots the normal coordinate
claims.statement: Exact rational exchange transports each raw word to one ambient ordering. Conjugating the pair residue by this transport preserves the complete principal part, including the change of root and all Taylor coefficients on the spectator. The resulting collision coalgebra has all-chart transitions, separated coproducts and supported counits.

claims.title: Every finite word has compatible supported collision maps
claims.statement: The finite cobar words of the ordered Cousin coalgebra have support counits on every surjection. Their affine Spencer complexes form a strict contravariant diagram with an associative lax external product over the original base. Two paths to \(13\mid2\) and to \(13\mid24\) agree with their normal derivatives retained.
hypotheses: Use an ordinary state module flat over a commutative algebra over a characteristic-zero field, with free vacuum summand, exact rational fields and Laurent-polynomial finite-state exchange. The curve is an affine line punctured at finitely many rational points. Use algebraic tensors and retain the full principal part.

claims.title: Original-base word integration recovers the intrinsic mode quotient
claims.statement: The singleton-word comparison extends to a unital dg algebra map \(\Theta:P_U(V)\to G\), where \(G\) is the normalized direct-sum integral of the finite word and Spencer complexes. Relation homotopies on the whole complexes identify \(H^0(G)\) with the full-arity intrinsic mode algebra, with \(H^0(\Theta)\) its identity in these coordinates.
hypotheses: Use ordinary flat states with a free vacuum summand, exact rational exchange over the same characteristic-zero base, all finite normal orders, algebraic tensors and direct-sum totals. The empty unit is isolated. Negative cohomology and an independent global or completed geometric realization require their own comparison.

claims.title: The integral finite-root Hall cobar is exact in every charge
claims.statement: For the polynomial one-loop Hall model over \(R=\mathbb Q[\hbar]\), the finite-root-jet map \(F_R:\Omega(W_R)\to S_R\) is a quasi-isomorphism of augmented dg associative algebras in all charges. Parabolic symmetrizers identify the charge-\(m\) bar with a Coxeter sphere complex. Its contraction lowers primal root degree by at most \(\binom m2\) per step, so the transposed contraction increases the finite jet cutoff by at most that amount. The map \(F_R\) intertwines charge, translation, the tautological moments and \(Y(a,z)b=(e^{zT}a)b\).
hypotheses: Take the algebraic direct sum in charge with finite root support. The operation is regular. A supported covariant comparison on the full oriented critical flag, before proper direct image, requires its own field map.

claims.title: Vacuum normalization commutes with the adic limit
claims.statement: In the arity filtration multiplication by the classical vacuum mode \(v\) is injective. The associated graded of the quotient by \(v-1\) is the quotient by its leading term \(v\). The normalized finite-precision intrinsic modes are free over their precision rings, and their inverse limit agrees with normalizing the completed module.
hypotheses: Use the determinant-one rational fields on the punctured line with the full configuration and integration-by-parts relations. Complete only in \(\hbar\).

claims.title: A diagonal pole lies outside the algebra of classical currents
claims.statement: The central-level quotient of the polynomial affine enveloping algebra embeds in the classical normalized intrinsic modes. Its current symbols miss the two-input class with coefficient \((x-y)^{-1}\) on \(e_{12},e_{21}\). Consequently the Cauchy currents cannot generate every normalized intrinsic mode.
hypotheses: Take rank at least two. The diagonal-pole class is tested in the intrinsic algebra before evaluation on a smooth module.

claims.title: Both divided determinants vanish at precision two
claims.statement: For each rational Cauchy half-matrix \(X\), every coefficient of the descending-column determinant \((q_X-1)/\hbar\) vanishes in the intrinsic mode algebra through \(R_2=\mathbb C[\hbar]/(\hbar^2)\). The cancellation works for every rank at least two and every numerical level.
hypotheses: Use creation at zero, annihilation at infinity and the original rational configuration relations. This calculation precedes vacuum specialization.

claims.title: The opposite-root commutator inside the normalized mode algebra
claims.statement: In rank two the Laurent residue identity for the corrected Cauchy current \(U_f=B_f-\hbar Q_f\) gives the divided mixed opposite-root commutator through \(\hbar^2=0\). Both the spectator and composite terms survive the calculation. Covariance and the two partial traces then determine the other auxiliary components.
hypotheses: Take all Laurent test polynomials, \(e_{12},e_{21}\) as marked opposite roots, and vacuum mode \(v=1\). The rank-two relation uses the divided halves and centered mixed relation.

claims.title: The rank-two Cauchy map into intrinsic modes is injective and proper
claims.statement: For every numerical level \(K\), including \(0,-2\), the two Cauchy matrices induce an injective map \(D_K/\hbar^2D_K\to\overline M_2\) of \(R_2\)-algebras in rank two. Both divided determinants, the two half relations and the centered mixed relation hold in the normalized target. The classical current symbols give injectivity through this precision. A two-current diagonal pole witnesses proper image.
hypotheses: The calculation uses divided generators modulo \(\hbar^2\). The same embedding holds in every rank. At \(K\ne0\) the fixed images fail modulo \(\hbar^3\). At \(K=0\) they extend at every precision. In rank two an order-\(\hbar^2\) correction vanishing at \(K=0\) gives a proper normalized embedding modulo \(\hbar^3\) at every level. The level-splitting coproduct takes values in joint modes, whose comparison with separately integrated modes must retain the cross-diagonal poles.

claims.title: The finite Ising Ward category has a faithful fibre over three idempotents
claims.statement: For the Ising minimal model the finite semisimple Ward category has simples \(1,\psi,\sigma\) with \(\sigma\boxtimes\sigma=1\oplus\psi\). Its faithful long fibre is over \(\mathbb C^3\). The matching projector implements the relative tensor. The three simple fibres have dimensions \(3,3,4\), so the reconstructed weak Hopf algebra has dimension \(34\).
hypotheses: Use the simple Virasoro quotient at \(c=1/2\), the separated Ward product, the marked braiding, restricted duals and the weak tensor unit. A scalar-valued ordinary fibre changes the tensor problem.

claims.title: Products of adjacent double exchanges span the intertwiners on every spin power
claims.statement: The adjacent double exchanges of \(\sigma^{\boxtimes n}\) generate its complete endomorphism algebra in the finite Ising Ward category. On an output multiplicity space of dimension \(d\), the projective pure braid image is elementary abelian of order \(d^2\) and its representatives span the full matrix algebra.
hypotheses: Retain the matching projector in each tensor power and the finite-base unit. For \(n=2m\) the neutral output multiplicity is \(2^{m-1}\).

claims.title: A marked half-exchange distinguishes the two Ising orientations
claims.statement: The forward and reversed ribbon structures have projectively identical adjacent double exchanges. In the two labelled spin channels the ratio of half-exchange eigenvalues is \(i\) for one orientation and \(-i\) for the reverse. The spin twists are inverse to one another.
hypotheses: Fix the channel labels and a positive half-turn. Projectivizing a full two-channel double exchange removes the orientation-sensitive scalar.

claims.title: Four-spin Ward monodromy realizes both marked double exchanges
claims.statement: Place four spin primaries at \(0,z,1,\infty\). The two solutions of the second-order null-vector equation continue around zero and one by \(D=e^{-\pi i/4}\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)\) and \(FDF\), with \(F\) the normalized Hadamard matrix. Identifying the two channel bases intertwines the actual Ward continuations with the categorical double exchanges.

claims.title: The reflected four-spin form with a prescribed vacuum normalization
claims.statement: Assume diagonal reflected gluing of the four-spin block and leading vacuum coefficient one. The invariant Hermitian form is uniquely fixed, giving \(|f_+|^2+|f_-|^2\) in the monodromy basis. Normalizing the energy block to unit leading coefficient gives relative weight \(1/4\) and three-point coupling of magnitude \(1/2\).
hypotheses: The gluing ansatz and vacuum normalization are physical inputs. Monodromy determines their consequence on this two-channel block.

claims.title: Logarithmic sewing retains the nonsplit endpoint modules
claims.statement: The lower-bounded, finite-length, \(C_1\)-cofinite universal Virasoro category has a represented logarithmic Ward tensor product at every complex central charge. At \(c=1,25\) the full categories in this class are exact rigid ribbon categories reconstructed by complete ribbon quasi-Hopf algebras. A nonsplit input at \(c=25\) can have a fused output with Jordan blocks of size two.
hypotheses: Take restricted contragredients and the finite coend topology. Continuum reflected Hilbert modules and an independently prepared physical filling have their own domains.

claims.title: Both exceptional vacuum torsion towers have length one
claims.statement: For the polynomial universal \(W_4\) vacuum complex at \(k+4=\pm3/2,\pm2/3\), the first Bocksteins in degrees \(8\to9\) and \(11\to12\) both have rank one. The two local torsion summands, in degrees nine and twelve, are each \(R/(t)\) for a local uniformizer \(t\). A nonzero derivative across a maximal constant minor detects valuation one. The reciprocal local-family isomorphism carries the two signs to their reciprocals.
hypotheses: Use the full zero-weight relative vacuum complex over the local parameter ring, with the native coupling and all three ghost species. Dimensions of a single special fibre alone do not determine the valuation.

claims.title: A nonzero weak module invisible to all derived vacuum probes
claims.statement: At \(c=-22/5\) the universal regular \(W_3\) vacuum has a nonzero weak module \(M\) with \(\mathbf R\!\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf1,M)=0\). A finite zero-weight cochain calculation, together with contraction on the remaining weights, gives the vanishing. The vacuum-generated subcategory therefore misses objects of the full smooth category.
hypotheses: Use the universal regular algebra and the actual module. A polarized localization on all smooth modules must compare its unit and counit on nonvacuum objects as well.

claims.title: The fibre-marked row and traces miss 1,750 compact cubics
claims.statement: Let \(V=H^2(\mathrm{K3},\mathbb Q)\) with intersection form \(q\). A normalized commutative first-order product correction cyclic for the fixed Poincaré pairing is determined by a symmetric cubic \(T\in\operatorname{Sym}^3V^*\). Fix the fibre insertion \(F\) and all correction traces. Their common kernel \(\ker(\iota_F,\tau_q)\) has dimension \(1750\) and injects into internal degree \(-2\) of Hochschild degree two.
hypotheses: Fix the ordinary graded cup algebra, its marking, unit, full pairing and separate cap scalars. The product correction has degree \(-2\) and the first-order parameter has degree two.

claims.title: A sharp family of rational null probes recovers the cubic
claims.statement: Once the fibre row and correction traces are fixed, 1,750 explicit rational square-zero insertions distinguish every remaining first-order K3 cubic. Fewer fixed linear scalar measurements cannot suffice. With full middle rows instead, 21 independent rows and all traces determine the tensor if the normal to their span is anisotropic.
hypotheses: Take the same commutative normalized cyclic first-order corrections with fixed marked graded cup algebra, unit, Poincaré pairing and cap scalars. An isotropic normal to a hyperplane leaves one undetermined coefficient.

claims.title: A positive Gaussian tilt changes an assigned third cumulant
claims.statement: On a finite numerical Gaussian cycle whiten \(m\) real linear coordinates. For each real symmetric cubic \(T\) there are positive normalized probability densities with third cumulant \(tT\) at every sufficiently small nonzero real \(t\). The original mean, covariance, even tests of those coordinates and laws of the spectators are preserved.
hypotheses: The density is constructed on the finite cycle. A specified physical action would have to supply the tilt independently.

claims.title: Marked compact and Gaussian cubic measurements agree after choosing a frame
claims.statement: Identify the 22 middle K3 coordinates over \(\mathbb R\) with 22 whitened real Gaussian probes. For the positive tilt with cubic \(tT\), the changes in the marked and trace measurements are exactly \(tT(F,a,b)\) and \(t\,\tau_q(T)(D)\). The same 1,750 null insertions distinguish the common kernel on both sides.
hypotheses: Use the commutative normalized cyclic compact corrections at the fixed cup algebra, unit, marking, cap scalars and full pairing. The indefinite K3 form enters the trace test, while the independently defined Gaussian has positive covariance. The chosen marking is part of this comparison.

claims.title: The wider theta quotient exhibits the full spectral annulus
claims.statement: On the native theta Hilbert quotient \(K_s\), \(1/2<s<\min(a,1)\), translation by any real \(t\ne0\) has spectrum and Fredholm essential spectrum exactly \(e^{-s|t|}\le|\lambda|\le e^{s|t|}\). Its ordinary and essential norms equal \(e^{s|t|}\).
hypotheses: Keep the native Hardy-strip quotient with its arithmetic zero divisor. The spectral calculation is on \(K_s\) itself.

claims.title: Inter-width inclusion has dense nonclosed range
claims.statement: For \(1/2\le b<s<\min(a,1)\) the canonical injection \(j:K_s\to K_b\) has proper dense range. If both widths are strict interior widths, the spectrum and essential spectrum of \(j^*j\) are \([0,1]\).
hypotheses: Density does not give an equivalence of Hilbert norms. The endpoint \(b=1/2\) is allowed in the range statement.

claims.title: No equivalent Hilbert norm makes the wider theta translations unitary
claims.statement: At every strict width \(1/2<s<\min(a,1)\) the spectral annulus of translation on \(K_s\) reaches outside the unit circle for \(t\ne0\). Spectrum is invariant under equivalent norms, so this group cannot act unitarily for any such norm. The inclusion into a narrower quotient has proper dense range.
hypotheses: The obstruction concerns this bounded translation representation. A positive realization on an independently specified carrier is a separate question.

claims.title: One compact shape gives an equivalent Weil positivity test
claims.statement: Write \(Q(g)=W(g*g^*)\) for the complete Weil form. For a fixed explicit tilted dyadic convolution bump \(\phi\) of half-width \(2^{-20}\), put \(E_n=Q(\phi+R_{\log n}\phi)\), where \(R_t\) denotes translation. The Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to \(E_n\ge0\) for all sufficiently large integers \(n\). The limsup growth exponent of \(\max(0,-E_n)\) equals \(\sup_\rho|\operatorname{Re}\rho-1/2|\).
hypotheses: Use the full prime-power, archimedean and polar terms, and true zero multiplicities. The proof fixes one phase and passes through the explicit formula. The signs of the infinite tail remain unknown.

claims.title: Arithmetic point values lose a normal derivative modulo the prime square
claims.statement: On an integral prime-power jet chart the chosen normal operator gives \(D_0(x_0^p+p x_1-x_0)=-p\pmod {p^2}\). A kernel supported only on arithmetic points misses this value. The residue and Frobenius comparisons require their specified height changes, supports and variance.
hypotheses: Use the enriched integral nerve with its polynomial normal jets. A common integral local-field operation must compare its independently specified products on the same domain.

claims.title: The Weierstrass determinant realizes the normalized Igusa root
claims.statement: For a smooth proper genus-two curve write \(H=\pi_*\omega\), let \(W\) be its six Weierstrass branches over the base and \(e_5:\operatorname{Sym}^5H\to(q_W)_*(\omega^5|_W)\) their evaluation map. With \(j\) the Jacobian morphism, \(\det(e_5)^2=2^{32}\pi^{20}j^*\Xi\). After identifying the two oriented sign lines, \(j^*D_5=-\det(e_5)/(2^{16}\pi^{10})\). Both section identities pull back to smooth complex families, including families over nonreduced bases.
hypotheses: Use the Hodge and étale square trivializations and the fixed reference sign. An independently constructed compact Hall line, a physical Pfaffian and extension to the stable boundary need further identifications.

claims.title: A common strict lower cochain bound suffices at every level
claims.statement: In every simple type and at every level, the native unit is invertible on a dg \(B\)-source with a representative whose cochain terms share a strict lower bound. Internal weights may range without a common bound. More generally, K-injectivity of the actual twisted cofree realization is sufficient.
hypotheses: Use the actual smooth affine–right-native bimodule and its original adjunction. A lower bound on the terms of a representative and a bound only on its cohomology impose different conditions.

claims.title: Finite exterior sources have explicit mapping spaces on arbitrary ordinary targets
claims.statement: For \(r\) degree-one exterior generators, each nonempty subset \(I\) contributes a top of degree \(2-|I|\) and a bottom of degree \(1-|I|\). The signed splitting equations on \(2(2^r-1)\) entries compute the derived mapping space into any ordinary algebraic dg vertex target. At scalar target it is \(\mathbb C^{r+\binom r2}_{\rm disc}\times K(\mathbb C^r,1)\).
hypotheses: Use algebraic tensors and state-complex quasi-isomorphisms. The finite ordinary source quotients realize the transitions. The genuine actor category retains an independent boundary leg.

claims.title: The two remaining conditions for the genuine Heisenberg actor
claims.statement: The comparison from strict roofs to the specified genuine Heisenberg action space is an equivalence precisely when the whole zero-detector sector is connected and the genuine automorphism space of the marked object inducing the identity on state cohomology is contractible.
hypotheses: Use the nonzero-level rank-one Heisenberg source, all its genuine unit paths and the full two-leg slice. An isomorphism of the scalar loop factors alone leaves both conditions untested.

claims.title: Two marked roots give a sharp depth bound on the actual residue complex
claims.statement: With four simple positive spectator bounds and two marked roots, the literal raw vertex kernel has projective dimension at most one over the five-variable relative ring. Each genuine pair-image module has projective dimension at most two. The resulting cokernel has projective dimension at most four, short of the height of its only possible defect support.
hypotheses: Take the original incidence maps, \(\mu=1\) and zero spectator-pair bounds. The quadratic contact is taken over the full relative polynomial base.

claims.title: Second residue compatibility holds for every marked count at four simple bounds
claims.statement: Let \(G_m\) be the kernel from the four true triple images to the fourfold image, modulo the image of the six pair maps. At four simple positive spectator bounds and \(\mu=1\), \(G_m=0\) for every \(m\ge0\), including \(m=5\). At two marks depth excludes the height-five support. At larger \(m\) a flat coprime-factor chart reduces the only possible associated prime to that same quadratic contact.
hypotheses: Use the original zero-pair-bound image complex or its specified fractionally normalized common-pair lattice. The charge-six total-complex vanishing also requires the prescribed pure, pair and triple amplitude bounds and injectivity of the original first residue.

claims.title: One selected residue column and the remaining charge-seven group
claims.statement: For four simple positive spectator bounds at \(\mu=1\), the one-selected complex satisfies \(H^i(C_1(m))=0\) for \(i<m-1\), for every \(m\). At charge seven the total complex has \(H^n(D_{4,7})=0\) for \(n<6\), and \(H^6(D_{4,7})\simeq H^2(C_2(5))\). The latter is the actual four-spectator, two-selected group, whose value remains to be computed.
hypotheses: Use the original signed four-label complex over \(\mathbb C\) with genuine pure, pair and triple lower amplitudes, the quartet finite-normal Spencer inequality for the complete root-count family with its holonomic, factorization and deck conditions, and the original first-residue injection.

The fourfold coefficient has projective dimension at most three, finite jointly nilpotent normals and finite zero-mark module on this recipient. The common scalar gives the stated arbitrary nonnegative spectator-pair bounds.

claims.title: Two independent incoming bars support a three-pole current evaluation
claims.statement: Take the intersection in which every outer Laurent coefficient has finite spectator span across the entire inner series. Two independently resolved incoming bars on this intersection carry the original full three-pole current evaluation. The finite rational rows of the tensorator control all incoming lengths for each outgoing word, and radial shuffle compares the two original binary evaluations.
hypotheses: Use the algebraic pair-first coefficient topology, the nonrational rank-one affine system and separately support-preserving actions. Finite total spectator cohomology supplies the full comparison with the named independently factorized endpoint.

claims.title: Two separately resolved pairs support a four-pole evaluation
claims.statement: At four marked positions form the outer coefficient from the two independently completed pairs in the \((12)(34)\) order. Its intersection with the symmetric coefficient algebra carries the original four-pole current evaluation over the split scalar ring \(D_*\). The two incoming bar augmentations preserve the finite tensor rank of each outer coefficient and the rational-head identities on the actual outer bar.
hypotheses: Intersect the conic scalar ring with the split scalar space \(B=(\mathbb C((p_1))\otimes_{\mathbb C}\mathbb C((p_2)))((q))\) inside the common symmetric coefficient carrier, giving \(D_*=D_{\rm con}\cap B\). Use factorwise or separately support-preserving incoming actions. A native regular intermediate, both occupied integral products and general changes of tree need additional constructions.

claims.title: Occupied projection admits every fixed jet of the surviving pair
claims.statement: After the middle occupied projection the surviving two-point current evaluation and its unit have all prescribed finite normal jets in the shifted chart \(q\mapsto q/(1+tq)\). Before projection the unscaled regular middle slot can have coefficient \(-t^{-1}x_0\) on the horizontal unit. Thus the projected jet theorem has a sharper domain than an unprojected slotwise integral splitting.
hypotheses: Keep the proper current, the original surviving chart, the pulled-back tests and the indicated occupied covector. The two integral ternary iterates require a comparison before this projection.

claims.title: The one-exterior integral cone has odd elementary divisors
claims.statement: On the protected one-exterior regular constituent with pole cap \(m\), one recombination is invertible. For the other grouping the separated remote term is an identity, and the local cokernel is the \(K[t]_{(t)}\)-module given by \(K[x,r]/(x^m,r^m)\) with \(t=x-r\). Its elementary divisors have orders \(1,3,\ldots,2m-1\). Finite normal jets retain the quotient and annihilator terms.
hypotheses: Keep the original discrete valuation base, the local flag, its proper-pole head and the chosen one-exterior coefficient. The full two binary iterates have other sectors and different occupied maps.

claims.title: Two independently prepared composites sew on a receiving graph domain
claims.statement: At outer coordinate one the received-energy graph domains admit two independently prepared Virasoro composites. Sewing gives a bounded positive component and a separately normalized diagonal vacuum component. The positive part is in the four-word image closure at the admitted inner coordinates. Three such inputs admit a positive rotation in its specified region.
hypotheses: Use the original label spaces, common positive-energy graph bounds and the prescribed vacuum form. A global meromorphic and vacuum reassociation on arbitrary completed inputs requires a further continuity theorem.

claims.title: Continuity for a composite depends on its original image norm
claims.statement: A continuous forest functional extends to the closure of the original positive tree image precisely when each target seminorm satisfies a uniform finite Gram bound with one admissible superexponential polar weight on all finite original states. Vanishing on the kernel of the positive projection tests algebraic descent, while the Gram bound tests continuity on the receiving image.
hypotheses: Use complete Hausdorff targets, the original tree coefficients and its actual image topology. A quotient topology on a parameterizing source can be strictly different.

claims.title: The M2 flux has zero algebraic Yoneda square
claims.statement: For every fixed positive rank \(N\) the central flux class has square zero in the algebraic endpoint derived endomorphisms. On the polynomial Weyl Lie algebra its scalar four-cocycle is an ordinary Chevalley–Eilenberg boundary. The specific shuffle representative itself takes the nonzero value \(3\lambda^4\) on \(x,y,x^3,y^3\).
hypotheses: Use the actual polynomial algebra at the stipulated Weyl parameter, its scalar quotient and the original endpoint module. The existence of an algebraic primitive leaves its locality and its physical junction comparison to be tested.

claims.title: No uniformly finite spatial jet realizes the marked M2 primitive
claims.statement: Fix \(\lambda\ne0\), \(N>0\) and any Taylor order \(L\). On the original polynomial inputs there is no trilinear primitive for the specified flux-square cochain that factors through the order-\(L\) jet at the origin in each input. The result holds with scalar coefficients and with the full endpoint endomorphisms.
hypotheses: High distinct odd powers kill every proposed uniform finite-jet differential on a suitable test while the flux-square representative survives. An order-dependent or analytic counterterm would require another domain.

claims.title: Separated M5 surfaces detect the order of the Miura derivative
claims.statement: For two disjoint magnetic collars and a Weyl test \(f(z)w\) of degree at most two in \(z\), the half-difference of the ordered Ward readings is \(c_M(q_1j_2[f\prime]-q_2j_1[f\prime])/2\) through first order. With \(q_i=K_i\tau/c_M\), \(K_i=N_i\) and \(W_1\sim c_MT\), this matches the order-odd derivative of the two-surface Miura stress tensor. Two unit stacks with \(f=z^2/2\) and one current excitation on the second stack give \(+\tau/2\) times the vacuum.
hypotheses: Use the disjoint unit-integral temporal collars, right-action Ward marking, the original incoming flux and the fixed tree-level charge calibration. Contact at coincidence and a separate physical orientation and phase calibration require independent maps.

claims.title: Oriented critical multiplication on the full flag
claims.statement: Construct a supported arrow in the same variance from the charge-two critical flag to its independent Cauchy-field recipient before proper pushforward. For each multiplication, the difference between the two actual composites must equal \(dH+Hd\) on that common coefficient. The two odd directions, node attachment, projective framing, supported unit and both orders are part of the map.

claims.title: An uncut affine marginal and fixed-adjoint stress covariance differ on an even test
claims.statement: Integrating the actual affine Gaussian on its uncut BV cycle gives a normalized stress marginal. On an interior even quadratic test its mixed Green coefficient differs from the fixed-adjoint stress covariance in the specified gauge. Changing the overall scalar of a state preserves its normalized two-point values.
hypotheses: The distinguishing test is generally off shell. On a common cyclic complex the induced Wick products of closed linear probes agree. A cut and a physical cap require a separate comparison.

claims.title: Spatial sewing for the independently prepared gravitational cap
claims.statement: Construct the affine-to-stress pushforward on the actual cut family and identify its quartet integration, orientations, phases, residual modes and reference insertion with those of a separately specified cap. The sewn map must compare source-dependent observables and higher connected moments on their common physical domain.

claims.title: Consecutive cuts, ordered collisions and the transposed bar algebra
claims.statement: For connected positive-arity coefficients, bar–cobar reconstruction terminates in finite length at each arity. The word tensor uses consecutive cuts. Ordered collision convolution uses all ordered decompositions. On the stipulated holonomic coefficients Verdier transposition changes the bar coalgebra to an algebra for the corresponding shriek tensor.
hypotheses: Keep the empty tensor unit, the singleton vacuum, dualizing coefficient, variances and normal jets separately. Identifying an independently specified second field theory requires a marked comparison of operations.

claims.title: All-genus arithmetic gluing retains one shared discriminant label
claims.statement: For the specified holomorphic extension, the marked vacuum average at genus \(g\) uses a tuple in the discriminant group \(D^g\). Each handle has its own coset coordinate, but one gluing isometry acts on the entire tuple. Contracting the commutant block with this averaged theta vector gives the arithmetic value. The standard-section Siegel–Weil factor is one for \(r>g+1\) and two otherwise.
hypotheses: Take a strongly rational holomorphic complex vertex algebra with chosen Cartan, strongly rational Heisenberg commutant, positive nonvacuum simple weights, positive even lattice rank \(r\ge3\), matching period and anomaly lines, and the genuine stabilizer weights. Independent averaging on the two sides of a separating cut changes the joint amplitude.

claims.title: A compact coefficient can survive on a stratum with zero numerical integral
claims.statement: On the nonsplit Kummer local product stratum the oriented dual-line cubic gives a nonzero coefficient before numerical integration. The geometric relative unit lives over the classifying stack of the elliptic curve, while the numerical reduced derivation kills the scalar algebra unit. A coefficient comparison must retain these two inputs.

claims.title: Yoneda multiplication in the exceptional vacuum algebra
claims.statement: In the coupled polynomial \(W_4\) vacuum complex the \((-1)\)-mode of a cocycle gives Yoneda composition with its graded sign. In weight zero this is graded commutative. At shifted level \(3/2\) the degree-three generator pairs the six chosen starting classes, in degrees \(0,5,7,8,9,12\), with their six partners. The zero entries have primitives in the same PBW complex. The reciprocal and sign comparisons carry the two-sided strings to the other exceptional fibres. For the additional degree-eight class \(u\), one also has \(\eta_7u=0\) in degree-fifteen cohomology at all four shifted levels. This determines the remaining binary product.
hypotheses: Use the exhibited representatives and ordered ghost basis. At \(k+4=3/2\), alternative rational cocycles have product zero by the ghost-spin bound. In the fixed representatives the product is a coboundary. Reciprocal and complementary duality transport its cohomology class.

claims.title: Each originally marked current obstructs a lift to two bulk inputs
claims.statement: On either of the two marked preparations \(a_Ee,ea_E\), with \(a_E=J_E(-1)\), the noncritical endpoint evaluation at the vacuum pair has value \(v_E=J_E(-1)\mathbf1\). Its native differential already has coefficient \(2E_1h_0\) at order zero. A closed two-bulk-input lift would make this value a cycle. Its failure survives forgetting the actor actions.
hypotheses: Use the original rooted-input and output projection, its two endpoint markings and \(R_3\). The retained homotopy lands after this projection. Changing the source by pullback gives a different lifting question.

claims.title: A cubic jet distinguishes the sixth field from its positioned tensorator
claims.statement: On the ordered merged input \(v\mid v^2\) the order-six regular difference between the repaired sextic and quintic fields is \(-Q_6(v^3)\). For the actual balanced disjoint tensorator the order-six difference vanishes. At order seven on \(v^3\otimes v\) with unit base coefficients and \(z=z_1-z_2\), the coefficient of \(z^{-6}v^2Tv\otimes v\) in the difference is \(-5267/270\).
hypotheses: Use the fixed spectral frame, the two original field orders and the given cubic state, coordinates and parameter. This local formal field calculation does not select an independently realized global spectral theory.

claims.title: A differentiated marked input separates two elliptic cubic contacts
claims.statement:
On the old-root/new-root zero-jet graph put \(B=b+ ar V_k\), \(\omega=d ar V_k\), \(s=(s_j)_-\) and \(
u=ds\). The target-boundary and source-precomposition columns vanish on \(B,Bs,\omega,B
u,\omega s,\omega
u\). In the third column, the graph-first order compared with either specified \(q\)-first order gives \(b\zeta_j c_Vc_x/2\) on \(B
u\) and zero on the other five rows.
hypotheses: Use the old and new roots, the specified ordering and fixed lower primitives. A full relative elliptic cubic must compare its independent compact coefficient, old-cylinder term and complete Hom differential.

claims.title: The first three optimal graded Witt tail depths are three, five and seven
claims.statement: For smooth graded positive-Witt complexes whose cohomology is annihilated by a common tail \(L_k\), sufficiently deep restriction splits the complex as its cohomology noncanonically. The first three optimal universal depths are \(3,5,7\) for \(k=1,2,3\). The third improves the purely numerical threshold eight because a nonzero cup product removes the first apparent obstruction.
hypotheses: Keep the cohomological annihilator and internal grading. Explicit nonformal two-layer complexes at depth \(2k\) give the matching lower bounds in the first three cases.

claims.title: Full unweighted moment-map restriction on a regular McKay orbit
claims.statement: For a finite subgroup \(\Gamma\subset\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb C)\) and dimension \(n\delta\), the unweighted block restriction from the invariant moment-map Koszul complex to \(((\mathbb C[x,y]^\Gamma)^{\otimes n}\otimes\Lambda^\bullet\mathbb C^n)^{S_n}\) is a quasi-isomorphism with its exterior generators retained.
hypotheses: Take the doubled affine McKay quiver, ordinary unweighted block traces and \(n\ge1\).

claims.title: Removing the matching scalar odd class preserves McKay restriction
claims.statement: Normalize the sum of the ordinary vertex traces by \(\sum_i\delta_i\). Its odd scalar is closed and maps to \(\sum_j\theta_j\). After splitting off that common exterior factor, regular-orbit restriction is still a quasi-isomorphism on the two quotients.
hypotheses: Use the unweighted blocks on both sides. Dimension-weighting replaces the trace multiplier by \(\sum_i\delta_i^2\) and requires its own scalar complement.

claims.title: Permutation symmetry leaves two four-line attachments
claims.statement: For four identical unit charges at level two, fix the positive elementary half-exchange to act by \(+i\). On the deepest link \(V=H^2K\) the label permutations act as \(\mathbf1\oplus\operatorname{sgn}\). Among the labelled quotients \(P_W\), exactly the two character lines have an equivariant structure extending the fixed enhancement on the open. A transposition acts by \(+1\) or \(-1\) on the respective closed stalk.
hypotheses: Take the normal slice of four ordered points modulo translation and the trivial action on the fibre of \(d-\tfrac12d\log\Delta\) under relabelling. The phase \(+i\) is the open half-braid. The two signs are stabilizer actions at the collision.

claims.title: Ordinary coarse pullback singles out the trivial line
claims.statement: Let \(\pi:X\to X/S_4\) be the ordinary coarse quotient. Among the two equivariant members of the labelled family, only \(P_{\mathbf1}\) is an ordinary inverse image with the prescribed linearization. It equals \(\pi^*\bar j_{!*}\bar L[3]\). The pullback counit is the inclusion of the stabilizer invariants on each stalk. At the origin it misses the nonzero sign stalk of the other member.
hypotheses: Selection of a physical coefficient by this criterion assumes that it belongs to the stated family, has the fixed \(+i\) open enhancement and is an ordinary coarse pullback. Equivariance alone imposes the two-line alternative.

claims.title: Two independently rooted four-input vacuum sewings agree
claims.statement: In their common strict convergence region, the two original four-positive-input Virasoro sewings with vacuum at infinity agree after the prescribed channel transform. The equality holds as a map on one finite Hilbert tensor stage for all four original inputs, including every finite vacuum descendant test.
hypotheses: Use the positive square roots, local coordinates, external phases and the original positive input modules. Uniformity for the graph norms of independently completed composites requires a different bound.

claims.title: The integrated reflected heat two-jet vanishes at positive level
claims.statement: For the fixed-adjoint coefficient on the specified smooth two-source reflected Ward family, put \(g=|\kappa|^2/4>0\). In units of \(du\wedge d\phi/(16\pi)\) the three local neutral mixed contributions are \((-\log(1+g)/g,\log(1+g)/g,0)\). The integrated two-jet vanishes. On a common interval satisfying the uniform gap conditions the relative finite-part germ is divisible by \((\lambda_+\lambda_-)^2\).
hypotheses: Fix \(q=e^{-2\pi}\) and the prescribed source Fourier characters and adjoint. The quartic neutral coefficient, general sources, zero-level remainder and gravitational cap are separate comparisons.

claims.title: Two compact Kummer chart roots have the same overlap ratio
claims.statement: On the opposite-sheet overlap of the marked Kummer charts, the ratio of the second ordered root frame to the first is \(-1/2\) in the prescribed coordinates, and its square is \(1/4\). The cotangent determinant root and the cubic-chart root have the same transport, in both extension orders.
hypotheses: Take the common determinant refinement and the chart coordinate \(t=-x_2\). To compare a separately prescribed compact root one must also compute its downstairs holonomies on the common elliptic translation torsor.

claims.title: A nodal cubic pole distinguishes the third and fourth normal cuts
claims.statement: At the charge-two node, on the specified ordinary jet \(R/(u^p,D)\), the possible evaluations of a map to the moment–Cauchy complex form \(\ker(u^{p-1}:T\to T)\). The full cubic rational representative cannot lift on the third cut and has a strict lift on the fourth with both odd directions retained.
hypotheses: On the stated finite jet keep the moment complex, both residual odd directions and the actual field graph. The cubic obstruction at the third cut uses the universal coefficient \(2t_1t_2(t_1+t_2)q^3\beta^{-3}\) or its nonzero specialization. The cubic vanishes where this coefficient specializes to zero. The independently oriented full flag map before direct image remains open.

claims.title: A cross-marked Ward derivative detects a relative class
claims.statement: For a \(p\)-derivative on the first label and a current derivative on the second, the projected and full Ward defects agree on the specified two-label test. Their coefficient is \(-(-1)^j\hbar\partial_z^{i+j}C_1(t_2-t_1,z_1-z_2)\). It represents the nonzero degree-two connecting class of the quotient product in the supported complex.
hypotheses: Use polynomial level or a nonzero numerical level, the indicated normal derivatives and support. The cone inclusion of the defect is exact, while the corrected relative lift is nonzero. Other multispectator operations require their own tests.

claims.title: Four trace-invisible compact deformations integrate polynomially
