claims.statement: On the fixed K3 cup algebra, choose the stipulated totally isotropic two-plane perpendicular to the marked fibre and section. Its symmetric cubes give a four-dimensional family of polynomial associative multiplications with the same fibre-marked row, full pairing and multiplication traces. Suitable middle insertions distinguish them.
hypotheses: Keep the fixed ordinary identification, unit and cap scalars. This integrates the chosen isotropic family. The fixed-coordinate four-state equation decides integrability for arbitrary marked cubics. Identifying an independently prepared compact operation is additional data.

claims.title: Four simple spectator bounds give strict charge-six vanishing
claims.statement: For the original signed four-spectator residue complex at \(\mu=1\) with all four positive bounds one, \(H^n(D_{4,6})=0\) for \(n<6\) and every nonnegative spectator-pair bound. At five marks the one-selected degree-three group vanishes, removing the last possible contribution below total degree six.
hypotheses: Use the full polynomial spectator base, the pure, pair and triple lower amplitudes and the original first-residue injection. The common scalar recovers the named nonnegative bounds from the zero-pair-bound computation.

claims.title: Energy floors control completion and cellularity on unbounded complexes
claims.statement: For an algebraically energy-graded smooth positive-current complex let \(b_q\) be the lower energy floor of \(H^qX\). If \(b_{t-p}+p(p+1)/2\to+\infty\) for every fixed integer \(t\), then the actual smooth unit and the intrinsic derived-torsion counit are invertible. In particular \(X\) belongs to the subcategory generated by the shifted trivial cells.
hypotheses: Use the smooth positive \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) current algebra. If floors are required only in sufficiently low cohomological degrees, assume the other layers are joint torsion for the counit conclusion. Arbitrary Postnikov maps and multiplicities are allowed.

claims.title: Arbitrary pointings in recognized native actor families
claims.statement: The two recognition maps are inverse on full pointing spaces for genuine-unit main-diagonal Chevalley actors and their module-radical extensions. They also recover every pointing on the given unbounded nonunital commutative dg actors with connection and the nonunital Chevalley actors admitting the stipulated horizontal singleton representative.
hypotheses: The question for an arbitrary unbounded coassociative actor asks whether the same inverse transports root changes and higher mixed collisions on the actual presheaf.

claims.title: Opposite Jordan charges leave a collision datum invisible to finite jets
claims.statement: Let \(Av_2=v_1\), \(Av_1=0\) and \(B=-A\). Although the total charge vanishes, the original first-pole endpoint section has off-diagonal differential \(h^{-1}\delta_0v_1\). Every finite normal Taylor projection kills the relevant localized class. A geometric endpoint comparison must carry this attachment across separation and collision together with the cap.
hypotheses: Use the full supported/separated diagram and the actual Jordan charge representations. Comparing finite numerical charge fibres or their finite Taylor jets alone misses this row.

claims.title: Reconstructing Heisenberg endpoints with their cap
claims.statement: Construct an equivalence from independently defined, unaugmented geometric endpoint modules at finite numerical and Jordan charges to the polynomial varying-vacuum relative bar. It must intertwine the collision and separation maps, full mapping complexes, polynomial vacuum, cap and higher coherences.
hypotheses: The separated Laurent primitive that cancels a particular binary defect has its own regular-energy continuity condition. The cancelling Jordan pair tests the full topological attachment.

claims.title: Associativity on independently completed Virasoro composite fields
claims.statement: Compare the two genuine four-input rootings after each inner pair has already been completed in its own image topology. The prescribed intertwiner must preserve the meromorphic and vacuum components, both units and the next gluing on a common stage. Positive projection can kill nonzero vacuum data.
hypotheses: Keep the actual inner and outer coordinate domains, the independent incoming graph norm and every admitted descendant test. Equality for original positive modules supplies a test case.

claims.title: The prescribed Cauchy lifts fail at nonzero level
claims.statement: For every \(N\ge2\) and every nonzero numerical level \(K\), the original Cauchy lifts in the vacuum-normalized all-arity mode algebra fail both same-half RTT relations and the centered mixed relation modulo \(\hbar^3\). Their respective residues are \(K/[3y^2z^2(y-z)]\), \(K/[3(y-z)]\) and \(K/[3yz(y-z)]\). At \(N=2,\ K=-2,\ y=1,\ z=2\) the mixed residue is \(1/3\). Reduction excludes an all-order map with these generator images. At level zero they give compatible proper injections in every rank at every finite precision and in the \(\hbar\)-adic limit, both before and after vacuum normalization. Classical PBW gives injectivity wherever the map exists, while the two-point pole forces proper image.
hypotheses: The field coproduct has a different recipient. The obstruction uses the original generator images, the centered spectral shifts, local-vacuum normalization and division of each RTT defect by \(\hbar^2\) before truncation. The level-splitting coproduct takes values in modes on a joint configuration. Comparing its target with separately integrated modes must account for the cross-diagonal poles.

claims.title: A marked higher Heisenberg realization on a complex surface
claims.statement: On \(\mathbb C^2\) the paired higher Heisenberg coalgebra under the occupied vacuum has an associative full-cut cobar and a pro-perfect dual for the transposed cut tensor. Its compact Dolbeault–Spencer realization compares to the independently specified paired smooth Gaussian observables through all finite insertions.
hypotheses: Use the oriented holomorphic volume, finite-dimensional paired degree-zero labels, the declared shifts and the Gaussian covariance \(\hbar\kappa\). Identifying the singular field or line category requires the supported operations on its own boundary.

claims.title: A calibrated transverse moment agrees with the normal residue
claims.statement: For the normalized Bochner–Martinelli current \(T_d\) in complex dimension \(d\ge2\), the expanding circular normal moment with weight \(w^m/m!\) acts on \(\partial_{\rm tan}^a\partial_w^bT_d\) as \(\delta_{mb}(-1)^b\partial_{\rm tan}^aT_{d-1}\). It agrees with the correspondingly calibrated Laurent residue, including its supported boundary.
hypotheses: Use the ordered fibre-simplex map, its dimension-dependent normalizations and the circular prescription. At \(d=2,m=2,b=0\) a noncircular exhaustion can add a nonzero smooth antiholomorphic term.

claims.title: Reversal changes the sign of a regulated five-wheel
claims.statement: On the coefficient oscillator put \(R=x^{\rm degree}\), \(H=A_{-qp}\), \(E=A_{q^2/2}\) and \(F=A_{-p^2/2}\). Then \(\operatorname{Tr}(RH^3EF)=-\operatorname{Tr}(RH^3FE)=x(1+10x+x^2)/(1-x)^6\). For \(x=e^{-t}\) the leading coefficient is \(12t^{-6}\).
hypotheses: This is the ordered coefficient trace of quadratic Hamiltonians. To obtain a spacetime string wheel or an independently prepared boundary state one also needs its physical graph weight, orientation, bulk insertion and support.

claims.title: A lower-spin D3 component carries a second-page Bockstein
claims.statement: At the indicated rank-two D3 multiplicity of highest weight one in charge \(q=3\), the three graded torsion summands have lengths \(1,2,1\). Their filtration Bocksteins occur on pages one, two and one. Retaining only the largest-spin summand loses the middle torsion block.
hypotheses: Use the formal polynomial-parameter module before specialization, the reduced rank-two sector and the fixed multiplicity \(r=1\). The physical bulk-to-defect realization has additional operator and sewing data.

claims.title: The geometric section state has an untraced cubic
claims.statement: For the elliptic K3 section class \(C\) at reduced coefficient \((C,1,0)\), the relative Donaldson–Thomas pants pairing on all of \(H^*(S,\mathbb Q)\) is the cubic \(q(C,-)^{\otimes3}\). It comes from the oriented proper boundary kernel. A normalized numerical trace introduces the usual multiple-cover weights only after this operation.
hypotheses: Fix the full Poincaré pairing, cup unit, marking and cap scalars. Identifying the cubic with a protected physical state requires independent preparation and compatible sewing.

claims.title: A quantitative enlargement of a complete positive Weil window
claims.statement: Let \(c=7.0942\times10^{-109}\), \(R=2\exp(10^7/c)\) and \(d=c/(10^5R)\). On every interval of width at most \((31/10)(1+d)\) the complete form obeys \(Q(g)\ge(c/2)\|g\|_2^2\) for every complex \(L^2\) vector, allowing extended value \(+\infty\). This gives an explicit increase over the certified width \(31/10\).
hypotheses: Use zero extension, the original prime-power, real-place and polar terms, and the fixed width-\(31/10\) lower bound \(c\). The claim concerns the entire window, including vectors outside finite-dimensional projections.

claims.title: Positive Weil form on two shrinking windows
claims.statement: For every integer \(n\ge2\), take independent complex functions on intervals centred at \(0\) and \(\log n\) of common width \(0<w\le\min(2^{-19},1/(2n))\). The complete Weil form on their sum is bounded below by \(1-2/e-2^{-9}\) times the sum of their squared \(L^2\) norms. The fixed width \(2^{-19}\) works through \(n=262144\).
hypotheses: Use form-domain functions on the occupied pair of intervals and retain all prime-power and polar terms. No condition is imposed on a single larger connected interval by this inequality.

claims.title: The sharp Hölder threshold for a local Fourier expansion
claims.statement: Let \(E\) be a Banach space over \(\mathbb C_p\). For first-difference \(\alpha\)-Hölder functions \(f:\mathbb Z_p\to E\) with \(\alpha>1\), the normalized Haar integral is representative independent and the inverse expansion indexed by \(\mathbb Q_p/\mathbb Z_p\) converges uniformly. At \(|\xi|=p^m\ge p\), \(\|\widehat f(\xi)\|\le p^\alpha[f]_\alpha p^{-(\alpha-1)m}\). The exponent is sharp on the Hölder unit ball. For \(0<\alpha\le1\) the entire class admits no normalized translation-invariant scalar integral.
hypotheses: Use \(|p|_p=p^{-1}\), a character of conductor \(\mathbb Z_p\), fixed compatible roots of unity and nonarchimedean norms. Bounded coefficient maps intertwine. The global integral chiral comparison has another source.

claims.title: The target cardinality filtration splits additively
claims.statement: For the explicit algebraic general-exchange integral \(G\), the layer of cardinality \(r\) is equivalent to \((D_r)_{h\Sigma_r}\) with its lifted exchange action. The exhaustive cardinality filtration splits additively up to quasi-isomorphism and its spectral sequence degenerates at the first page. Products still have lower-arity collision contacts.
hypotheses: Use the punctured affine line in characteristic zero, an ordinary flat state module over the original base with free vacuum summand, Laurent-polynomial finite-state exchange, arbitrary finite normal orders, direct-sum totalization and the isolated empty unit. This splitting is on the target integral.

claims.title: A single M5 propagator fixes opposite raw and connected signs
claims.statement: Use one native positive Wilson insertion and one positive chiral surface source. At nonzero separation \(y=w_{\rm line}-w_{\rm surf}\) the raw bilinear pairing is \(-e\,j(x)/(4\pi^2 y)\) and the connected Gaussian exchange is \(+\hbar e\,j(x)/(4\pi^2 y)\).
hypotheses: Take the increasing temporal orientation, specified complex volume, \(dz/(2\pi i)\) surface measure, positive-action convention and prescribed heat limits. Distinct supports keep this one-edge term separate from a contact at coincidence.

claims.title: Weight-zero base change kills a unit-good critical telescope
claims.statement: At raw critical level the quadratic energy-two vector in the universal affine vacuum is invariant under horizontal and positive currents. Its nonzero PBW symbol makes iterated right multiplication injective. The resulting telescope has zero derived weight-zero base change and nonzero derived ghost-quotient base change, and its original unit is invertible under the native adjunction.
hypotheses: Use the actual quadratic current and its strictly lower-bounded source representative. Other explicitly constructed critical telescopes lie in the realization kernel. The two base changes and the identity of the chosen telescope are essential.

claims.title: The two coupled four-point flags have distinct images
claims.statement: On the open four-point configuration let \(M=N_a(r)\otimes(W,d-J\,d\log(t-r))\), with \(N_a\) the specified rank-two slope-two angular connection and \(W\) two-dimensional with one nonzero nilpotent Jordan block \(J\). In the simultaneous defect \(C=\operatorname{Cone}(j_!M\to j_*M)\), the flags through \(r=1\) and \(t=r\) are the shifted duals of the two formal restrictions after restriction to the same \(234\) collision germ. With the same marked source, their second-minus-first difference has ranks \((0,1,3,2)\) at \(a=0\) and \((0,0,2,2)\) at \(a\ne0\) in degrees \(1,0,-1,-2\) of \(i^!C[1]\). The joint ranks \((1,5,8,4)\) and \((0,2,6,4)\) equal those of the boundary from the punctured \(234\) line.
hypotheses: Use algebraic holonomic operations over \(\mathbb C\), \(\mathrm{DR}(\mathcal O_{\mathbb A^3})=\mathbb C[3]\), the ordinary outer star link, the horizontal frame at \(r=1\) and the labelled logarithms in a common positive real chamber. The independent sectorial comparison and other flags require more data.

claims.title: The marked vacuum quartic vanishes at shifted level −3/2
claims.statement: For the universal principal \(W^k(\mathfrak{sl}_4)\) vacuum at \(k+4=-3/2\), the only potential higher entry in the marked normalized minimal model is \(b_4(sa,sa,sa,su)=\gamma\,s(az)\). Its unnormalized four-input Lie antisymmetrization is \(6\gamma\,s(az)\). The actual \((-1)\)-modes on all smooth weak coefficients identify the commutator dg Lie algebra of the graded-opposite derived endomorphisms up to quasi-isomorphism with a Lie algebra whose commutators land in the acyclic translation ideal. Consequently \(\gamma=0\). The associative vacuum endomorphism dg algebra is formal, the Hochschild characteristic map is onto, and ordinary associative formality transports to the other three exceptional fibres.
hypotheses: The quartic evaluation itself uses the marked affine reduction and the integrated \(2\theta^\vee\) orbit at \(k+4=-3/2\). Reciprocal vertex-algebra equivalence and complementary duality of the compact shifted vacuum transport the underlying associative result, with opposite composition where required. Explicit two-sided representatives now exist on the original coefficients for the marked degree-nine negative and degree-twelve positive classes. The comparison of separately pinned reductions requires additional data.

claims.title: Sharp nilpotence over the real and complex K3 markings
claims.statement: On \(E=\langle C,F\rangle^\perp\) in the marked zero-scalar stratum, the traceless commutative associative middle multiplication preserves a nondegenerate symmetric form of Witt index \(w\). If \(m=\min(\dim E,2w+1)\), then \(E^{m+1}=0\) and a law on this form attains \(E^m\ne0\). Here \(\dim E=20\). The given rational and real marking has \(w=2\), while the complexified form has \(w=10\). The cyclic degeneration of \(z^{21}-s\) attains \(E^{20}\ne0\) at zero in the reduced closure of the complex étale stratum. Its orthogonal orbit splits into two \(SO(g)\)-orbits. Their closures are distinct components of dimension \(190\) in that reduced zero fibre. Every regular trace word and every inserted positive-genus scalar agrees with the section throughout the zero-scalar locus. On the complementary locus a torus with the point insertion determines the scalar \(k\), and three marked middle insertions determine the cubic on \(E\).
hypotheses: Fix the rational 24-state cup coordinates, grading, unit, pairing, cap scalars, fibre row and first multiplication traces. On the zero-scalar stratum the nilpotent middle algebra has no unit. The torus formulas use the integrated product over a characteristic-zero field with formal parameter \(t\), point class \(p\), and arbitrary marked insertions. The nonzero-scalar reconstruction uses all middle triples. Scalar extension of a given real law preserves its sixfold identity. Other components, multiplicities and independent compact-state preparations remain open.

claims.title: Higher transport at the binary collision on the sphere
claims.statement: For two ordered points on \(C=\mathbb P^1(\mathbb C)\), write \(i\) for the diagonal, \(j\) for its complement, \(p\) for the first projection from that complement and \(q:S(TC)\to C\) for the unit tangent circle bundle. Then \(i^*Rj_*p^*L\simeq Rq_*q^*L\) on perfect complex local systems. For graded stalk basis \(e_0,e_1,e_2\) and flat superconnection \(d+\omega N_c\) with \(N_ce_2=e_1\), \(N_ce_1=ce_0\), the positive generator of \(\pi_2(C)\) acts from degree two to degree one by \(\left(\begin{smallmatrix}c&0\\2&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)\). The remaining differential takes \(e_2+\vartheta e_1/2\) to \(-c\gamma e_0/2\). In degrees zero through five the global ranks are \((1,1,1,1,1,1)\) at \(c=0\) and \((1,1,0,0,1,1)\) at \(c=1\).
hypotheses: Use the normal \(v_2-v_1\), positive angular form of fibre integral one, normalized complex area \(\int_C\omega=1\), \(d\vartheta=-2q^*\omega\) and \(\gamma=\vartheta\wedge q^*\omega\). The source basis is \((e_1\otimes\theta,e_2\otimes1)\) and the target basis is \((e_0\otimes\theta,e_1\otimes1)\). Take the southern horizontal frame minus the northern one along the equator, oriented as the boundary of the northern hemisphere.

For the same constant open coefficient and diagonal \(\mathbb C[-3]\), the zero and orientation attachments give extraordinary global ranks \((1,1,1,1)\) and \((1,0,0,1)\) in degrees \(1,3,4,5\). An all-arity factorization algebra requires compatible operations and a vacuum.

claims.title: Harmonic transfer on a sourced affine meridian collar
claims.statement: On the \(q=1/2\) solid torus take the source defined by \(F=zA(u)\), \(u=\log r\), \(A=e^{i\lambda f(u)}\), with small real \(\lambda\) and smooth periodic \(f\) constant near both ends. The closed weight-two scalar \(F^{M-2}(\partial_zF)^2\) at \(M\ge2\) gives the outer-to-inner transfer \(R_M=e^{-ML}(A(u_0)/A(u_1))^M\) for \(L=u_1-u_0\) in separately fixed angular frames. Cyclic homotopy correction extends the geometric pullback to the affine Hessian on smooth finite rotation modes. In a transported finite gauge and density the radial Gaussian scalar is source-independent.
hypotheses: The global Ward source has source-free end collars. The positive harmonic has deck multiplier \(q^M\) and lies on the cut shell. The cyclic correction preserves radial support and uses an angular Green operator.

With the supplied positive Virasoro vacuum marks at \(c>25\), put \(\eta=e^{-L-i\lambda(f_1-f_0)}\). The two ordered weight-five measurements are \(4c\eta^5\) and \(14c\eta^5\), and the orthogonalized weight-six measurement is \(62c\eta^6/7\). A separately fixed one- or five-mode measure gives additional results for specified interior Ward fillings. The comparison of full regulators with the compact cap remains open.

claims.title: Two-sided classical affine flux and the on-shell Ward action
claims.statement: On a sufficiently small radial Ward deformation, a positive solution normalized at the outer end and a relative negative solution normalized at the inner end give the increasing-radius, negative-first flux \(c_MR_M\) on a nonflat intermediate meridian. Their conserved current is \((2\pi i)^{-1}(dz-\mu)\wedge ab\). For the raw negative harmonic \(c_M=-(2M-4)!!/(2M-3)!!\). With \(s=A^{\prime}/A\), \(h=1+s/2\), the classical critical action changes by \((\kappa/32)\int(4s^2/h+(s^{\prime})^2/h^3)\,du\). A returning twist can change the action at fixed end transfer.
hypotheses: Use \(q=1/2\), nonzero \(\kappa\) and the original complex-bilinear pairing. The smooth periodic radial profile is close to one, with \(\partial_z(zA)\ne0\), monotonically increasing reparametrized log radius of positive derivative and rigid unit-modulus end collars. The two solutions are prepared on their own halves.

These calculations concern a marked classical flux and saddle action. On a chosen finite subspace the two individual half-densities, signed gluing integral and a relative filling phase can also be specified. The continuum measure and its absolute cap phase remain separate.

claims.title: Prepared K3 states and cubic trinion measurements
claims.statement: For the marked elliptic K3 let \(E=\langle C,F\rangle^\perp\subset H^2(S,K)\), of dimension twenty. A weighted isotropic rank-one deformation changes the diagonal trinion at a middle state \(x\) by \(t\lambda q(u,x_E)^3\). Freely available projections in \(S_0\subset E\) distinguish all such rivals from the fixed reference exactly when \(S_0^\perp\) is anisotropic. If each probe must be null in \(E\), the sharp counts over \(\mathbb Q,\mathbb R,\mathbb C\) are \(3,3,19\). For all weighted cubics on a known totally isotropic \(r\)-space \(U\subset E\), precisely \(\binom{r+2}{3}\) fixed readings recover the cubic. Connected positive-genus scalar sewings in these families agree with the reference.
hypotheses: Use a characteristic-zero field and formal \(t\), the ordinary K3 cup product, marked section and fibre and independently fixed scalar reference. For a generally restricted linear preparation space with unrestricted states in it, recovering the known-\(U\) cubic requires and suffices that \(S_0\to U^*\) be onto.
The original 20-dimensional rational marking has real signature \((2,18)\) and rational Witt index two. Physical or Hall preparations and the oriented trinion require independent constructions.

claims.title: Null lifts and pairwise identification of weighted K3 cubics
claims.statement: Over \(\mathbb Q\) and \(\mathbb R\), two ordinary square-zero middle states suffice and are necessary to distinguish every isotropic rank-one rival from the reference when the probes may lie in all \(H^2(S)\). The states \(C+e_i+f_i\) for the two marked hyperbolic pairs have non-null projections to \(E=\langle C,F\rangle^\perp\). To identify an arbitrary unknown weighted rank-one tensor against every other such tensor, exactly twenty fixed diagonal readings are necessary and sufficient over either field, even with the probes null in \(E\).
hypotheses: Tensors, including their scalar weights, are the unknowns. An arbitrary available null basis of \(E\) determines all the linear pairings up to a common factor because cubing is injective over \(\mathbb Q\) and \(\mathbb R\). Over \(\mathbb C\) the lower bound remains twenty, one rational null basis fails, and the optimal pairwise count is open.

Over \(\mathbb C\), let \(\zeta\) be a primitive cube root of unity. The unit-weight directions \(e_1+e_2\) and \(e_1+\zeta e_2\) give identical readings on one rational null basis. At the additional null probe \(f_1+f_2\) their cubed pairings are \(8\) and \(-1\).
claims.sourceLabel: Chapter 15, “Which preparations detect a cubic on K3 cohomology?”

claims.title: An independently normalized finite quantum measure on a nonflat meridian
claims.statement: Two solid-torus Ward fillings agree near every face, corner and cut and have equal critical actions on each half. A fixed compact current and conjugate give bulk couplings \(B_1=1-i\epsilon,\ B_2=B_R=1\). Fix the two oriented input frames and independent half-densities. For one frequency-five meridian pair the sewn moment is \(Z_{j;k,\ell}=e^{-S_{\rm cl}/\hbar}\delta_{k\ell}(-\hbar)^k k!/(B_jB_R)\). At \(\epsilon=1/8\) the ratio of the two unnormalized vacua is \((64+8i)/65\) with phase \(\arctan(1/8)\). Sampling both dilation-related bulk supports exchanges the two diagonal couplings and gives ratio one.
hypotheses: Use \(q=1/2,\ \kappa\ne0,\ \hbar>0\), a common nonflat meridian, source-free exterior collars and the same oriented classical boundary primitives. The sources differ in disjoint interior patches in the left half. The fixed bulk contour is \(x=w,\ y=\bar w\). The negative-first Green pairing calibrates the seam, whose signed contour is \(b=-\bar a\).

For five frequencies \(2,\ldots,6\) use compact charges \(\pm17\), the product half-densities and the prescribed positive Virasoro identification, \(c>25\). If \(L\) is the collar width, the unnormalized ordered and projected stress values are \(Z_{\rm vac}\) times \(4ce^{-5L},\,14ce^{-5L},\,(62c/7)e^{-6L}\). The regulator is fixed before comparing the fillings. The full sourced boundary measure, its continuum limit and absolute cap phase are open.

claims.title: Two-sided characteristic cocycles on the exceptional coefficient resolution
claims.statement: For \(y=v_-\) in degree nine at \(\tau=k+4=-3/2\), or \(y=z_+\) in degree twelve at \(\tau=3/2\), the original endomorphism algebra of the BRST coefficient functor admits explicit normalized regular-bimodule Hochschild cocycles in every arity. They have \(F_0=sO_y\), \(F_1(sQ)=-|y|\,sO_y\) and \(F_1(sT)=(-1)^{|y|}sO_{H_cy}\), where \(T=[Q,H_c]\). Both endpoint compositions occur. Graded commutativity and the absence of cohomology in the higher obstruction degrees suffice for these two generators.
hypotheses: Use the universal principal \(W^k(\mathfrak{sl}_4)\) and all smooth weak coefficients. In the negative raw ghost basis \(\delta_2=-\gamma_2/\tau\), the signed primitive deletes the spin-two letter with multiplier \(2/3\). Its first coefficient is \(122031\bmod 1000003\). On the positive fibre the specified vacuum-matter Cartan coefficients are exactly \(+1\) for \(a_+=h_{3,0}\) and \(-1\) for \(z_+\).

For the positive affine three-class, previously established fixed-fibre associative formality gives consistency of a \(31\times41\) system of rank nine. Two fixed diagonal minors have determinant \(+1\). Three arity-two and six arity-three native values suffice. Their numerical evaluations, a native cochain for the extra degree-eight class and identification of the separately normalized reduction maps remain open.

claims.title: Ordered spectral cuts of the chiral cotangent Yangian
claims.statement: The level-zero coproduct and independent translations of its outputs give polynomial maps \(C_{\mathbf s}:V\to V^{\otimes n}[\mathbf s]\) preserving every vertex product. A refinement adds the local position to the position of its parent. For complex simple \(\mathfrak g\), ordinary Zhu reduction of \(V\) with its unshifted coproduct gives the dense polynomial cotangent Yangian at graded evaluation \(\hbar=1\) as a bialgebra.
hypotheses: Finite-dimensional Lie algebra in characteristic zero, rational splitting at spectral infinity, universal vertex envelope at level zero.
The vertex coordinate and the Yangian spectral variable are independent.

claims.title: A field-valued double pole and its derivative
claims.statement: For \(X=T^{(1)}\), the double pole of \(K_{E_{12}u}(z)L_{E_{21}}(w)\) is \(\chi=X_{22}-X_{11}\). Its simple pole contains \(\partial_z\chi\) in addition to the algebroid current. Colliding inputs one and three first, then applying the middle current \(L_{E_{12}}\), gives \(2X_{21}\).
hypotheses: Level-zero matrix vertex algebra for \(GL_2\), with the first insertion minus the second as pole coordinate.
For the three-current residue, expand in \(|z_1-z_3|<|z_2-z_3|\) and take the double-pole coefficient before the simple-pole coefficient.

claims.title: The ordered cuts differ at coincidence
claims.statement: Reversing the two loop factors changes their second matrix coefficient by \([A_1,A_2]\), where \(A_i\) is the first jet of the corresponding loop. Thus an intertwiner of the two ordered field actions, with the output flip removed, cannot be regular at coincidence and equal the identity there on the whole regular vacuum tensor.
hypotheses: Level-zero matrix algebra for \(GL_N\), \(N\ge2\), on two copies of the universal regular vacuum module.
The normalization at spectral coincidence is imposed on the entire tensor product.

claims.title: Framed scattering on the mini-twistor sheet
claims.statement: There is a rank-two meromorphic sheet of Hecke type \((1,-1)\) with scattering matrix \(T=I+Q/u\) and \(Q^2=0\). Two sheets compose by \(T_1T_2\). An incoming polynomial change of frame \(\xi\) induces the outgoing change \((T^{-1}\xi T)_+\), which recovers classical dressing from the transport.
hypotheses: Classical holomorphic-topological BF theory on the real correspondence space over \(\operatorname{Tot}_{\mathbb P^1}\mathcal O(2)\).
Framed ends, a single allowed spectral pole at zero and identity normalization at spectral infinity.

claims.title: The crossed celestial residue excludes the marked map
claims.statement: After evaluation at the identity negative loop and at a spectral point, the Poisson bracket of two Cartan-torus-invariant symbols in the cotangent vertex algebra has no quadratic part. It cannot reproduce the surviving crossed quadratic simple pole of the commuting flat \(\mathfrak{so}_8\) first jets of colours \(12,34\).
hypotheses: Level-zero marked regular polynomial WZW sector with fixed lower and mixed Ward operations.

The complete source residue retains its nonzero crossed projection after evaluation. The map preserves the common torus and the standard marking of the zero-jet colour currents, at any invariant target level.

claims.title: The intrinsic five-dimensional defect and its fusion
claims.statement: Does the five-dimensional theory determine nonabelian defect currents, their contact terms and their quantum fusion from its bulk fields and boundary conditions? With tangent Fermi matter and a prescribed current source, framed words of Hecke sheets detect every algebraic state for a complex simple gauge algebra. An intrinsic comparison must derive the matter and the source prescription, recover the ordered one-form under real-direction fusion and identify the corresponding global Ward identities.
hypotheses: The nonabelian holomorphic-topological theory is locally defined on \(\mathbb R_t\times\mathbb C_z\times\mathbb C_u\). Gauge and shift boundary conditions, the framings and the level must be specified.
The same normalization of the currents and subtraction of coincident insertions must apply on individual defects and across every successive fusion.
claims.sourceLabel: Cotangent matter on a framed Hecke sheet

claims.title: The Zhu kernel and the poles of composite fields
claims.statement: On an ordered PBW word with all coordinate modes on the left, a differentiated coordinate gives zero in the standard Zhu algebra. Otherwise replacing every current mode \(-n\) by \(-1\) multiplies the class by \((-1)^{\sum(n-1)}\). The current letters multiply in reverse order in the dressing smash product. The resulting kernel has leading terms \(C_2(V)\). From the vertex brackets and the level, the Wick formula computes every pole of a composite field.
hypotheses: The universal dressing vertex envelope over a characteristic-zero field, with functions of standard weight zero and polynomial currents of weight one, at any invariant level.
Algebraic states and finite arity. For a rational matrix coefficient, the output functional is supported in finitely many weights.
claims.sourceLabel: Chapter 12, “The Zhu projection and the poles of composite fields”

claims.title: The one-form in an ordered product of matrix loops
claims.statement: The correction to the coordinate-current coproduct on \(n\) loop factors is a sum over ordered pairs \(i<j\) of products of the transported spectral and vertex derivatives. Every parenthesization gives the same sum. For \(P=I+E_{12}u^{-r}\) and \(Q=I+zE_{21}u^{-s}\) the whole correction to \(\Delta K\) is \(NrE_{11}u^{-r-s-1}\). Its first nonzero coefficient can therefore occur at any order \(k\ge3\).
hypotheses: The level-zero universal matrix vertex algebra for \(GL_N\), with the coordinate functions normally ordered on the left. The example uses \(N\ge2\) and \(r,s\ge1\).
The vertex variable \(z\) and the spectral variable \(u\) are independent. Each Laurent coefficient involves a finite sum.
claims.sourceLabel: Chapter 12, “The one-form in an ordered product of loops”

claims.title: Two sphere block algebras of one vertex bialgebra
claims.statement: For the standard coordinate action with twist \(\theta\), the one-point vacuum blocks form the graded completion of the affine vertex centre at level \(-\theta K\). For the mini-twistor action the two chart Ward identities give a different convolution. Its degree \(-2\) blocks contain two elements whose commutator in degree \(-4\) has leading symbol detected by \(4K(c,[a,b])\). This convolution is noncommutative for every twist.
hypotheses: The chiral cotangent Yangian at chiral level zero for a complex simple Lie algebra \(\mathfrak g\) with nonzero invariant form \(K\). The affine level \(-\theta K\) belongs to the description of the standard block algebra.

The sphere has one vacuum insertion. In the mini-twistor coordinate action \(u\) is a fibre coordinate of \(\mathcal O(2)\), and the dual is completed in spectral degree. The symbol is evaluated on \(a,b,c\in\mathfrak g\).
claims.sourceLabel: Chapter 12, “Two sphere algebras of the chiral cotangent Yangian”

claims.title: The RTT Yangian on consecutive configurations
claims.statement: Attach one copy of the RTT Yangian to each maximal run of equal consecutive positions. Adjacent runs merge by ordered multiplication. The resulting bar factorizes across separating cuts, and the Yangian coproduct induces a counital, coassociative map to two copies at the same positions. Its flat Hopf deformation over \(\mathbb C[h,t]\) has independent first variations of the bracket and cobracket. Their composite is nonzero on a rank-two current.
hypotheses: Word configurations on \(\mathbb A^1_{\mathbb C}\), with the same-position tensor obtained by taking the extraordinary tensor of the two bars before cobar. The occupied singleton carries the RTT Yangian \(Y(\mathfrak{gl}_N)\).

The polynomial family is generated by \(X_{ij}^{(r)}=h^rt^{r-1}t_{ij}^{(r)}\), with \(t_{ij}^{(r)}\) the ordinary RTT modes. The full Yangian occurs at \(h=t=1\). The nonzero composite uses \(N\ge2\).
claims.sourceLabel: Chapter 12, “Consecutive collisions of RTT Yangian states”

claims.title: The outer collision distinguishes a word from an unordered configuration
claims.statement: At \((x,y,x)\) with \(x\ne y\), three consecutive runs remain and the three-point bar is smooth along \(z_1=z_3\). Factorization across \(\{1,3\}\mid\{2\}\) would place the singular two-point bar there. The same bar therefore cannot satisfy factorization across that partition.
hypotheses: The bar determined by consecutive runs of equal positions, with the RTT Yangian as singleton coefficient. Its adjacent product has a nonzero kernel containing \(1\otimes a-a\otimes1\) for any nonscalar state \(a\).
claims.sourceLabel: Chapter 12, “Consecutive collisions of RTT Yangian states”

claims.title: A Cartan twist of the rational Yangian fields
claims.statement: On three marked colours a Cartan twist changes the signed ratio of the two simple poles of \(J_{12},J_{23}\) at \(h=0\) to \(e^{-3\eta}\). With \(h\) the rational Yangian parameter, the exchange residue in the \(H_1\otimes J_{13}\) component is \(he^{-\eta}+O(h^2)\), where \(H_1=E_{11}-E_{22}\). The level-additive field coproduct lands in the transported tensor with cross contractions. Removing the tensor marking gives a monoidal equivalence on positive Yangian modules.
hypotheses: The divided determinant-one rational quantum affine vacuum of rank three at numerical level \(K\), over \(\mathbb C[[h,\eta]]\), with products taken at each finite parameter precision.
The twist multiplies states of charges \(\alpha,\beta\) by \(\exp(\eta\alpha_1\beta_2)\), using \(H_1\) and \(H_2=E_{22}-E_{33}\) to measure charge.
claims.sourceLabel: Chapter 12, “Two parameters in the rational Yangian fields”

claims.title: A critical-level coefficient of the double Yangian vacuum
claims.statement: In the type-A double Yangian vacuum, the field of a creation word translates its current parameters by the vertex coordinate and multiplies by the inverse shifted annihilation matrix. At the critical level \(K=-N\), the vacuum component of the mixed root entry \(A_{12}(p)B_{21}(v)\mathbf1\) is exactly \(-N/((p-v)^2-N^2\hbar^2/4)\).
hypotheses: The normalized general-linear RTT double of rank \(N\ge2\), completed in \(\hbar\), with \(T=I+\hbar A\) and \(T^+=I-\hbar B\). The expansion is at \(p=\infty\).
The two currents act on the universal vacuum module in a fixed formal coordinate.
claims.sourceLabel: Chapter 12, “A vacuum field of the double Yangian”

claims.title: The charge-dependent tensor of cotangent currents
claims.statement: Weight the number of currents by a Rees parameter \(h\) and twist fields of root charges \(a,b\) by \(F(a,b)=q^{B(a,b)}\). The residue bar factorizes across consecutive cuts. Its cobar has a same-position coproduct with middle exchange \(\chi(a,b)=F(a,b)/F(b,a)\). In rank three the ordered simple poles of \(J_{12},J_{23}\) have coefficients \(hqJ_{13}\) and \(-hJ_{13}\). The graded coefficient categories are symmetric-monoidally equivalent.
hypotheses: The level-zero matrix chiral cotangent Yangian over the polynomial Rees ring with \(q\) invertible. \(B\) is integral and bilinear on the root lattice. The displayed poles use \(B(a,b)=a_1b_2\) in the simple-root basis.
The external group algebra of the root lattice supplies the charge exchanges. The coproduct is defined on the regular lattices of the residue construction.
claims.sourceLabel: Chapter 12, “A two-parameter coproduct for the cotangent currents”

claims.title: A pole obstructs the ordinary tensor for coloured currents
claims.statement: Let \(x,y\) be the \(21,32\) entries of the first negative-loop coefficient. For the prescribed coproduct on a singleton, an input regular at \(z_1=z_2\) acquires principal part \((1-q)y\otimes x/(z_1-z_2)\) in the ordinary same-position tensor. This obstructs that target already modulo \(\eta^2\) when \(q=e^\eta\). The middle charge exchange cancels the principal part.
hypotheses: Rank \(N\ge3\), level zero, the ordered binary collision lattice and the two adjacent simple-root charges with \(\chi=q\). The singleton coproduct and separated cut are fixed.
claims.sourceLabel: Chapter 12, “A two-parameter coproduct for the cotangent currents”

claims.title: A fixed-point double pole on the bosonic Hecke surface
claims.statement: Bulk BF transgression on the smooth rank-two Hecke orbit gives momenta with \(p_i(z)x^j(w)\sim\hbar\delta_i^j/(z-w)\). At \(Q=E_{12}\) the frame generator \(\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)+2uE_{21}\) fixes the orbit point and acts by \(2I\) on its tangent plane. Its bosonic current therefore has self double pole \(-8\hbar^2\). Every weight-one one-form improvement leaves this value fixed, whereas the corresponding level-zero dressing current has zero double pole.
hypotheses: Scattering \(T=I+Q/u\) and \(T^{-1}\) have only a simple pole, \(Q\ne0\) is nilpotent, and the real ends are framed. The electric representatives reach the ends.
The quantum current is a geometric lift of this frame action in the transgressed bosonic first-order surface theory.
claims.sourceLabel: Chapter 14, “An electric mode of the mini-twistor defect”

claims.title: Polar fluxes realize the abelian cotangent vertex bialgebra
claims.statement: The two towers of polar BF fluxes have regular mutual operator products. Their real-direction fusion is addition, by the flux integral over an enclosing sphere. In the stated normalization their differential polynomials form the entire level-zero \(GL_1\) chiral cotangent Yangian. The determinant and scalar currents give the corresponding central factor for \(GL_N\).
hypotheses: Free abelian holomorphic-topological BF theory with a normal boundary condition allowing both polar fluxes and arbitrary finite principal parts. The linear fluxes are paired with regular test modes.

This identifies the flux subalgebra of the surface observables. Over a reduced complex base a meromorphic \(GL_1\) scattering matrix invertible away from one support and based at infinity has determinant one.
claims.sourceLabel: Chapter 14, “Two fluxes on a meromorphic surface”

claims.title: The marked current on a coupled Hecke sheet
claims.statement: Write \(h=Q_{22}-Q_{11}\) and \(p=Q_{21}\) on the smooth nilpotent \(GL_2\) orbit. For \(K_{E_{12}u}\) against \(L_{E_{21}}\), the double pole is \(h\) and the simple pole contains \(Dh\) beyond the bracket current. The outer three-current residue is \(2p\). On two equal marked profiles the \(u^{-3}\) correction to the fused current is \(2Q\). On the profiles \(X=E_{12}\) and \(Y=zE_{21}\) it is \(2E_{11}\) in this order and \(-I\) in reverse order.
hypotheses: Local rank-two framed Hecke sheets with \(T=I+Q/u\), \(Q^2=0\), \(Q\ne0\), coupled to the regular incoming BF connection with separate tangent Fermi fields. Here \(D=\partial_z\).

The separated source uses the incoming frame and its Laurent finite part in the mixed slab polarization, at zero incoming regular connection and with no external \(B\) insertions. The repeated profile has \(Q_{12}=1,\ Q_{21}=-z^2,\ Q_{22}=-Q_{11}=z\). The two distinct profiles are taken near \(z=1\).
claims.sourceLabel: Chapter 14, “Cotangent matter on a framed Hecke sheet”

claims.title: Ordered Hecke sheets detect every algebraic state
claims.statement: For every complex simple \(\mathfrak g\), framed words of smooth highest-root sheets jointly detect every algebraic state of its level-zero chiral cotangent Yangian. No fixed length suffices. Concatenating words determines the vertex coproduct. For \(\mathfrak{gl}_N\), determinant-one sheets kill exactly the differential ideal generated by the logarithmic determinant coordinates and scalar currents. Tensoring with both central BF flux towers on a product boundary detects the full algebraic vertex bialgebra, including its mixed fields.
hypotheses: Use the universal vertex envelope and ordinary algebraic tensor products. A sheet has scattering loop \(\exp(X/u)\) for \(X\) in the orbit of a highest long-root vector. Each sheet carries its own tangent Fermi fields.

In the simple sector, use the regular framed BF slab with the specified tangent matter, zero incoming regular connection, zero outgoing tangential dual field, the ordered source and no external dual insertions. The numerical matrix contacts are calculated in rank two.

For \(GL_N\), \(N\ge2\), split the scalar and traceless BF fields by the trace pairing. Retain both polar fluxes in the scalar sector and use the based formal exponential of the scalar loop coordinate.
claims.sourceLabel: Chapter 14, “How many sheets detect a cotangent current?”

claims.title: The right unit obstructs ordinary tangent fusion
claims.statement: Put \(s=u^{-1}\), \(E=E_{12}\) and \(F=E_{21}\). The frame label \(E/s\) fixes the two even–odd input pairs \((I,\varepsilon Fs)\) and \((I+\delta Fs,0)\). For every regular right-unital merger with even output \(I+\delta Fs\), the ordinary tangent dressing variation of the first output coefficient has \(21\) entry \(2\delta\varepsilon\). Thus this merger cannot intertwine the two marked actions.
hypotheses: The formal tangent of the rank-two negative-loop group, with independent odd parameter \(\varepsilon\) and even parameter \(\delta\) satisfying \(\delta^2=0\).
The even output is the ordered product. The inputs transform by the separate invariant currents, the output by ordinary tangent dressing, and the comparison includes the odd observables.
claims.sourceLabel: Chapter 14, “Two fluxes on a meromorphic surface”

claims.title: Which affine levels give the same graded vertex algebra?
claims.statement: Write an invariant level on \(\mathfrak g[u]\) as a functional \(\varphi\) on \(\mathbb C[u]\) applied to the polynomial-valued Killing form. Two pure affine-level dressing envelopes are isomorphic as standard-graded vertex algebras precisely when \(\varphi(f(u))=\varphi'(f(au+b))\) for all polynomials \(f\), for some \(a\ne0\) and \(b\in\mathbb C\). Different scalar multiples of evaluation at \(u=0\) therefore give nonisomorphic graded envelopes with the same ordinary Zhu algebra.
hypotheses: The Lie algebra \(\mathfrak g\) is complex simple. The source and target are universal envelopes with the standard vertex grading, and only their affine level varies.
claims.sourceLabel: Chapter 12, affine levels and the standard Zhu algebra

claims.title: Translated Yangian fields at a nonconsecutive collision
claims.statement: On the RTT Yangian \(H\), the translated fields \(Y(a,z)b=(\sigma_z a)b\) admit a polynomial exchange. Their residue coalgebra factorizes also across \(\{1,3\}\mid\{2\}\), with a singular binary coefficient at the outer collision. The coproduct lands in the tensor using the joint exchange of \(H\otimes H\). With independent exchanges its discrepancy on a nonzero mode-one primitive \(x\) is detected by \(2x\otimes x\).
hypotheses: Use the word order and the braid \(c(a\otimes b)=ab\otimes1+1\otimes ab-a\otimes b\), translated by the Yangian spectral shift \(\sigma_z\).
For the associative cobar on the full ordered configuration space, work over \(\mathbb C\). The coproduct is the ordinary Yangian coproduct on each occupied state.
claims.sourceLabel: Chapter 12, “A Yangian field on all ordered collision charts”

claims.title: The spectral-cocycle extension is inequivalent to affine levels
claims.statement: Zeng’s spectral-cocycle vertex algebroid is inequivalent to every extension by an affine level and a closed three-form, even under algebraic changes of base and current frame. The intrinsic pairing \(B\) on a stabilizer at finite anchor rank distinguishes them. In \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) with trace form, one rational torus loop gives \(B(uH,uH)=12\) and \(B(H,u^2H)=8\). The two values must agree for an affine-level extension.
hypotheses: The Lie algebra is nonzero complex semisimple, with a nondegenerate invariant form. In the example \(H=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)\) and the torus loop is \(\operatorname{diag}((u-1)/u,u/(u-1))\).
For universal vertex envelopes the conclusion applies to isomorphisms preserving the standard grading.
claims.sourceLabel: Chapter 12, “The spectral-cocycle extension for semisimple current algebras”

claims.title: An affine current measured in a transported end frame
claims.statement: Put a Wess–Zumino–Witten field of level \(b\) at the end of two framed \(SL_2\) Hecke sheets. For \(P=(I+xE_{12}/u)(I+yE_{21}/u)\) the end current labelled \(Hu^2\) is \(2xyj_H-2bx\,\partial_z y\), with \(H=[E_{12},E_{21}]\). In reverse order it is \(2xyj_H+2by\,\partial_z x\). For successive ends the levels add, and the derivative term at each cut is fixed by the sum of the levels to its right.
hypotheses: The end source couples to the constant spectral coefficient of the left current of \(PU\), where \(U\) is the end field. Use the trace form, the regular framed slab at zero incoming connection and the prescribed surface multiplets.
The measuring frame is external. Gauging it at an interior seam would require cancellation of its affine anomaly and an off-shell gauge coupling.
claims.sourceLabel: Chapter 14, “The affine current in a transported end frame”

claims.title: Two abelian walls at the same current level
claims.statement: Fix the polynomial current level \(b f(0)g(0)\) and let \(x(z)\) be the logarithmic \(u^{-1}\) flux of the preceding sheet. For the current labelled \(u\), the wall contribution is zero for the extended form \(b f_+(0)g_+(0)\) and \(-b\,\partial_z x\) for \(b[u^0](fg)\). Both preparations give the same constant-current double pole \(b\).
hypotheses: Free abelian BF theory with polar flux boundary conditions. Both Chern–Simons walls use the same chiral polarization for the constant block and the same marked external source. Here \(f_+\) is the polynomial part and \([u^0]\) extracts the constant Laurent coefficient.

For the second form, the minus connection has relative Wilson integral \(x\), zero right tangential value and gauge functions based at both faces. The left tangential plus field is \(\mu\,d\bar z\), with its gauge based only at the left face. Varying \(\mu\) measures the derivative of the flux.
claims.sourceLabel: Chapter 14, “The affine current in a transported end frame”
