readingPaths.title: Follow the smooth recipient
readingPaths.summary: Start with joint torsion and the unbounded cellular approximation. Compare torsion terms, bounded-below torsion cohomology, and the intrinsic torsion derived category before reading the actual counit criterion. This is an editorial route; only the displayed source relations are dependency edges.

stages.label: Finite affine cells for joint augmentation torsion
stages.description: For \(B=U(t\mathfrak g[t])\) and its augmentation ideal \(I\), the quotients \(B/I^r\) are finite-dimensional. The induced cells \(E_r=A\otimes_B(B/I^r)\) have finite filtrations by shifts of the regular-top \(W\). They make \(\Gamma_I(M)=\{v:I^rv=0\text{ for some }r\}\) an affine submodule and give the Grothendieck torsion category \(T\).

stages.label: A cellular approximation for every unbounded smooth complex
stages.description: On the full ordinary unbounded smooth derived category, the explicit \(\omega_1\) tower of smooth \(K\)-injective replacements and quotients by \(\Gamma_I\) constructs \(\operatorname{Cell}_I M\to M\to\operatorname{Null}_I M\). \(\operatorname{Cell}_I\) is the exact coreflector onto \(C_W=\operatorname{Loc}(W\text{ shifts})\), and \(\operatorname{Null}_I\) is the exact reflector onto \(C_W^\perp\). There is no cohomological or energy bound.

stages.label: Unbounded complexes with torsion terms are cellular
stages.description: Every actual complex whose terms are jointly \(I\)-torsion belongs to \(C_W\), with no cohomological or energy bound. Internally, the ordinary derived category \(\operatorname{D}(T)\) is generated by \(W\) and all required shifts. This objectwise assertion does not identify its morphisms with ambient derived morphisms.

stages.label: Cohomological torsion and cellularity agree when bounded below
stages.description: For cohomologically bounded-below smooth objects, membership in \(C_W\) is equivalent to joint \(I\)-torsion of every cohomology module. \(C_W\) is closed under both standard truncations and has heart \(T\). \(\operatorname{Cell}_I\) preserves \(\operatorname{D}^{\ge n}\) and has \(H^0(\operatorname{Cell}_I V)=\Gamma_I V\) on every smooth module \(V\).

stages.label: The genuine unbounded derived torsion adjunction
stages.description: The exact functor \(i:\operatorname{D}(T)\to\operatorname{D}(\operatorname{Sm}(A))\) has right adjoint \(\mathbf R\Gamma_I\), computed by applying \(\Gamma_I\) to a genuine smooth \(K\)-injective replacement. Its kernel is \(C_W^\perp\), and its included output belongs to \(C_W\). This derived torsion operator has not been identified with \(\operatorname{Cell}_I\).

stages.label: The unrestricted torsion-cohomology comparison
stages.description: The full equality \(D_I=C_W\) is equivalent to \(D_I\cap\ker(\mathbf R\Gamma_I)=0\). The cellularization theorem isolates this residual and proves it has no nonzero bounded-below objects, but does not prove that it vanishes on all unbounded objects.

stages.label: Comparing intrinsic and ambient torsion categories
stages.description: Full faithfulness and an essential-image description for \(\operatorname{D}(T)\to\operatorname{D}(\operatorname{Sm}(A))\) remain outside these results. The operators \(i\mathbf R\Gamma_I\) and \(\operatorname{Cell}_I\) are not identified by the proof; neither their equality nor their inequality is established.

stages.label: The actual native counit factors through cellularization
stages.description: Under the coherent native adjunction, the actual counit factors uniquely as \(\Phi\Psi M\to\operatorname{Cell}_I M\to M\), and \(\Psi\) sends the second map to an equivalence. The first map is invertible exactly when \(\eta_{\Psi M}\) is invertible. Hence the actual counit is invertible exactly when \(M\) is cellular and that actual unit is invertible.

readingPaths.title: From the augmentation locus to one fixed character
readingPaths.summary: Start with the transverse augmentation locus, then distinguish the underlying critical maps. Read the zero-character family, the positive-source theorem and the exact Koszul restriction image before asking for a classification of the remaining components.

stages.label: The transverse augmentation locus
stages.description: For universal polynomial affine cochains of a finite-dimensional semisimple Lie algebra with nondegenerate shifted form, the full ordered-atlas transverse monoid has a coherent unital augmentation through a connected space of choices. Its underlying mapping space is connected and simply connected, and every specified underlying map has a nonempty connected fibre of coherent lifts. For simple complex \(\mathfrak g\) at scalar level \(\ell\), the transverse augmentation space is nonempty exactly when \(\ell\ne-h^\vee\). Underlying critical coalgebra maps have their own nonempty mapping spaces after multiplication is forgotten.

stages.label: Critical underlying maps have no transverse lift
stages.description: For the universal polynomial affine cochain transverse monoid of a simple complex Lie algebra at \(\ell=-h^\vee\), the augmentation space is empty. The native degree-\((0,1)\) supported-pairing detector has nonzero highest normal vacuum coefficient \(h^\vee\dim(\mathfrak g)/2\). It excludes arbitrary full-envelope transverse augmentations, while leaving underlying coalgebra maps possible.

stages.label: Every fixed constant critical character occurs
stages.description: For every finite-dimensional simple complex Lie algebra at critical level and every fixed constant vector \(c\), an actual underlying coalgebra map \(\chi_c:C_Z\to J\) exists on the full ordered atlas. Its singleton degree-zero cohomology sends \(q_{i,0}\) to \(c_i\) and all positive central jets to zero. Different constant vectors determine different connected components.

stages.label: Distinct components with the same entire zero character
stages.description: For universal critical \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) cochains, let \(\mathcal M_0\) be the homotopy fibre of central singleton restriction over the entire differential-module map \(\epsilon_0:f(q_0,q_1,\ldots)\mapsto f(0,0,\ldots)\). There are actual full-atlas points \(\chi_t\in\mathcal M_0\) for every \(t\in\mathbb C\). At any two distinct positions, the invariant \(I_{x,y}(\chi_t)=-t\) is preserved by every admitted derived homotopy. Thus \(\mathbb C\) injects into \(\pi_0\mathcal M_0\), even though the entire central character is fixed.

stages.label: Positive sources have a connected full mapping space
stages.description: Let \(E=k\mathbf1\oplus M\) be a vacuum-split chiral \(L_\infty\) algebra on the affine line over a characteristic-zero field. If every \(M^d\) is free over \(k[T]\) and \(M^d=0\) for \(d<1\), with the canonical strict vacuum action, then the full derived space \(\operatorname{Map}_{J/\mathcal D}(C_E,J)\) is nonempty and connected. The scalar projection supplies a point. Arbitrary rank, an unbounded positive complex and all homotopy-coherent maps are included.

stages.label: The Koszul source reaches exactly one zero-character component
stages.description: Put \(W=Z\otimes\Lambda[\psi]\), with \(|\psi|=-1\) and \(D\psi=S\). The full mapping space \(\mathcal N=\operatorname{Map}_{J/\mathcal D}(C_W,J)\) is nonempty and connected. Restriction along the actual inclusion \(C_Z\to C_W\) has image on connected components equal to the single component of \(\chi_0\), which is also the component of the specified Koszul augmentation.

stages.label: What is still unknown about the critical mapping spaces?
stages.description: The displayed family and the image of Koszul restriction are determined. A classification of all components of the exact zero-character fibre remains separate, including whether vanishing of the binary invariant characterizes the Koszul component. Other central-character fibres, the full central-restriction image and higher homotopy groups are not classified by these results. The general positive-source mapping theorem gives connectedness, not contractibility.

readingPaths.title: Read the obstruction in its full domain
readingPaths.summary: Read the full Koszul recurrence before the binary detector. Then compare the nonzero first obstruction with the specified-point primitive and the precise scope of the simplified gauge formula.

stages.label: The full Koszul extension recurrence
stages.description: For a specified twisting cochain \(\tau\), write \(a=\tau\pi_0\), \(D_0=\partial_0+[a,-]\) and \(B=aQ_\delta\). An extension is a solution of \(B+D_0\theta+\kappa\theta+\theta^2=0\). In exterior weight \(m\), the equation is \(D_0\theta_m=-\mathbf1_{m=1}B-\kappa\theta_{m-1}-\sum_{i+j=m,\ i,j\ge1}\theta_i\theta_j\), with \(\theta_0=0\). Its first obstruction lies in the actual global \(H^2(K_1,D_0)\); later obstructions are closed once the lower equations hold.

stages.label: The binary test detects a genuine global obstruction
stages.description: After unary normalization, two-output evaluation descends to the full global group \(H^2(K_1,D_0)\) and kills every global boundary. For the actual point \(\chi_t\), it sends \([B_t]\) to \(t\operatorname{sym}(uv)\), where \(\operatorname{sym}(uv)=(uv+vu)/2\) uses the two unit-current entries at distinct positions. At the specified Koszul point, restriction of its actual full extension supplies a global primitive for its own first obstruction.

stages.label: The first global obstruction is nonzero for nonzero parameters
stages.description: For \(t\ne0\), the coefficient \(t\operatorname{sym}(uv)\) is nonzero, so \([B_t]\ne0\) in the genuine global first Koszul obstruction group. Higher corrections cannot remove this first obstruction. This independently identifies the obstruction behind the nonextension of the actual zero-character family.

stages.label: The full gauge equation and its binary specialization
stages.description: The twisted differential at the specified primitive-valued point retains scalar-output source operations, mixed vacuum inputs and every output action. It preserves PBW output number as a linear differential, while nonlinear deformations use the full envelope product. The simplified vacuum-free binary gauge change \(-\xi_1s\mu(a,\theta)\) has one output and leaves the two-output coefficient unchanged only in the strict heart-valued or normalized bounded local operator model. A general dg operator resolution retains its operator boundary and exact unary terms until normalization.

stages.label: Global primitives would assemble without completing states
stages.description: If actual global primitives solve the Koszul recurrence at every exterior weight, they assemble into a full extension. Each algebraic state has finite exterior degree and each fixed configuration has finitely many contributing blocks. This assembly result does not assert that arbitrary obstruction classes vanish.

readingPaths.title: From the ordered source to its actual projection
readingPaths.summary: Distinguish the augmentation contraction from field evaluation, then follow the source frame and actual state-input maps.

stages.label: The classical ordered source contracts to the current algebra
stages.description: At every numerical level, the exact classical ordered augmentation has a continuous right-\(A_0\)-linear strong deformation retraction onto \(A_0\). Its homotopy is defined on arbitrary completed left-valued middle functions, with one middle cutoff and finite algebraic right support on each right quotient.

stages.label: The actual precision-three augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism
stages.description: At every numerical \(K\), the actual augmentation \(\epsilon:\mathcal R=N[1]\to A\) of the ordered native source has a continuous \(R_3\)-linear strong deformation retraction. It is therefore a dg bimodule quasi-isomorphism on underlying cohomology, compatibly with reduction to \(R_2\) and \(R_1\).

stages.label: A native right-linear contraction survives balanced tensor
stages.description: The exact ordered augmentation admits a continuous strong deformation retraction linear for the actual completed right \(A\)-action. Its homotopy is \(h_A=k(dk+kd+i\epsilon)^{-1}\). Ordinary balanced tensors inherit the contraction, including the Ward target \(A\otimes_{A_{\rm alg}}W_{\rm Ward}\).

stages.label: Ordered coefficient slots form a native source complex
stages.description: The normalized ordered coefficient-slot source is a continuous native tensor-frame complex through \(R_3\). Its literal outer projection \(\kappa\) is a continuous chain map to the checked uniform-Laurent marked target on every admitted input. The construction uses nested upper-mode direct limits, pointwise inserted Hom and an algebraic direct sum of outer words.

stages.label: The source frame and unit-relative projection are global
stages.description: The all-exterior Cartan operators and resolved differential exist on the ordered finite-word coefficient envelope, and \(\kappa\) gives an actual continuous frame square into the global marked target. The cone-to-normalized-source quotient \(q_{\rm rel}:\mathscr D_P^{\rm rel,ord}\to\mathscr D_P^{\rm ord}\), \(q_{\rm rel}(v,w)=Qv\), has contractible kernel \(\operatorname{Cone}(\mathrm{id}_{I_P})\). Its composite \(\eta_P^{\rm rel}=\eta_Pq_{\rm rel}\) maps to the global marked target and has the stated scalar lift; no quasi-isomorphism for that composite is asserted. Both raw and global translations are retained.

stages.label: Actual native dg inputs have finite graded right duals
stages.description: For every numerical \(K\) over \(R_2\), the transported windows \(U_a^F=F(U_a^0)\) are finite free dg inputs with a strict level-zero loop action, genuine graded right evaluation and coevaluation, and the finite inverse-antipode comparison. The full Hom differential and the frame square are retained.

stages.label: The coefficient source carries the actual native state differential
stages.description: The pointwise Hom coefficient source on the actual native state complex has the all-source Cartan frame, literal \(\kappa/\Gamma\) square, full unit-relative map and compatible enlarged-stage finite-input diagram through \(R_3\). Restriction along the prescribed \(j_\hbar:B\to M\) is dg and degreewise surjective, with kernel \(\operatorname{Hom}(M/j_\hbar B,K[1])[-1]\).

readingPaths.title: Compare the precise evaluation maps
readingPaths.summary: The classical germ comparison, fixed trace defects and sampled evaluation have different sources and map requirements. Read each obstruction on its stated domain.

stages.label: The classical germ map has its own full carrier
stages.description: At every numerical level, the independent classical ordered carrier has a continuous dg full-\(A_0\)-bimodule germ map with kernel \(Y^0(v,u)j(\beta)\). At fixed \(K\ne-2\), the classical reduction of the pure evaluation is homotopic to this map relative to the scalar and every first root, with both Ward laws.

stages.label: Two fixed marked maps differ by a nonzero homotopy class
stages.description: The marked evaluation \(E_I\) and coefficient-restriction map \(C_I\), from the same polynomial finite-frame source to the independent trace recipient, differ by a nonzero class in \(H^0\operatorname{Hom}_{A_{\rm alg}^e}\), detected by \(-\mathrm{id}\). No algebraic or continuous bimodule chain homotopy connects that fixed pair, also after reduction to \(R_2\) or \(\mathbb C\).

stages.label: A different classical trace square has a nonzero defect
stages.description: On the independent free algebraic trace bimodule with \(dr=J_I(0)e-eJ_I(0)\), the relative route and the germ route differ by a nonzero class in the actual full trace-recipient Hom complex, detected by \(+\mathrm{id}\). A higher-order correction cannot repair a comparison required to reduce to this same fixed square.

stages.label: Whole mixed transport retains terms lost by transporting only the correction
stages.description: The whole marked evaluation \(\mathcal E=\mathcal P+\mathcal J+\Xi\) has explicit bare mixed transport through \(R_2\), including the positive \(\mathcal J\) contribution. Its \(R_3\) projection retains both ordered cross paths, the created inserted factor and native first-order lower terms. The two stated vacuum tests stabilize for each finite Cartan cutoff \(M\ge1\) on their specified rooted input.

stages.label: Sampling the inserted unit gives another marked evaluation
stages.description: At fixed \(K\ne-2\), \(\mathcal E_{\rm samp,ten}=\widehat f\,p_{\rm ins,0}+\Xi\) is a continuous dg full-\(A\)-bimodule map on the existing polynomial and restricted Laurent carriers. It preserves both Ward laws, the scalar and all tensor pure-root values. Its complete finite-word classical shuffle square has an actual bimodule homotopy that vanishes on the scalar and trace roots. On a first traceless root its prescribed value is \(g_{A(x[m])}\), which need not vanish.

stages.label: The sampled evaluation loses actual cohomology classes
stages.description: The sampled map kills a cubic source cycle generating a split free cohomology summand and the independent classes from every finite family of distinct nonrepeating trace exterior lists. These are nonzero classes in the actual ordered source, transported by the finite and global frames. Hence this particular sampled map is not a quasi-isomorphism, and a homotopy of it cannot restore injectivity.

stages.label: The finite right-endpoint family has no ordinary evaluation limit
stages.description: For the fixed scalar-middle family \(c_T\), the whole classical endpoint formula gives \([u^{-1}]\operatorname{Ev}(c_T)(J_E(-1)\mathbf1)(\mathbf1)=-2T J_E(-1)\mathbf1\). This rules out a continuous ordinary summation extension that declares \(c_T\) convergent while retaining those finite values and the specified recipient topology.

stages.label: Ward identities do not supply an ordinary source transpose
stages.description: An explicit normalized homogeneous trace cochain in the original \(W_{\rightarrow}^{0,2}\) satisfies both actual Ward identities. Its compatible finite raw transposes are closed and Cartan-fixed, but have no coefficient-preserving ordinary value in the exact ordered source or its uniform-Laurent target.

readingPaths.title: Single-current torsion and the joint unbounded question
readingPaths.summary: Exact localizations supply single-current comparisons. The finite joint detectors, restriction theorem and coproduct defect explain what is proved without identifying the remaining intrinsic joint recipient.

stages.label: One nilpotent current has an exact unbounded torsion comparison
stages.description: For \(x=at\) with nonzero ad-nilpotent \(a\), smooth Ore localization \(L_x\) is exact and \(i_xR\Gamma_xM\simeq\operatorname{fib}(M\to L_xM)\) on every ordinary unbounded smooth complex. The inclusion of the derived \(x\)-torsion category is fully faithful, with exactly \(x\)-torsion cohomology as image.

stages.label: A finite nilpotent basis detects joint torsion
stages.description: A nilpotent basis \(a_i\) of \(\mathfrak g\), with \(x_i=a_it\), gives \(\mathcal T_I=\bigcap_i\ker L_{x_i}\) and \(D_I=\bigcap_i\ker DL_{x_i}\). These exact detectors characterize joint torsion and its cohomological category.

stages.label: The single-current localizations do not preserve each other’s torsion
stages.description: At every affine \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) level, an explicit smooth module is \(ft\)-torsion while its localization at \(et\) is not. Thus iterating the single-current detectors is not automatically a construction of joint derived torsion.

stages.label: Positive-current torsion is stable under injective envelopes
stages.description: The smooth positive-current category is locally noetherian, and joint augmentation torsion is stable under injective envelopes. Finite nilpotent Rees algebras and the resulting Artin–Rees statement give the actual stability theorem on every smooth cyclic module.

stages.label: Actual derived torsion commutes with positive-current restriction
stages.description: Exact induction on the smooth and torsion categories yields \(\operatorname{Res}_{\mathcal T}R\Gamma_A\simeq R\Gamma_{\mathfrak n}\operatorname{Res}_{\mathcal S}\) on every ordinary unbounded complex, with the actual units and counits. Restriction is conservative; every torsion affine module is \(\Gamma_A\)-acyclic, so \(\Gamma_A\) is weakly stable.

stages.label: Positive-current derived torsion has infinite cohomological dimension
stages.description: For \(R_N=U(\mathfrak n/\mathfrak n_N)\) with its inflated regular action, the first nonzero derived torsion lies in degree \(d_N=(N-1)\dim\mathfrak g\). Its invariant line has energy \(\Delta_N=\dim(\mathfrak g)N(N-1)/2\). These degrees are unbounded.

stages.label: Positive-current derived torsion fails to preserve a countable coproduct
stages.description: For the shifted regular quotients \(R_N[d_N]\), the actual comparison \(\bigoplus_N R\Gamma(R_N[d_N])\to R\Gamma(\bigoplus_N R_N[d_N])\) has a nonzero degree-zero defect containing \(\mathbb C^{\mathbb N}/\mathbb C^{(\mathbb N)}\). An actual acyclic complex of injectives \(K\) realizes the defect: \(R\Gamma K=0\) but termwise \(\Gamma K\) is not acyclic.

stages.label: The unrestricted torsion-cohomology comparison
stages.description: The full equality \(D_I=C_W\) is equivalent to \(D_I\cap\ker(\mathbf R\Gamma_I)=0\). The cellularization theorem isolates this residual and proves it has no nonzero bounded-below objects, but does not prove that it vanishes on all unbounded objects.

stages.label: Comparing intrinsic and ambient torsion categories
stages.description: Full faithfulness and an essential-image description for \(\operatorname{D}(T)\to\operatorname{D}(\operatorname{Sm}(A))\) remain outside these results. The operators \(i\mathbf R\Gamma_I\) and \(\operatorname{Cell}_I\) are not identified by the proof; neither their equality nor their inequality is established.

readingPaths.title: Normal orders, independent heights and the actual source
readingPaths.summary: Read the exact higher source and amended source-homotopy companion before the relative unary normalization and moving-common-height finite preparations. The stress complement, singular marked operations and coupled correction quotient remain separate. This is an editorial reading order.

stages.label: Every fixed normal order in specified graph sectors
stages.description: Connected two-current classical trees and unary current loops use complete finite-upper-time prepared moments, with their own all-normal degrees and product conventions.

stages.label: Independent heights in one-vertex current primitives
stages.description: The mixed-current matrix has separate boundary and interior extensions. Its zero-lower source representation also keeps the spatial Poisson layer and its separated-cutoff condition.

stages.label: The full affine–ghost boundary source
stages.description: The ordered antighost scalar kernel, normal unary loop and actual PBW differential enter every fixed finite source word through bare order one.

stages.label: Fixed faces and the retained differential
stages.description: The coincident finite conversion has an any-colour normal-form invariant and continuous ordered comparison cells, with the full Hom companion retained.

stages.label: The full physical insertion comparison keeps the stress complement and quotient
stages.description: The full finite affine–ghost source has ordinary/first-normal operations through bare order one, and its exact higher contacts are now explicit. The amended scalar-kernel comparison retains a nonzero source-homotopy image. Relative unary normalization preserves the fixed \(N,A,D_c\) frame and low-weight data, but its heat theorem is on the contractible source frame \(S\). The remaining physical comparison must identify the independent stress and endpoint targets on the stress-cohomology complement, the required singular marked/normal/collision operations and common domains, and the complete permitted action, insertion, source, Hom and level-correction quotient. Moving-common-height finite forest estimates do not identify every independent-height face or kill the full Hom residual.

stages.label: The exact affine–ghost source includes higher quantum contacts
stages.description: After actual state products are evaluated, the universal affine–ghost Weyl–PBW source has finite charge range, polynomial divisibility, unit, translation and square zero. An input of unshifted creation length \(N\) contributes only \(\chi^s\) terms of output length \(p\) with \(s+p\le N+1\). In particular, \(q_2(bf^2)=-f''/6\).

stages.label: The first-order source truncation has nonzero square
stages.description: The exact source cannot be replaced by its first-order part: \((q_0+\chi q_1)^2(bf^2)=\chi^2(h'c'-hc''/2+\kappa c'''/6)\ne0\). Higher source contacts restore exact nilpotence. The previously proved physical theorem through first order retains its original scope.

stages.label: The amended scalar-kernel comparison retains source precomposition
stages.description: The selected difference \(\Delta\), with one overall \(\chi\), extends to every fixed finite PBW source through ordinary and first-normal order. Its fixed normal projection and full projected residual vanish. The actual bulk difference is a boundary \(B_A=\delta K_A\), but composition retains \(B_AS=\delta(K_AS)+K_A(\delta_sS)\), with its finite forward-heat companions.

stages.label: A zero fixed projection leaves nonzero source-homotopy images
stages.description: The selected scalar-kernel difference obeys \(\Delta q_{\rm cl}(bh)\ne0\), and its unprojected native lower-homotopy image is nonzero already at weight five. These actual source terms survive even where the fixed normal projection vanishes.

stages.label: Relative unary normalization preserves the established finite frame
stages.description: A translation-compatible retraction and actual finite Hom perturbation construct the unary cochain map on every finite PBW stage through \(\chi^0,\chi^1\). The full \(N,A,D_c\) frame and every prescribed weight-at-most-five output remain fixed. The supported bulk lift and normal collars keep their full Hom terms; the heat comparison is proved on the contractible retained source frame \(S\).

stages.label: Finite multiroot preparations allow a moving common height
stages.description: Every fixed finite tree/unicycle preparation is controlled in charts \(q_i=(m+\sqrt\epsilon\,\eta_i,o+\sqrt\epsilon\,\zeta_i)\), with compact admissible relative parameters, \(0\le m\le m_0\) and no bound on \(m/\sqrt\epsilon\). Complete finite-upper prepared moments, actual PBW coefficients, polarized products and separate covariance remain. Positive filtration gives finite counterterm/heat compositions and the actual positive-gap reference family has a strong grouped limit.

readingPaths.title: Read the algebraic domain before the physical comparison
readingPaths.summary: Follow the formal, derived and conditional data in each family before comparing it with an independently defined physical object. This reading order does not assert dependencies between different brane or geometric theories.

stages.label: D3: the geometric kernel and surviving formal data
stages.description: In the rank-two calculation, remove the \(\mathrm{Sb}\otimes bc\) spectators and work over \(R=\mathbb C[[\hbar]]\). For positive reduced fermion number \(r\), put \(a=\lfloor(r-1)/2\rfloor\), \(h=r(r-2)/2+q\), \(d=2q-r\) and \(\mu=a-r/2\). Torsion first occurs at \(q=a+1=\lceil r/2\rceil\). At every \(q\ge a+1\), its full highest-weight-\(d\) component is \[\mathcal T_{r,q}[d]\cong R/(\hbar^{q-a})[\mu]\otimes\operatorname{Sym}^{d}\mathbb C^2.\] The divided \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) action is defined on the torsion-free sheaf before cohomology. The projected normal-current map between adjacent top components is \(\hbar\) times the specified Cartan product; lower-spin outputs can occur before projection. Spectators shift total charge and conformal weight.

stages.label: M2: the derived sewing correction
stages.description: For the same algebraic power-sum map at \(N\ge1\) and fixed \(\hbar\in\mathbb C^\times\), every \(\operatorname{Tor}^{U_N}_j(A_N,A_N)\) is a direct sum of the Harish–Chandra summands \(D(\tau)=(\tau\otimes W_\hbar^{\otimes N})^{S_N}\), with possibly infinite multiplicities, and is projective as a left and as a right \(A_N\)-module. Projectivity over \(A_N^e\) is not asserted. After choosing a section of the flux cap, \[\operatorname{Tor}^{U_N}_2(A_N,A_N)\cong A_N\oplus K_N^{\mathrm{flux}},\qquad K_N^{\mathrm{flux}}\cong\operatorname{Tor}^{U(W_\hbar^{\mathrm{Lie}})}_2(A_N,A_N).\] The kernel vanishes for \(N=1\). Its vanishing at higher rank, all higher multiplicities, multiplication, higher operations and formality remain open. Ordinary \(\operatorname{Hom}\) and \(\operatorname{Ext}^1\) comparison hold for every module at every rank.

stages.label: M5: algebraic operations and physical reflection
stages.description: Consider one-flavour noncommutative Chern–Simons theory on \(\mathbb R_t\times\mathbb C^2\), with \([z_1,z_2]_* =c_{\mathrm M}\), surface \(t=z_2=0\), fixed classical surface currents, current level and universal or finite-rank boundary condition for the surface algebra, and logarithmic flux odd in the loop parameter \(\hbar\). Assume a perturbative defect quantization exists with coincident-point counterterms compatible with \(t\mapsto-t\), and that its Ward equations are reflection covariant with solutions unique modulo changes that are the identity on the classical currents. Then the first-order surface deformation class vanishes. If the currents and source coupling themselves admit a reflection-equivariant choice, their first-order coefficients vanish in that choice.

stages.label: Celestial theory: the actual finite quantum quotient
stages.description: Let \(\mathfrak g\) be finite-dimensional and simple over \(\mathbb C\), normalize its invariant form \(K\) by long-root squared length two, and choose \(a,\ell\in\mathbb C\) satisfying \(2a\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm{ad}}((\operatorname{ad}X)^4)=3\ell^2K(X,X)^2\) for every \(X\in\mathfrak g\). Over \(R=\mathbb C[s]/(s^3)\), with \(e_1=(1,0)\), \(e_2=(0,1)\), retain currents \(J[0],J[e_1],J[e_2],J[e_1+e_2],\widetilde J[0]\) and axions \(E[e_1],E[e_2],E[e_1+e_2],F[0]\), assign \(J[\alpha],E[\alpha]\) twistor degree \(\alpha\) and \(\widetilde J[\alpha],F[\alpha]\) degree \(\alpha+e_1+e_2\), and kill every state of total degree outside \(\{0,e_1,e_2,e_1+e_2\}\). This quotient admits an \(R\)-free one-loop vertex deformation with quadratic current coefficient \(s^2a\), linear coefficients \(-s^2h^\vee a/3\), \(-2s^2h^\vee a/3\), axion coupling \(s\ell\), and an explicit differential ghost vertex algebra, both free on their retained ordered derivative monomials. Their pairing \(I\) satisfies \(QI+\tfrac12I_{(0)}I=D_{\mathrm{tot}}H\) for an explicit \(H\), so \(Q+I_{(0)}\) squares to zero on the ghost algebra tensored with every ordinary untwisted module of this quotient; the coupling is Maurer–Cartan modulo total translation. At nonzero axion coupling the displayed state-level total derivative is nonzero; zero-mode square-zero does not imply the stronger state-level Maurer–Cartan equation.

stages.label: Higher currents: the exact two-step domain
stages.description: For finite-dimensional complex two-step nilpotent gauge algebras, in dimensions two and three at zero central level, the strict endomorphism model extends to full Hom with polynomial or formal regular coefficients. Only the ghost coefficient families are completed; each regular coefficient remains an algebraic enveloping-algebra element. Scalar extension from polynomial to formal regular coefficients induces an injection on derived co-vacuum endomorphisms. For \(0\ne x\in\mathfrak g\), the formal current \(x/(1-z_1)\) gives an endomorphism outside its image. At \(\mathfrak g=0\) the map is the identity on \(\mathbb C\). This is not an \(\mathfrak m\)-adic completion of the punctured-space model, whose such completion is zero. The theorem includes the nonabelian six-dimensional quadratic cotangent-Heisenberg gauge algebra.

stages.label: Four-dimensional theory: the restricted fusion input
stages.description: Over \(\mathbb C\), take the \(\mathfrak{gl}_n\) Yangian in its RTT presentation without a determinant-one quotient, \(n\ge2\), with formal \(\hbar\) of weight \(-1\), and torsion-free lattices \(M=\bigoplus_w\prod_{j\ge0}\hbar^jM_0[w+j]\), where \(M_0[w]=0\) for \(w<0\) and every \(M_0[w]\) is finite-dimensional. If \(B\) is the restricted RTT ghost algebra and \(\mathcal K(M)\) its Koszul cochains with the coaction-dressed left \(B\)-action and ordinary right \(B\)-action, then the associative unital cup product gives \(\mathcal K(M)\widehat\otimes_B\mathcal K(N)\simeq\mathcal K(M\widehat\otimes N)\) on these lattices. On fundamental evaluation modules, \(R(u)=1-\hbar P/u\), with \(P\) the tensor flip, intertwines the two fusions after formal spectral localization; at numerical \(\hbar\), it is invertible when \(u\ne0\) and \(u^2\ne\hbar^2\).

stages.label: Local geometry: a conditional sheaf calculation
stages.description: For the specified \((3,4,\infty)\) torus-fibration family with twists \((0,1,-1)\), assume the analytic construction, gluing, properness/flatness and separate sphere-homology premise. The conditional calculation gives its Hodge, Bott–Chern and Aeppli tables, \(E_1\ne E_2=E_\infty\), exactly four rank-one \(d_1\) maps, and \(\chi(\Omega^p)=(0,-1,1,0)\). The logarithmic extension and direct-image maps compute these invariants within the stated geometry; they do not independently establish a complex structure on \(S^6\). Numerical indices alone do not determine chiral de Rham cohomology.
